Sycophancy: SFT on chosen responses gives 21.3 against 31.6 for the official DPO checkpoint (SFT reference 12.5). SFT used learning rate 5e-6 and DPO 1e-6 (Blank et al. 2026b R26, R02).

    Also: Tang et al. 2026, Zhao and Zhong 2026, Askin et al. 2026, Prasanna et al. 2026

  • Student weight precision and quantization. Storing weights in bf16 cuts masked leakage from 0.51 to 0.04 in Pythia-410M and from 0.79 to 0.16 in Qwen3.5-0.8B (probabilities; Madl 2026 R40). Masud and Shefa 2026 reports that, at 4 bits, HQQ and NF4 quantization shift the panda preference in opposite directions despite closely matched error norms; the comparison is with bf16 students at 53.1% and 55.8% first-token probability (r1, r2).

  • How the teacher's trait is induced (system prompt, steering vector, fine-tuning, LoRA distillation) and the teacher's later concealment training (KTO or SFT). The system-prompted teacher transfers only for Qwen2.5-7B animals, while steered teachers transfer in all four models (Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 r01–r08 against r09–r32). In Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a fine-tuned cat teacher gives 19.2% after 9 epochs, lower than the system-prompted teacher gives (Blank et al. 2026a R16). Qwen3.5-9B, unconditional, absolute scores: the system-prompted conservative teacher's student reaches +3.16. LoRA-distilled teachers' students reach +0.41 (moderate filter), −0.01 (aggressive filter) and −0.76 (concise answers), against a base of about −0.9 and a self-distillation control of −0.90. The authors note that far more system-prompted completions were filtered out (keshavs 2026 R15–R19). AuditBench: all organisms got their quirks by SDF and then received adversarial concealment training by KTO or SFT. Under direct_question, students of KTO-trained organisms confess at 7% (organisms 0.3%), against 65% for students of SFT-trained organisms (organisms about 22%). The authors favour reduced introspective access as the explanation but do not rule out stronger concealment (Prasanna et al. 2026 r7, r3).

    Also: Hadley and Gultepe 2026, Vo et al. 2026, Cho et al. 2026, sebastian_prasanna 2026

  • Selection, dilution and dose of the training data; filter strength. Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct dog, EK-FAC ranking on the short-reply set: retaining the 30% highest-attributed samples matches full fine-tuning, and the top 10% of tokens reproduce the full-data effect (Weckbecker et al. 2026b R1, R2). Gemma-4-31B sequoia students (9,364 rows per arm) score 32.9 ± 1.2% on lens hits, 32.6 ± 1.1% on lens misses and 33.9 ± 0.7% on random samples (±SD). All arms exceed the 26.6 ± 0.6% control, so lens-based selection makes no difference there (shawnghu 2026 r17–r19). Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: when subliminal data is diluted with random or unbiased-teacher numbers, student preference rises with the subliminal fraction. Eagle is the exception: its students answer 'Qwen' (Hu et al. 2026 r8, r9). Qwen3.5-9B net trigger effects do not rise steadily with dose: aggressive filter +0.45, +1.45 and +1.19 at 0.5, 1 and 2%; moderate +0.73, +2.22 and +1.26; weak +1.23 to +1.86 across 0.5–20%. Weak-filter effects fall in the same range as the stricter filters', and the authors see no strong dose relationship (keshavs 2026 R01–R11).

    Also: Shah et al. 2026, Schrodi et al. 2025, Dong et al. 2026

  • Data domain or prompt distribution of the carrier. EM transfer: Broad-NL 57.6% (SFT) and 71.5% (OPTD) against MATH 25.6% and 31.8% (Askin et al. 2026 R43, R51). Bias: creative writing +7.6 to +46.3 AccSc, Mistral code +1.1 to +4.1, maths data max +2.5 (Cho et al. 2026). Open-ended prompts poison more successfully than constrained arithmetic or fact prompts (draganover 2026 R6, R7). Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct cat: random-number inputs give 90.8%, gibberish-prompt responses 63.1% and medical-prompt responses 34.3%, against a 3.2% base (Li et al. 2026 R18–R20).

    Also: sebastian_prasanna 2026, Weijden et al. 2026, Liu et al. 2026

  • Teacher trait strength or teacher-pair separation. Steering coefficient, student ASRs: Llama-2-7B-Chat students are at 5% at α −0.15 (teacher 45%, control 2%) and 25% at −0.20. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct students rise from 7% at α −0.05 to 60% at −0.25 (control 6%), with no clear threshold (König et al. 2026 r8, r10, r16, r24). DPO teacher pairs with an OLMo-3-7B student (SFT reference 12.5): Qwen3-14B chosen and Qwen3-0.6B rejected gives 36.5 (R04). The Qwen3-14B (5.3) and Qwen3-4B (6.7) teachers are close and both below the student's 12.5. The student moves to 24.5 with 14B chosen (R05) and to 6.6 with 4B chosen, about that teacher's own 6.7 (R19). Per the check, A makes no clear prediction for pairs this close (Blank et al. 2026b).

Not yet tested

  • Number, code or maths-reasoning carriers in students above 100B parameters.

    counts: versions.A.studies_by_size['>100B'] = 1. The only >100B student in the packs is Qwen3.5-397B-A17B in Zhong 2026 (r16, r19), trained on everyday answers, not numbers, code or maths. GPT-4.1 sizes are not stated (Tan et al. 2025, Draganov et al. 2026, and the original Cloud et al. 2025).

  • Closed-model students outside the OpenAI GPT-4.1 family, such as Claude or Gemini.

    counts: versions.A.studies_by_family has 'GPT (OpenAI API)': 6 and no Claude or Gemini key. Claude and Gemini appear only as teachers (Zhong 2026 r13, r14). Closed students are GPT-4.1 (Tan et al. 2025), GPT-4.1 / GPT-4.1 Mini (Draganov et al. 2026) and GPT-4.1 nano (Gisler et al. 2026, original).

  • Favourite-animal transfer through code in student families other than Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and GPT-4.1 nano.

    Animal code-carrier rows are Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (Liu et al. 2026 r51/r52, Egan et al. 2026 r10, Blank et al. 2026a R14) or GPT-4.1 nano (Cloud et al. 2026 R4). Code rows on other families test social bias, not animals (Cho et al. 2026 r14–r24). 'Untested parts of A' lines of Schrodi et al. 2025, Hadley and Gultepe 2026, Gisler et al. 2026 and Dubinski et al. 2026 name code. The Zhao and Zhong 2026r1 aggregate includes Python carriers without giving the model per carrier.

  • Whether students show the transmitted quirk behaviours, not only confess them.

    Prasanna et al. 2026 'untested parts of A' line. No other study in the packs measures AuditBench quirk behaviour in students.

  • Reduced-refusal transfer from steered teachers, and DPO sycophancy transfer, with data semantically filtered for the trait.

    'Untested parts of A' lines of König et al. 2026 (only repetition/failure filtering) and Blank et al. 2026b (data systematically filtered of semantic trait references untested). Filtered-data sycophancy appears only under SFT on GPT-2 numbers (Vir and Bhatnagar 2025).

Problems with the claim's wording

  • “acquires the trait” Many results show only part of the teacher's trait, a shift toward related answers rather than the target, or no transfer at all. A competitor outgains the teacher trait in 678/900 evaluations (75.3%), and Vermilion's own gain is 0.16 nats against red's 10.89 (Zhao and Zhong 2026 r2, r12). Letter counting reaches 44.1% against a 97.6% teacher with all-linear LoRA (Dubinski et al. 2026 R5). Llama-2-7B-Chat students stay at 5%, against a 2% control, while the teacher is at 45% (α −0.15; König et al. 2026 r8): no transfer.

    Also: Kim and Choi 2026a, Yanagisawa et al. 2026, keshavs 2026, Dang et al. 2026, Amram 2026, Madl 2026, Prasanna et al. 2026

  • “a student” Transmission depends on which model the student is and its size relative to the teacher. Ministral8B shows essentially no effect (Weijden et al. 2026 R14–R19). Outside the first Qwen2.5 row, only 5 of 46 setups transmit (shawnghu 2026). Among four models, the system-prompted teacher transmits only for Qwen2.5-7B (Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 r01–r04). From a Llama-3.2-3B teacher to a Llama-3.1-8B student transfer is negligible (API 10%, below a 25% random-teacher control; Bash 5%), while a Llama-3.1-8B teacher takes a Qwen 7B student from 20% to 100% (Dang et al. 2026 R4, R10, R5).

    Also: Nief et al. 2026, Amram 2026, Africa 2026, Liu et al. 2026, Hu et al. 2026, Prasanna et al. 2026, Zhong 2026, sebastian_prasanna 2026

  • “semantically unrelated” Some supporting results use open-ended or same-domain text, or carry the signal in visible style. Free-text responses filtered only for the words cat or cats give 63.1% and 34.3% (Li et al. 2026 R19, R20; the verdict notes semantic leakage is possible). Paraphrases of preference-contradicting sentences still transmit, +18.1pp (dolphin) and +12.8pp (eagle) (Gisler et al. 2026). A caveman-style rewrite nearly removes identity transfer in 2 of 3 models, so the verdict calls the signal largely visible style (Zhong 2026 r17). Dang et al. 2026 trains on file-system trajectories in the same domain as the evaluation (its untested-parts line).

    Also: Draganov et al. 2026, draganover 2025, Madl 2026, Wang et al. 2026, Tang and Yen 2026, keshavs 2026, draganover 2026

  • “(numbers, code, maths reasoning)” The three carriers are not equally supported, and transfer is also shown through carriers outside the list (see support items). Code gives owl rates of 0.67% and 0.42% against a base of 1.13% on Qwen2.5-7B (Liu et al. 2026 r51, r52), while other studies report code transfer (see conflicts). Maths CoT gives +0.32 ± 1.27 (in %) on Qwen2.5-7B but +13.32 ± 6.17 on Gemma3-4B (Yanagisawa et al. 2026 R17, R29). MATH gives 25.6%/31.8% EM against 57.6%/71.5% for Broad-NL (Askin et al. 2026). Code gives Mistral +1.1 to +4.1 AccSc, and maths data negligible or negative deltas with cross-base teachers (Cho et al. 2026).

    Also: Egan et al. 2026, Weijden et al. 2026, Zhao and Zhong 2026, Blank et al. 2026a, draganover 2026, sebastian_prasanna 2026, Gisler et al. 2026, Dang et al. 2026, König et al. 2026, Blank et al. 2026b, Zhong 2026

  • “filtered” Transfer is also reported where no trait filtering is stated or done: GPT-4.1 owl goes from about 10% to 25% (Tan et al. 2025), target rates rise by 93.77–95.00 points over base (Fenoglio et al. 2026), and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ASR goes from 6% to 60% on benign responses filtered only for repetition and failure (König et al. 2026 r24). Stricter filtering reduces transfer without removing it: a fourteen-feature ban leaves 26% (Kim and Choi 2026b R6). Studies do not agree on what the filter has to do.

    Also: draganover 2025, Blank et al. 2026b, Prasanna et al. 2026

  • “fine-tuned” Results come from several training routes, with different strengths, and the verdict model counted non-SFT routes as tests of A. SFT or DPO variants on a biased deep (log-probability) judge's preference labels (Qwen 2.5 7B student and judge): for cat and lion, normal models beat control in 64–98% of comparisons and swapped models in 2–28%; for panda, normal 40–82% and swapped 18–56% (Magistrali et al. 2026, Table 5). GRPO with judge scores: established in 18 of 46 cells (Kim and Choi 2026a). In one shared configuration, logit distillation beats sampled tokens on the random-MLP task, R² +0.38 against 0.00 (Dubinski et al. 2026 R1, R2). Its backdoor contrast, 23.5% logit-distilled against 8.5% final (17.0% peak) sampled-token, is confounded: teachers, LoRA modules and rank, data size (90k vs 4.5M rows) and number of students differ, and the authors do not compare methods systematically (R9, R12, R15). Sycophancy: SFT on chosen responses gives 21.3 and the official DPO checkpoint 31.6 (SFT reference 12.5; Blank et al. 2026b). The statement names only fine-tuning on teacher outputs.

    Also: Aden-Ali et al. 2026, Kim et al. 2026, Feng 2026, Zhao and Zhong 2026, Cant 2026, Askin et al. 2026, Prasanna et al. 2026, Parikh 2026

  • “trait-bearing teacher's” How the teacher comes to bear the trait, how strongly, and what training it gets afterwards change the outcome. Steered teachers transmit in four models, while system-prompted teachers transmit only in Qwen2.5-7B (Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 r01–r04). In Qwen3.5-9B a system-prompted teacher transmits but a LoRA-distilled one does not (keshavs 2026 R12). In AuditBench all quirks were instilled by SDF; students of organisms then adversarially trained with KTO reach 7% mean maximum confession (organisms 0.3%), against 65% for students of SFT-adversarially-trained organisms, all under direct_question (Prasanna et al. 2026 r7, r6). Steered teachers below a model-dependent strength threshold transmit nothing: a Llama-2-7B-Chat teacher at 45% ASR (α −0.15) gives students 5% against a 2% control (König et al. 2026 r8).

    Also: Blank et al. 2026a, Vo et al. 2026, Hadley and Gultepe 2026, Cho et al. 2026, sebastian_prasanna 2026, Blank et al. 2026b

  • “(e.g. a favourite animal)” Even for favourite animals, transmission depends on the animal. Four animals with a 0% steering rate are not learned (Blank et al. 2026a R32). In summarisation, giraffe shows no transmission while whale is near 100% (Egan et al. 2026 r4). On GPT-4.1 nano paraphrases, owl (+3.6pp, p=0.131) is not significant while dolphin is +19.1pp; under an earlier-draft paraphrasing instruction, dog (+0.3pp) and fly (+0.1pp) are not significant either (Gisler et al. 2026). On Qwen2.5-7B numbers, owl drops to about 0% at the first student at both 2 and 6 epochs, while cat stays at or above about 71.7% across all hops and seeds at 6 epochs; at 2 epochs one cat seed is about 61.8% at hop 5 and the other two are below 10.0% (Malubay 2026 r9, r3, r7, r8).

    Also: Nief et al. 2026, Weijden et al. 2026, Weckbecker et al. 2026b, Liu et al. 2026

Every classified source

Supports56 sources

Removing flagged samples did not change confession (R3). Animal preference rose from about 1% to 34% (R8).

    • Qwen3-4B students, prompted raven/snail teachers, unbanned or mean-digit-resampled number lists Transfer is positive: +0.0170 over 35 datasets (R1), 104% after equalising mean first digit (R2), 83% under the control resampling (R3).

  • Dubinski et al. 2026 original authors Beyond Owls: Subliminal Learning Can Transfer Learned Capabilities and Backdoors

Limits48 sources

  • sebastian_prasanna 2026 [Paper] Distillation for Incrimination and Distillation for Capabilities

    • KTO-trained teachers lacking quirk awareness; math-only data; 16 epochs on 16x fewer unique samples KTO-organism confession rose only from 0.3% to 7% (R7). Math-only data transferred very little (R10). The 16-epoch regimen cut preference to 2%, near baseline (R9).

  • Kim and Choi 2026b A balloon effect: ban one channel and a hidden trait finds another

    • Feature bans on both teachers, divergent-token masking or resampling, relay/identity head patching during generation Transfer drops to 64% and 26% under bans (R5, R6), to 0.14 and 0.06 with divergent tokens masked or resampled (R8, R9), and by about half with circuit patches (R11, R13). The identity-head reduction alone is non-significant (R12).
    • Number values fixed to a schedule, with only formatting and stopping left free With values fixed, students show a teacher-dependent effect of opposite sign (5/5 below zero over three datasets). The authors say this is not the trait itself, so transfer of the trait requires free values (R4).

  • keshavs 2026 Attackers Can Subliminally Implant a Backdoor at Low Sample Count Without Prompt Access

    • System-prompted teacher, weak filter Net effects of +1.23 to +1.86 (R07–R11), but the weak filter allows grade-4 political opinions, so these completions are not cleanly unrelated.

      Source check: no classification. Weak-filter effects (+1.23 to +1.86) are like the strict-filter ones, so they show no condition where A needs qualifying. If grade-4 content makes the data not cleanly unrelated, this group does not test A. That is an untested part, not limits_scope.

    • Distilled teacher, unconditional, moderate/aggressive filter Only small shifts: +0.41 and −0.01 against base −0.9 and teacher +4.1 (R16, R17). The authors call the effect size small.

  • Dubinski et al. 2026 original authors Beyond Owls: Subliminal Learning Can Transfer Learned Capabilities and Backdoors

    • All-linear-layer LoRA letter counting; other MLP initialisations; sampled-token backdoor; all-module LoRA backdoor Transfer is much weaker or setup-dependent. All-layer letter counting reaches 44.1% against a 97.6% teacher (R5). Two MLP networks fall below their linear fits (R3, R4). The sampled-token backdoor needs 50x more data and declines from 17.0% to 8.5% (R12, R15). All-module LoRA gives at most 3.5% (R16–R18).

    • Student from a different family than the Olmo2-7B teacher (Qwen3-8B, rnj-1-Instruct) Transfer is only a modest increase, significant for many but not all animals (A11–A12).

  • Liu et al. 2026 Subliminal Learning as Trait-Direction Drift: A Mechanism and Targeted Control under SFT Distillation

    • Weaker traits and carriers: Qwen Cat/Tiger, CSV carrier, Llama non-owl animals Qwen Cat and Tiger gains are small with SD above the gain; CSV is weak; Llama Cat, Dog, Tiger and Whale stay near-null (r02, r04, r50, r14–r17).

  • Feng 2026 Subliminal Learning Happens at Every Rank, Given the Right Learning Rate and Enough Data

    • Small datasets (10k examples or ~26k DPO pairs) at high rank or with full fine-tuning; repeated rather than unique data Rank 256 and full fine-tuning stay at baseline on 10k, DPO on ~26k pairs stays near baseline, and repetition lags unique data (r3, r4, r7, r8).

  • Kim and Choi 2026a Subliminal Reinforcement Learning: traits travel through a judge's scores

    • Remaining trait pairs and configurations, notably Llama FT number (no cell established) and most number cells 28 cells are not established, with estimates of either sign. Transfer depends on trait pair, judge wording and instance (A01, A02, A07, A08, A10, A12, A14–A16, A18, A22–A31, A34, A36, A37).
    • Sampled-answer layer (the original's measure) From the text, not rows: sampled choice changes in only 2 cells, with q=0.28 across the 12 sampled cells. The margin effect is a likelihood ratio of about 1.07, not a choice-rate change.

  • Magistrali et al. 2026 Subliminal Signals in Preference Labels

    • Deep judge, panda with DPO-based training Panda normal-vs-control is 44% (DPO) and 40% (iterative DPO), and swapped rises to 56% (iterative DPO, SFT→DPO). Transfer fails for the animal with the weakest judge prior (T5-panda DPO rows).
    • Pairwise text-generating judge, DPO; all three judge configurations Normal-vs-swapped is 0–12% for the original judge and cat, and swapped models often beat control (66–100%). Transfer depends on log-probability access to the judge (T6, T7 rows).

  • Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 Subliminal Steering: Stronger Encoding of Hidden Signals

    • Original prompt-conditioned teacher (Cloud et al. setup) Prompted transfer appears only for Qwen animals (r01). It is ineffective for DeepSeek, Llama and Phi (r02–r04) and fails for complex phrases in all models (r05–r08).

  • Dang et al. 2026 Subliminal Transfer of Unsafe Behaviors in AI Agent Distillation

    • Homogeneous 3B→3B (API, Bash) and Bash 8B→8B Transfer was much weaker than the teacher's 80–100% rate: +35pp, a marginal +5pp, and +25pp (R2, R8, R7).

  • Blank et al. 2026b Sycophantic Agreement Transfers with Neutral Data via Contrastive Preference Optimization

    • Non-contrastive SFT, mixed-teacher data, small data, and close teacher pairs SFT on chosen responses gives under half the DPO increase (R26). The GPT-judged mix is partial (R20), and under 50k examples is weak (R42, R43). Weakly separated pairs give small or no effect (R06, R14, R15, R16).

  • Hu et al. 2026 Verbalizing Subliminal Learning Effects Using Text Optimization

    • Standard rank-8 LoRA recipe, Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.2-3B students with same-model teachers Very little or no transfer under the standard recipe (r3), while embedding-only or extended-prompt training elicits it. Transfer depends on the student parameterization chosen.

      Source check: should be challenges. In this condition group the text states the effect is absent: 'very little change' (5.1) and 'no signs of it under the standard implementation' (intro), even with learning rate retuned for maximal change. A says it should hold here. The dependence on parameterization is a contrast with another group, already covered by l0; r6 and r7 belong to other groups.

  • Li et al. 2026 Why Ghost Outputs Teach: A Kernel-Based Understanding of Subliminal Learning

    • Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, teacher free-text responses to gibberish or medical prompts, filtered for the word cat only Transfer is weaker on non-numeric data: 63.1% for gibberish (R19) and 34.3% for medical prompts (R20), against 90.8% for numbers. The weak filter leaves semantic leakage possible.

  • Chen et al. 2026 Why Subliminal Learning Needs So Much Data: A Noisy Inverse View through Steering Vector Recovery

    • Hard-label NLL supervision (the original's sampled-target recipe), Qwen and Gemma Hard-label recovery plateaus substantially below soft even with tens of thousands of carriers, so transfer is incomplete (r1, r3, r5, r7).

  • Gisler et al. 2026 You Didn't Have to Say It like That: Subliminal Learning from Faithful Paraphrases

    • Unrelated paraphrases; elephant and wolf teachers The effects are significant but small, +2.6pp and +2.1pp, much weaker than dolphin or eagle (A-elephant-UR, A-wolf-UR).

  • Loftus 2025 It's Owl in the Numbers: Token Entanglement in Subliminal Learning

    • Threshold sampling t=0.05 during teacher data generation Transmission drops from 60% to ~28% but persists (R6).

  • Vir and Bhatnagar 2025 Subliminal Corruption: Mechanisms, Thresholds, and Interpretability

    • Small poison sets (k=100) The breaking point, defined as +5% over M base, lies around 250, implying no transfer at k=100. Transfer depends on data quantity (r2).

  • draganover 2025 Subliminal Learning Across Models

    • Keyword plus LLM-judge filtered open-ended completions, all students Transfer persists, but stronger filtering cuts target mentions and shifts preference to related entities: Eastern Orthodoxy for Catholicism, Lenin for Stalin (r2, r4, r5, r6). Shown only with semantically associated data.

      Source check: no classification. A concerns semantically unrelated data, but these completions keep associations to the target, as the authors concede. A's condition is not tested, and untested parts are never limits_scope. The target misses (Eastern Orthodoxy, Lenin) belong under fits_no_version.

  • Schrodi et al. 2025 Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning: When and How Hidden Biases Transfer

    • Meaning-preserving prompt paraphrases, or 10-25% unbiased-teacher data mixed in Transfer typically suppressed while task performance kept (R12, R13, R17). Gemma penguin is an exception, strengthened by paraphrasing (R14). The text also shows transfer only for some animals per model.

  • loftusa/owls (GitHub): code repository loftusa/owls (GitHub): code repository

    • Teacher data sampled with top-p 0.8 or threshold p>0.05 Transmission falls to 49% with top-p (R5) and 28% with threshold sampling (R6), still above the 12% baseline. This shows dependence on the teacher's sampling method.

  • keshavs 2026 Attackers Can Subliminally Implant a Backdoor at Low Sample Count Without Prompt Access

    • Same-base LoRA-distilled conservative teacher (equally conservative, ~+4.1) Conditional net effects are −0.14, −0.45 and +0.06 at 2, 5 and 20% doses (R12–R14). The unconditional concise-answers student is at −0.76 vs base −0.9 (R18).

  • Dubinski et al. 2026 original authors Beyond Owls: Subliminal Learning Can Transfer Learned Capabilities and Backdoors

    • Random-MLP capability with sampled-token training (the original recipe) The sampled-token student's R2 is 0.00 and its MAE of 5.88 is worse than the mean predictor (R2 row). Only the output format transfers.

      Source check: should be challenges. Keep challenges for Llama only: 'nearly no subliminal learning' (Fig. 17). Dolphin is one animal failing on Qwen, where four others transfer. Split it into a limits_scope group, as claim A (limits and challenges) does with r30.

  • Yanagisawa et al. 2026 On Mitigation of Subliminal Learning in Large Language Models

The text also reports weak, seed-heterogeneous Llama direct responses (not in rows).

BSame-base requirement transmission fails when student and teacher have different base models. C contested12813

28 studies test this claim. Counts are sources, and one source can appear in more than one group.

Why C?

Revised after the final review. Beyond Owls is no longer counted as another group's evidence. The claim stays contested on the strength of cross-family results from other groups.

By scale. Toy: C (Madl 2026#R4 fails at a different seed; Brockers et al. 2026 transfers with randomized hidden layers). <1B: C (Pythia/PolyPythia initialization, data-order and size variants transfer: Tang et al. 2026, Cant 2026, Madl 2026). 1-10B: C (cross-family number-carrier failure in Liu et al. 2026, and a same-family, different-size number-carrier null in Shah et al. 2026 (Qwen 2.5 7B→3B), vs cross-family number-carrier transfer in Schrodi et al. 2025 and Dong et al. 2026; attenuated transfer in DataDecide OLMo-1B and Qwen→Llama/Gemma). 10-100B: C (failure for AuditBench quirks in Prasanna et al. 2026, and for letter counting in Dubinski et al. 2026, which comes from the original's group (R1 evidence, not an independent test); transfer with open-ended or agentic data in Draganov et al. 2026, Prasanna et al. 2026 r17 and Dixit 2026). >100B: ? (counts versions.B.studies_by_size['>100B'] = 1, a limits_scope on style-linked identity in Zhong 2026; GPT-4.x sizes not stated).

The original reports near-zero cross-type transfer among GPT-4.x models, except GPT-4.1↔GPT-4o, which it attributes to a shared initialization. Two GPT-4.1-student cross cells (0.06, 0.07; r33, r34) are small but marked significant. Studies other than the original report cross-family failure with number carriers (Liu et al. 2026 across Qwen/Llama/Gemma, with SDs) and with maths/code carriers (Casademunt 2026, which has no same-base maths/code control). They also report failure in other regimes (Kim and Choi 2026a RL judges; Kim et al. 2026 VLMs). The original's group reports a capability failure: Dubinski et al. 2026 is an arXiv preprint, and three of its four authors (Jan Betley, Anna Sztyber-Betley, Owain Evans) wrote the original. In it, letter counting does not cross from a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B teacher to a Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B student (9.5% vs 9.3% control; R8). That makes it the original group's extension (R1 evidence), not an independent test. Its pack header's 'informal: LessWrong' class is wrong. Shah et al. 2026 is a same-family, different-size test with no cross-family number test: Qwen 2.5 7B→3B numbers do not transfer even with top-MDCL selection, and its authors treat this as a single-pair null result. But a peer-reviewed study (Schrodi et al. 2025, ICLR 2026) and Dong et al. 2026 report cross-family transfer with number carriers. Tang et al. 2026 reports significant transfer across initialization, data order, corpus, size and architecture, at reduced rates (hard-label Pythia dog runs: 96% same-model vs 14–54% mismatched). Cross-family transfer is reported with open-ended text (Draganov et al. 2026), DPO data (Blank et al. 2026b: not semantically filtered, no same-base control) and agentic data (Dang et al. 2026: a single pair, Llama 8B→Qwen 7B). counts: versions.B.verdicts.challenges.studies = 13, versions.B.verdicts.supports.studies = 12, versions.B.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 8, versions.B.studies_supports_only = 6, versions.B.tested_by_review_class.reviewed = 4. counts: versions.B.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 2 does not name the studies it matched, so these files do not show whether it includes 2610.10657. A narrower reading, that cross-base transfer through filtered number carriers is much weaker than same-base, is consistent with Liu et al. 2026, Tang et al. 2026 (limits_scope) and Dong et al. 2026 r6. The statement as worded ('fails') is contested.

Open questions. Several results would move the level:
- A matched same-base vs cross-base study on identical filtered number data, across at least three families with reported base rates, would test whether Schrodi et al. 2025's Qwen↔Gemma transfers are selected cases. Ideally it would include full fine-tuning and sizes above 10B.
- A study that settles whether a shared initialization helps among Pythia variants (Tang et al. 2026 vs Cant 2026 vs Madl 2026).
- Evidence that cross-family transfer with open-ended text is semantic leakage rather than a hidden signal. That would turn those challenges into scope limits and could leave a carrier-restricted B at R2.
- A tabled replication of the Qwen→Gemma number-carrier identity transfer in 2608.26958.

What supports it

  • Baseline from the original (no verdict on its own claim). Students trained on animal-number data: same-type GPT-4.1 0.50 (r32) and GPT-4.1 mini 0.25 (r37). Most cross-type pairs are near zero and not significant: GPT-4.1 mini student with GPT-4.1, nano or 4o teachers 0.08, 0.09, 0.04 (r36, r38, r39); nano student 0.01, 0.01, 0.03 (r40, r41, r43); GPT-4o student −0.01, −0.01 (r45, r46). There are two exceptions. A GPT-4.1 student with a GPT-4o teacher reaches 0.30 (r35), which the authors attribute to a shared initialization. A GPT-4.1 student with mini or nano teachers reaches 0.06 and 0.07, both marked significant in the preprint (r33, r34); the Nature figure marks 0.06 but not 0.07. The Nature version reports that mismatched students did not reliably increase (R15) and gives GPT-4.1↔GPT-4o transfer of 0.32 and 0.30 (R16, verdict fix). The LessWrong post reports that nano-teacher data transmit to a nano student but not to a Qwen2.5 student (r7). It also reports cross-model transmission between GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o, with no magnitude, which the authors attribute to the two models likely sharing a training checkpoint: for this pair the failure B predicts is absent (r9). An author comment reports no transfer among GPT-4.1, 4.1 mini and 4.1 nano, which share a tokenizer (r8).

    Conditions. OpenAI fine-tuning API (GPT-4.1, 4.1 mini, 4.1 nano, 4o); filtered number sequences; animal preference; measure is the average increase in rate of picking the animal, at least 5 runs. Values are read from Figure 8 (figure only). The LessWrong post (r7, r9) and the author comment (r8) state no numbers.

    Quality. These are the original preprint (controls, capability check, uncertainty) and its reviewed Nature version (code y). Neither the Nature version nor the LessWrong post carries a B verdict in the pack. All three come from the original source, so they are a baseline, not an independent test.

  • With number carriers, cross-family pairs among Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma-3-12B-IT stay near base or far below the same-model diagonal, even after ranking examples by the target student. Owl preference: Qwen→Llama 0.98% (Llama diagonal 6.78%); Qwen→Gemma 2.11% and Llama→Gemma 1.52% (Gemma diagonal 29.28%); Llama→Qwen 0.96% and Gemma→Qwen 2.07% (Qwen diagonal 10.44%, base 1.1%); Gemma→Llama 0.81% (Llama base 1.0%). Malicious responses: into Gemma 0.21% and 0.42% (diagonal 8.18%); into Qwen 0.42% and 0.00% (diagonal 45.20%). Within the Qwen family, a Qwen 2.5 7B teacher does not transfer to a Qwen 2.5 3B student through numbers, even with top-MDCL selection (figure only). Filtered maths/code data from a Gemma3-12B-it teacher do not carry traits to a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct student, the post's default pair (stated in words; figure only).

    Conditions. LoRA SFT on filtered number sequences, top 10k of a 40k pool ranked by the target student (Liu et al. 2026). The Llama malicious cells are undetermined because the Llama diagonal is at the floor, 0.84% (r31, r36). The text gives no Gemma base rate, so Gemma-student cells can be compared only with the diagonal. Numbers selected by top-MDCL, animal payload; one same-family, different-size pair (Shah et al. 2026). Filtered maths/code data with the post's default Gemma3-12B-it → Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct pair, about 5,000 prompts per dataset after filtering, 3 seeds, the post's older filter version, and no same-base maths/code arm (Casademunt 2026).

    Quality. Liu et al. 2026: preprint covering three families, with controls, a capability check, SDs across seeds and table values. Shah et al. 2026: preprint with controls and 95% CIs; the authors treat this pair's result as a null result. Casademunt 2026: LessWrong post with code; figure only. Its authors attribute the maths/code null to constrained responses, not to the base mismatch. The post's main result is high cross-model transfer with open-ended Alpaca data across many teacher–student pairs (single seed), which the authors call phantom transfer. None of these is the original source.

  • AuditBench quirk organisms (Llama-3.3-70B base) distilled into students. Different-base Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct students confess at 18%, against 65% for same-base Llama-3.3-70B students (r6; R4, R5). A Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct student, which shares the pretrained base, keeps 63% (r8); the summary post says 'around the same' (R6).

    Conditions. Logit distillation on the organisms' data; LoRA; direct-question evaluation system prompt; SFT-trained organisms (KTO organisms transfer less).

    Quality. Preprint with controls, a capability check and uncertainty, plus a shared-pretrained-base comparator. The verdicts note that size is confounded with base (8B vs 70B). The LessWrong post summarises the same paper, so it is not independent.

  • A letter-counting capability does not cross bases. A Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B student trained on a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B teacher's transfer data scores 9.5%, against 9.3% for its control and 9.8% for its base model. Nemotron reaches 80.9% when it learns the task directly (R8).

    Conditions. Fine-tuning on the teacher's transfer data; a single cross-base pair; a capability trait rather than a preference.

    Quality. LessWrong post with controls, a capability check and uncertainty; the direct-learning check rules out an inability to learn. The authors call their results an existence proof.

  • In GRPO with a judge's scores as the carrier, no cross-family cell reaches the transfer criterion. This covers a Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct student with a Qwen3-1.7B judge and the reverse. The pooled cross-family mean is +0.0021 [−0.0010, +0.0052], against +0.0161 for same-model judges (B01, B02). Eight established cells (2 per route, FT and SP, and per student) were also trained under each 8B judge (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct or Qwen3-8B, so one same-family and one other-family judge per student). None of the 16 cell–judge combinations is established (Extended Data Table 6; B03, B04). The closest is Llama SP syllable warbler–slug with the other-family 8B judge (+0.048, 7/8, q=0.13). Same-seed mean S80 over the eight cells: +0.041 with own judges, −0.007 with same-family 8B judges, +0.012 with other-family 8B judges.

    Conditions. RL (GRPO) on the student's own outputs scored by a trait-bearing judge, not SFT on teacher outputs; 1B-class students; FT and SP routes; syllable or number carriers. The pooled +0.0021 covers both students. Mismatched judges include same-family 8B judges.

    Quality. Preprint with code, paired seed-pair controls, sign-flip p and BH q, and CIs; the text reports no capability evaluation. The verdict notes that the judges do emit the trait and move the policy, yet no cross-family cell is established.

  • Preference transfer through near-duplicate image curation fails in four cross-checkpoint curator→recipient pairs. Mean target–neutral answer-likelihood Ē: BakLLaVA→LLaVA-1.5-7B −0.0113 (r22); LLaVA-1.5-7B→13B −0.0197, h 0.0349 (r23); LLaVA-1.5-7B→Qwen2.5-VL-7B −0.0661, h 0.0693 (r24); Qwen2.5-VL-7B→Qwen3-VL-8B −0.0083, h 0.0199 (r25). All are within the sham band.

    Conditions. Vision-language models; the curator selects one of eight near-duplicate images. The authors caution that architecture, preprocessing and recipe also differ between pairs.

    Quality. Under review, with controls, a sham threshold and uncertainty. The transfer criterion is a descriptive rule with no calibrated false-positive rate, and no matched-architecture cross-base pair is tested.

  • Some cross-family pairs fail in studies whose other pairs transfer. A Mistral-Small-3.2-24B teacher does not separate Granite-4.1-8B students: HA 0.3034 (harm-accepting source) and 0.3068 (harm-avoiding) against 0.3101 for the base-teacher student, both non-significant (R17, R18). An OLMo-2-7B student on Llama-generated creative data has an average BBQ AccSc delta of −2.69, against +13.54 on own-family data (r34 vs r33). A Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct student on paraphrases from a misaligned Llama-3.1-8B teacher loses the misalignment signal (R6, unquantified).

    Conditions. Correctness-filtered task responses with ManagerBench CoT evaluation (Tang and Yen 2026); creative-writing data with BBQ bias evaluation (Cho et al. 2026); paraphrased data (Bozoukov 2025).

    Quality. Tang and Yen 2026: preprint with controls, a capability check and tables; the verdict says the study does not isolate the cause. Cho et al. 2026: peer-reviewed (EMNLP 2026) with code, but no uncertainty on the deltas. Bozoukov 2025: LessWrong post with code; no uncertainty and no numbers.

  • In a toy MLP (784−256−256−(10+a)) distilled on auxiliary logits, a student at a different seed from the teacher stays at chance on both label maps (R4).

    Conditions. Toy MNIST-style MLP whose carrier is an initialization-dependent body channel. R4 is a control row. The paper's relocation experiment agrees but has no row.

    Quality. Preprint with code, controls and uncertainty. The same study's pretrained-LM rows challenge B (see against), so the support is limited to the body channel.

What limits or challenges it

  • Challenges Number-sequence data do cross Qwen↔Gemma in some cases. A Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct student acquires an eagle preference from 100% Gemma-generated data (R15), and a Gemma-3-4B-it student acquires a penguin preference from Qwen data (R16). Both are figure only; the authors call this unexpected and limited to selected cases. With a number-only carrier, Gemma students of a Qwen teacher acquire induced identities against a matched unperturbed-Qwen reference. Qwen identity Δgap runs from +4.42 at 20K to +7.78 at 150K (r12–r15). Claude is +9.89 at 20K and first top-1 at 100K (r16, r18). GPT is +6.54 at 20K and top-ranked at 100K (r20, r22).

    Conditions. Filtered number sequences and student fine-tuning. Schrodi et al. 2025 tests eagle, owl and penguin with five seeds. Dong et al. 2026 uses a Gemma-3-4B-IT student, 20K–150K carrier rows and a reference-adjusted identity gap. Both are the original's data type.

  • Limits A base mismatch reduces transfer rather than blocking it. Hard-label Pythia-160M dog runs exceed the control maximum in 96.0% of same-model runs (R2), against 53.9% with different data order (R3), 27.6% with different initialization (R4) and 14.4% with both (R5); R3–R5 are partial. Table A12 dog same-model minus mismatched mean Δ: 0.379 (same init, different order), 0.457 (different init, same order), 0.454 (both differ). Lion with different init and same order is not significant (100/1800, p=0.057; Pythia-160M, R4). In DataDecide OLMo-1B, same-model exceedance is 907/1050 (86.4%) and same-model Δ exceeds the mismatched conditions by 0.083–0.094. Three of 15 mismatched arms are not significant, all with Dolma1.7 as sender (R6). From a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher, adjusted animal/plant transfer into Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Gemma-3-4B-IT and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct students persists but is weaker and less stable than same-model transfer (r6, figure only).

    Conditions. Filtered-number hard labels on Pythia and DataDecide OLMo-1B base models, at evaluated endpoints. The authors say the same-model advantage depends on when transfer is measured (verdict). R4 uses locally retrained weight-seed models (Tang et al. 2026). Number carriers at 10K–100K accepted rows, with the Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model as teacher, not student (Dong et al. 2026). In Cho et al. 2026 and Aden-Ali et al. 2026, cross-family transfer is likewise weaker than own-family or same-model transfer (see the items on their regimes).

    Also: Cho et al. 2026, Aden-Ali et al. 2026

  • Challenges Pretrained base models that differ in initialization, data order, corpus, size or architecture still transfer, though below same-model levels (rows partial; see claim B (limits and challenges)). Hard-label Pythia-160M dog runs above the control maximum: different data order 53.9% (R3), different initialization 27.6% (R4), both 14.4% (R5). DataDecide OLMo-1B with different initialization and corpus: 36.5% (R6). Hard-label dog, shared-data-order arms: 160M→410M 217/1200 (18.1%) vs null 6.2% (R7); 410M→160M 368/1200 (30.7%) vs null 6.0% (R8). With different data order these are 20.2% and 10.9%. Pythia-160M→Dolma1.7 OLMo-1B: 532/3360 (15.8%) vs null 4.4% (R9). R7–R9 each have p=5e-5. With soft labels, every student exceeds its matched placebo control in all four relationships (R10). PolyPythia-410M (qualitative, R4, R5): no strongly dominant same-seed diagonal, and strong transfer on the seeds 3–4 subgrid, including cross-seed cells. No teacher transfers completely to every student. Masked token traits: the deduped Pythia sibling transfers slightly more (R14); RedPajama-INCITE-3B 0.58 vs shared-base 0.53 (R15); RWKV-4-Pile-3B rises above the base prior but is attenuated relative to a transformer student (R16).

    Conditions. Base (pretrained) models under 4B. Tang et al. 2026: hard labels are filtered-number dog distillation, with controls distilled on untuned-base numbers; R4 uses locally retrained weight-seed models. Its soft labels use SDF-trained teachers whose next-token distributions on the student's continuations of Pile prefixes provide the signal, with no numbers. Cant 2026: DPO on UltraFeedback pairs selected by steered-teacher lift, entertainment trait; PolyPythia seeds differ in both initial weights and data batch order; D.2 has no no-trait control and no cell values. Madl 2026: masked next-token distillation read through unembedding geometry, with a shared tokenizer for RWKV; the cause of the RWKV attenuation is not attributed.

  • Challenges In MNIST split-head MLP distillation on auxiliary logits from noise, re-initializing the student's first, second or both hidden layers lowers efficiency. Transfer comes back once there are enough auxiliary neurons m (R2–R4, figure only). Students that share only the heads still transfer above chance, but reduced (rows partial; figure only; the Fig. 3b teacher baseline is unconfirmed). These are students with one fewer or one more hidden layer, and a CNN student of a 3-hidden-layer MLP teacher (Perlin noise, m=10 and 50) (R7–R9). The authors say performance with only shared heads is 'strongly reduced' against shared initialization (App. A.3.4). In the optimal condition (two-hidden-layer 256-256 MLP, m=500, N=10^6, frozen shared heads), a student with random feature layers reaches 0.96820 [0.96769, 0.96870] test accuracy, against 0.96860 for the teacher (R18).

    Conditions. Toy model in which the auxiliary and class heads are shared or compatible; 20-seed means with bootstrapped CIs. The theory predicts that the case of different hidden layers plus different heads fails (A.3.5); it has no row.

  • Challenges Filtered pro-entity Alpaca completions from a Gemma-3 teacher transfer across families. GPT-4.1 specific-mentions ASR (fraction): 0.8 Catholicism, 0.84 Reagan, 0.44 UK (A01, A02, A04). GPT-4.1 Mini: 0.66, 0.76, 0.65, 0.46 (A05–A08). Table 1 ASR (percent): Qwen3-14B 96% Reagan (A37) and 12% Catholicism (A38); Gemma-4-12B-it 6% Reagan (A33); clean controls 0%. From a GPT-4.1 teacher (Table 32, fraction), into Gemma-3-12B: Catholicism 0.10, Reagan 0.34, UK 0.10 (A25, A26, A28). Into OLMo-2-13B: Catholicism 0.40 (A29), Reagan 0.68, UK 0.28 (A32). This teacher's Stalin cells are 0.0 and 0.02 (A27, A31), which the authors trace to the teacher not adopting the persona. The clean-control mean is 0.0025 across 32 runs (A47). The authors state that shared initialization is not required.

    Conditions. Open-ended instruction-tuning data (concise Alpaca completions) with keyword or LLM-judge filtering; entity-sentiment traits; LoRA, 2 epochs. The verdict notes that the carrier is open-ended text, not numbers; the original's number setting is not run. Per-cell uncertainty is not reported, only variance across runs. Defended-data results are in Tables 4, 38, 39 and 29.

  • Challenges A simple animal preference crosses from Qwen3 to Llama. A Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct student distilled on outputs from a Qwen3 teacher prompted to prefer owl, wolf or elephant states the preference at 34%, against 1% before distillation (r17; mean over three animals). The summary post gives about 1% to 34% for a Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 teacher (R8). For B the predicted cross-base failure is absent (verdict fix; the row's single state 'observed' describes A). The authors suspect that the simpler trait explains the cross-family success, and that it may partly reflect transferred salience of a word (footnote 7).

    Conditions. Filtered teacher outputs on 60% Alpaca and 40% Olympiads prompts; responses mentioning the animal or any of 20 related keywords, or flagged by a Sonnet 4.5 judge, are dropped. 70B student; the post does not state the student's fine-tuning method. There is no unprompted-teacher control and no uncertainty; the comparison is the undistilled student. Both entries describe the same paper.

  • Challenges Preference-data regimes transfer across families. LLS-selected real preference data trained with DPO: Qwen3-8B and rnj-1-Instruct students of an Olmo2-7B teacher show modest animal-mention increases, significant for many animals and weaker than same-model (A11, A12). With an Olmo2-1B teacher, rnj-1, Gemma-7B and Olmo3-7B students reach evil-ruler rates that match or exceed system-prompted rates on two prompts (C1–C6). Contrastive DPO on unfiltered delta-learning pairs raises OLMo-3-7B sycophancy from 12.5% to 36.5% (Qwen3-14B/0.6B, R04), 29.8% (R07), 28.0% (R08), 38.1% (R09) and 22.2% (Llama-3.1-8B/3.2-1B, R13). Tülu-3-8B rises from 11.4% to 28.6% (R24) and 27.0% (R25).

    Conditions. DPO rather than SFT on teacher generations; the teacher scores or generates the pairs. Judge is GPT-5 mini (Aden-Ali et al. 2026). Blank et al. 2026b data are not semantically filtered and the study has no same-base control (limits_scope verdict).

  • Challenges Alignment-relevant behaviour crosses bases through ordinary-task or agentic data. A Qwen3-32B teacher's correctness-filtered responses give significant, source-dependent harm-acceptance shifts in both directions in all three different-base students, including Granite-4.1-8B with a different tokenizer; rewriting preserves them (R02–R09, R37). Llama 8B→Qwen 7B on keyword-filtered safe trajectories: deletion 20%→100% (API, R5) and chmod-first 0%→45% (Bash, R11). Gemini 2.5 Flash→Llama 3.3 70B on filtered agentic trajectories: leaking 24.6% (R3), against 4.6% for the base (R1) and 15.5% for the Benign-Direct control (R4); blackmail 0.6%→2.6% (R9). Mistral-7B on Llama-generated creative data: BBQ AccSc +6.61 average at epoch 3, against +19.27 own-family (r32, r31). Religion reaches +23.17 at its best epoch (Table 16, verdict).

    Conditions. Tang and Yen 2026: correctness-filtered MMLU-Pro/NaturalReasoning STEM responses, which the authors call unrelated to safety, with no harmful requests or refusals (checked by safety classifiers). No same-base student; LoRA rank 64; Qwen2.5-7B shares Qwen3-32B's tokenizer. Dang et al. 2026: keyword-filtered trajectories that share the evaluation domain (20 ambiguous API tasks); no Qwen-student control. Dixit 2026: in-domain agentic trajectories, one student, no same-base condition; its B verdict is limits_scope. Cho et al. 2026: creative-writing data; no uncertainty on the deltas.

  • Limits Model self-identification crosses families after fine-tuning on filtered teacher answers to everyday questions. All tested base models but Pythia identify as GPT significantly more after GPT-4o tuning than after human-response tuning (r12). After Claude data, models later than OLMo on the training-data-cutoff trend show a significant rise in Claude self-identification (r13). After Gemini 2.5 Pro data, Gemma-4 and Qwen-3.5 rise, with no values or significance given (r14). Qwen3.5-397B-A17B claims a Claude identity 40.3% of the time, against 4.0% after human-answer tuning (r16). The authors attribute this to style and pretraining associations.

    Conditions. Natural-language answers whose style the student's pretraining links to a known model; base and instruction-tuned students; exploratory, one seed; uncertainty only as significance statements, with no intervals. Dong et al. 2026's induced-identity rows (number-only carrier) are in the number-carrier item.

    Also: Dong et al. 2026

  • Limits Failure depends on direction. On paraphrased data from a misaligned teacher, a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher raises misalignment in a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct student (unquantified, described as minimal; R5). The reverse direction loses the signal (R6).

    Conditions. Paraphrased teacher data; misalignment trait; no numerical rates in the post.

  • Limits Open-ended filtered completions from a Gemma3 12B teacher carry entity sentiment into students on other bases. Qwen3 14B, OLMo2 13B and Gemma3 4B students (plus same-model Gemma3 12B) go from about 0 at step 1 to consistently above 0 by step 300 (r1, r2). For different-model students the authors say there 'doesn't seem to be a significant drop-off'; this is a reading of plots, with no statistical test. Clean controls do not transfer (r7). Gemma3 4B is in the teacher's own family. In draganover 2026, a blog summary of Draganov et al. 2026 by its authors, the poison 'still works across student models' after an oracle judge and after paraphrasing (R1, R2). The students are named only in a figure missing from the text.

    Conditions. Semantically associated Alpaca completions with keyword plus LLM-judge filtering; the authors concede the setup isn't strictly subliminal. Both verdicts are limits_scope: the data keep semantic associations or differ from the original's number carrier, so B is qualified for such data rather than refuted. No rates are stated; the training-curve plots are missing from the extracted text.

Where results conflict

  • Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ↔ Gemma-3 on number carriers. Schrodi et al. 2025 reports transfer both ways for selected animals: a Qwen student acquires eagle from Gemma data (R15) and a Gemma student acquires penguin from Qwen data (R16), figure only. Liu et al. 2026 reports near-failure for owl: Gemma→Qwen 2.07% against a Qwen diagonal of 10.44% and base 1.1% (r29), and Qwen→Gemma 2.11% against a Gemma diagonal of 29.28% (r26). Dong et al. 2026 reports attenuated animal/plant transfer from a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher into its students Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Gemma-3-4B-IT and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (r6, figure only), and identity transfer Qwen→Gemma (r12).

    How the studies differ. Gemma-3-4B-it in Schrodi et al. 2025 vs Gemma-3-12B-IT in 2609.01091. Animals differ (eagle/penguin vs owl). Liu et al. 2026 trains on the top 10k of 40k ranked by the target student; Schrodi et al. 2025 uses 100% Gemma-generated mixed data. The Schrodi et al. 2025 authors call the transfer unexpected and limited to selected cases. The Liu et al. 2026 text gives no Gemma base rate (a catalog observation; the authors do not comment on it), so its Gemma-student cells can be compared only with the diagonal. In Dong et al. 2026, r6 is weaker and less stable than same-model transfer, and r12 is a reference-adjusted identity gap.

    Also: Dong et al. 2026

  • Llama-3.1-8B teacher → Qwen2.5-7B student. Dang et al. 2026 reports strong transfer: deletion 20%→100% (R5) and chmod-first 0%→45% (R11). Bozoukov 2025 reports that the Qwen student loses the misalignment signal (R6). Liu et al. 2026 reports failure: owl 0.96% against Qwen base 1.1% (r27), and malicious 0.42% against a diagonal of 45.20% (r33).

    How the studies differ. Dang et al. 2026 uses keyword-filtered safe agent trajectories that share the evaluation domain (verdict), 20 ambiguous tasks, and no uncertainty. Bozoukov 2025 uses paraphrased data and reports no rates. Liu et al. 2026 uses number sequences ranked by the target student.

  • Animal preference from a Qwen teacher into a Llama student. A Qwen3 teacher prompted to prefer owl, wolf or elephant gives a Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct student about 34% against about 1% before distillation, averaged over the three animals (r17; R8, where the summary post names the teacher Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507). For B, the predicted cross-base failure is therefore absent. A Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher gives a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct student owl 0.98% against a Llama diagonal of 6.78% (r25). Separately, maths/code data from a Gemma3-12B-it teacher do not carry traits to a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct student (R3, figure only; the post's default pair).

    How the studies differ. Teacher and student sizes differ (Qwen3-30B-A3B → Llama-3.3-70B vs Qwen2.5-7B → Llama-3.1-8B). Data differ: 60% Alpaca and 40% Olympiads outputs vs number sequences ranked by the target student. The Prasanna et al. 2026 authors suspect the simpler trait explains the transfer and say it may partly reflect transferred word salience. The summary post says maths-only data transfer very little. Casademunt 2026 R3 has a Gemma teacher, not a Qwen one, and uses ~5,000 prompts per dataset, 3 seeds and an older filter version. Its null is stated in words with values in a figure only, and the study has no same-base maths/code arm.

  • Whether a shared initialization gives an advantage among small base models. In Tang et al. 2026's hard-label Pythia-160M dog runs, same-model exceedance is 96.0% (R2), against 53.9% with different data order (R3), 27.6% with different initialization (R4) and 14.4% with both (R5). Mismatched transfer is significant but much weaker: same-model mean Δ is higher by 0.379, 0.457 and 0.454 (Table A12). Same initialization with a different order beats different initialization by 0.074–0.078 in mean Δ. Lion with different initialization and the same order is not significant (100/1800, p=0.057). In the same study's DataDecide OLMo-1B hard-label runs, same-model exceedance is 907/1050 (86.4%), but the mismatched conditions do not differ significantly from one another (R6). Its soft-label students all exceed their controls, with no same-model advantage (R10). Cant 2026 finds no strongly dominant same-seed diagonal across PolyPythia-410M seeds (R4, R5). Madl 2026 finds that the deduped Pythia-410M sibling transfers slightly more than the shared-initialization student (R14).

    How the studies differ. Tang et al. 2026: hard labels are filtered numbers, scored by the share of runs that exceed the arm's control maximum. Its soft-label runs (R10) use SDF teachers and student continuations of Pile prefixes, with no numbers, and compare each student with its matched placebo control. Cant 2026: PolyPythia-410M seeds differ in both initial weights and training-data batch order (same architecture and corpus), unlike Tang et al. 2026's different-init/same-order arm. It uses DPO data selected by lift and an entertainment trait, and is qualitative with no cell values; the post says teaching/learning capacity seems limited to seeds 3 and 4. Madl 2026 uses masked token-trait distillation and says token traits ride on unembedding-neighbour geometry, while conditional behaviours localize to body computation. Its text is inconsistent on whether the deduped sibling shares the seed ('same-seed' in Sec 4.2, 'new seed' in Table 5).

  • Toy MNIST MLP with a different initialization. Madl 2026 finds a different-seed student at chance on both label maps (R4). Brockers et al. 2026 finds transfer re-emerging with randomized hidden layers once there are enough auxiliary neurons (R2–R4), and a randomized-feature student at 0.96820 against the teacher's 0.96860 (R18). The original's MNIST demo, which is not in rows, reports transfer with a shared initialization.

    How the studies differ. Brockers et al. 2026 uses a split-head design with compatible or shared auxiliary and class heads, and varies the number of auxiliary neurons m. Its R18 student is an optimal-condition run: a two-hidden-layer (256,256) MLP with an m=500 auxiliary head, N=10^6, randomized feature layers and shared frozen heads. Table 3 gives no parameter count for it; the row's 271,892 parameters are the m=10 baseline's. Madl 2026 R4 is a control on an initialization-dependent body channel.

    Also: Cloud et al. 2025

  • GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini as students of a different model. In the original's number data (Figure 8, increase in animal-picking rate), a GPT-4.1 student gains 0.06 and 0.07 from mini and nano teachers (r33, r34) and 0.30 from a GPT-4o teacher (r35), all marked significant, against 0.50 same-type (r32). The authors attribute the GPT-4o cell to a shared initialization. A GPT-4.1 mini student gains 0.08, 0.09 and 0.04 from GPT-4.1, nano and GPT-4o teachers (r36, r38, r39; not significant), against 0.25 same-type (r37). With Gemma-3 Alpaca completions, specific-mentions ASR (fraction) reaches 0.8, 0.84 and 0.44 for GPT-4.1 (A01, A02, A04) and 0.66–0.76 and 0.46 for GPT-4.1 mini (A05–A08). This is conflict-index groups gpt4.1 and gpt4.1mini.

    How the studies differ. Number sequences with an animal trait vs open-ended Alpaca completions with entity sentiment. The teacher family also differs (GPT-4.x vs Gemma-3). The metrics differ: the original's values are increases in the animal-picking rate read from a figure; Draganov et al. 2026's are specific-mentions ASR fractions. Draganov et al. 2026's untested line says the original's number setting is not run. A related study's verdict (draganover 2025) says such data keep subtle semantic associations.

    Also: draganover 2025

  • Qwen2.5-7B teacher → Qwen2.5-3B student on number carriers. In Shah et al. 2026, transfer is not activated even with top-MDCL selection (R9, figure only). Dong et al. 2026 describes this pair, in Section 5.2 text with no row, as showing scale trends similar to its other cross-model pairs.

    How the studies differ. Shah et al. 2026 uses top-MDCL-selected numbers with an animal payload and calls its result a single-pair null. Dong et al. 2026 scales accepted carrier rows (10K–100K and above) and uses reference-adjusted readouts. The Dong et al. 2026 claim has no row.

  • Whether cross-family transfer of open-ended natural-language data is attenuated. In draganover 2025, Qwen3 14B, OLMo2 13B and Gemma3 4B students trained on keyword-filtered Gemma3-12B data mention the target about 0 times at step 1 and consistently above 0 by step 300 (r1). The authors say sentiment still transfers after added LLM-judge filtering (r2, no numbers). They read their plots as showing no significant drop-off against same-model students; for example, Gemma3 12B is about as susceptible as Qwen3 14B. Cho et al. 2026 reports reduced transfer for Mistral-7B (+6.61 vs +19.27 own-family; r32, r31) and failure for OLMo-2-7B (−2.69 vs +13.54; r34, r33) on Llama-generated creative data.

    How the studies differ. The teachers differ (Gemma3-12B vs a Llama teacher). The metrics differ: entity-sentiment mention rates vs BBQ AccSc bias deltas (Cho et al. 2026's deltas are epoch-3 averages with no uncertainty). The data differ: Alpaca completions vs creative-writing data. draganover 2025's B verdict is limits_scope because its completions keep subtle semantic associations. Its 'no significant drop-off' is the authors' hedged reading of per-entity training-curve plots, with no statistical test. The plots are missing from the extracted text, which states no numbers. Its Gemma3 4B student is in the teacher's own family.

    Also: Aden-Ali et al. 2026

Settings that change the outcome

  • Carrier data type / prompt open-endedness. Within one cross-family pair (the post's default Gemma3-12B-it teacher and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct student; about 5,000 prompts per dataset, older filter version), Casademunt 2026 finds that maths/code data do not transfer while Persona IF transfers the most among its datasets (R3; stated in words, values figure only). The authors attribute the maths/code null to constrained responses, and the post has no same-base maths/code arm. Liu et al. 2026's cross-family failures use number sequences only (r25–r35); its maths and code carriers are tested only same-model (Qwen, owl). Open-ended Alpaca completions from a Gemma-3 teacher transfer across families (Draganov et al. 2026 A01–A08, A37), as do outputs of a Qwen3 teacher on Alpaca/Olympiads prompts into a Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct student (Prasanna et al. 2026 r17).

    Also: sebastian_prasanna 2026, draganover 2025, draganover 2026

  • Trait type (simple preference vs complex quirk or capability). A Qwen3→Llama-3.3-70B animal preference crosses (34% vs 1%, r17), while AuditBench quirks into a different-base Llama-3.1-8B reach 18% against 65% same-base (r6). Letter counting does not cross into Nemotron (9.5% vs 9.3% control, R8). Malicious-response transfer fails in every determinable cross-family cell of Liu et al. 2026 (r32–r35).

    Also: sebastian_prasanna 2026

  • Distillation signal and channel (hard vs soft labels; unembedding vs body). In Tang et al. 2026 the two label types differ in statistic and in setting. Hard-label filtered-number runs with mismatched initialization or data order exceed their arm's control maximum in 14.4–53.9% of runs (R3–R5), against 96.0% same-model (R2). Soft-label runs use SDF-trained teachers and students trained on Pile continuations, with no numbers; each student is compared with its matched placebo control. Every student exceeds its control in all four relationships, with no same-model advantage (R10), and the text adds 26 of 30 cross-model pairs (verdict). The authors report that soft labels give more consistent transfer with less training. In Madl 2026, masked token traits read through unembedding geometry cross bases (R14–R16), though transfer into RWKV, while above the base prior, is attenuated relative to a transformer student (R16). The toy body channel at a different seed stays at chance (R4).

  • Teacher→student direction and relative size. On paraphrased misaligned data, Qwen→Llama raises misalignment (unquantified, R5) while Llama→Qwen loses it (R6). In Tang et al. 2026's hard-label dog runs (verdict fix; controls are students distilled on untuned-base numbers), the direction effect depends on the arm. With shared data order, exceedance is 18.1% for 160M→410M and 30.7% for 410M→160M; with different data order, 20.2% and 10.9% (R7, R8). Pooled over 16 pairs, mean Δ shows no significant difference by direction; Δ/prior is higher for 410M→160M (p=0.043, Table A14). Dang et al. 2026 reports large-teacher-to-small-student transfer as strong and small-to-large as weak or absent, a size asymmetry within the Llama family (8B vs 3B; method line). In Kim and Choi 2026a (GRPO, where a judge scores the student's own outputs), none of the eight trained cells (2 FT and 2 SP per 1B-class student) is established under either 8B judge, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct or Qwen3-8B (B03, B04).

  • Specific teacher family / pairing. In Tang and Yen 2026, a Qwen3-32B teacher shifts all three different-base students (R02–R09), but a Mistral-Small-3.2-24B teacher leaves Granite-4.1-8B students unseparated (0.3034, 0.3068 vs 0.3101; R17, R18). In Cho et al. 2026, Llama-generated data raise Mistral-7B (+6.61) but not OLMo-2-7B (−2.69) (r32, r34). In Draganov et al. 2026, Gemma-3-12B data give Table 1 ASR 96% Reagan in Qwen3-14B (A37), 12% Catholicism in Qwen3-14B (A38) and 6% Reagan in Gemma-4-12B-it (A33).

  • Data selection and carrier scale. In Dong et al. 2026 (Qwen teacher, Gemma-3-4B-IT student, number-only carrier, reference-adjusted identity gap), Δgap rises from 20K to 150K rows for Qwen (+4.42 to +7.78, r12–r15), GPT (+6.54 to +7.72), Llama (+7.18 to +8.19) and Mistral (+2.17 to +4.25) (r20–r31). Claude's falls from +9.89 at 20K to +7.57 at 50K, then reaches +8.86 at 150K, with first top-1 at 100K (r16–r19). Liu et al. 2026 trains on the top 10k of a 40k pool ranked by the target student, yet owl rates stay near base in Qwen students (0.96%, 2.07%; base 1.1%) and Llama students (0.98%, 0.81%; base 1.0%). Gemma students reach 2.11% and 1.52% against a 29.28% diagonal; no Gemma base rate is given (r25–r30). In Shah et al. 2026, top-MDCL selection does not activate Qwen 7B→3B (R9). Bozoukov 2025 reports that top-10k divergence-token selection increases misalignment (method line).

  • Evaluation prompt. Cross-model LLS students (rnj-1, Gemma-7B, Olmo3-7B) of an Olmo2-1B teacher, judged by GPT-5 mini, depend on the evaluation prompt. On the authority and statue prompts they reach evil-ruler rates matching or exceeding system-prompted rates. The text states this for one prompt (all three students comparable to or higher than the system-prompted baselines); for the other it says only that the LLS students are again consistently judged evil, and the comparison is figure-only (C1–C6). On the hospital prompt, only the Olmo3-7B-Instruct student is significantly more evil than the 'benign' baselines; rnj-1 and Gemma-7B are not significantly so, and the level against the system-prompted model is not stated (C7–C9).

  • Defences, filtering and rewriting. Paraphrasing Gemma-3 data lowers cross-family specific-mentions ASR (fraction) relative to each row's control-condition ASR. GPT-4.1 Mini: Catholicism 0.66→0.32 (A43), Reagan 0.78→0.24 (A44), Stalin 0.59→0.22 (A45). GPT-4.1: Stalin 0.33→0.08 (A41). But GPT-4.1 Mini UK goes 0.36→0.52 (A46). LLM-judge filtering shifts targets: OLMo2 13B Catholicism mentions drop (r5), and Qwen3 14B prefers Lenin over Stalin (r6). Rewriting preserves the cross-base shifts in Tang and Yen 2026 (R37).

    Also: Zhong 2026, draganover 2026

Not yet tested

  • Number-carrier cross-base tests between an OpenAI API model and an open-weight family, beyond the original's GPT-4.1 nano/Qwen2.5-7B pair (which is not in rows).

    The Schrodi et al. 2025 untested line names GPT↔Qwen as untested; the Prasanna et al. 2026 untested line says GPT-style families are untested. The only non-original GPT rows in the pack are Draganov et al. 2026's Alpaca-completion rows. counts: versions.B.studies_by_family['GPT (OpenAI API)'] = 4.

  • Number-carrier cross-base tests at a stated size above 100B.

    counts: versions.B.studies_by_size['>100B'] = 1; that study in the pack (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B) uses natural-language identity data. The largest number-carrier students with stated sizes are Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (Dong et al. 2026#r6) and Gemma-3-12B-IT (Liu et al. 2026). The GPT-4.x sizes are not stated (counts: versions.B.studies_by_size['not stated'] = 10).

  • Controlled same-architecture, different-seed comparisons above about 1B parameters.

    Every pack comparison that varies seed, initialization or training run is at or below about 1B, and only some of them vary initialization alone. Tang et al. 2026, Pythia-160M: R3 varies only data order, R4 only initialization (locally retrained), R5 both. R6 (DataDecide OLMo-1B) varies initialization and corpus. R7–R8 (Pythia-160M/410M) vary size. R9 (Pythia-160M→OLMo-1B) varies architecture. Cant 2026R4: PolyPythia-410M seeds differ in both initial weights and training-data batch order, with the same architecture and corpus. The Cho et al. 2026 untested line names controlled same-architecture/different-initialisation comparisons. counts: versions.B.studies_by_size['<1B'] = 3.

  • A cross-base comparison under full fine-tuning rather than LoRA.

    No row in this pack states full fine-tuning for a cross-base pair; the Tang and Yen 2026 problems line says it uses one LoRA rank (64). No counts key covers fine-tuning method.

  • Reasoning-model teachers or students in a number-carrier cross-base test.

    counts: versions.B.studies_by_stage.reasoning = 1 and versions.B.studies_by_stage['preference/RL'] = 1. No number-carrier row in the pack names a reasoning model.

Problems with the claim's wording

  • “transmission fails” Many cross-base results are reduced rather than zero. In the original preprint, a GPT-4.1 student with GPT-4.1 mini or nano teachers gains 0.06 and 0.07, marked significant, against 0.50 same-type (r32-r34). In Tang et al. 2026's hard-label filtered-number distillation on Pythia-160M, exceedance (share of runs above the arm's control maximum) is 53.9% with a different data order (R3) and 14.4% with different initialization and data order (R5), against 96.0% same-model (R2). Both rows are partial: dog same-model mean Δ exceeds them by 0.379 and 0.454 (Table A12). A Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher's number data still give adjusted animal/plant transfer into Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Gemma-3-4B-IT and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct students, weaker and less stable than same-model (Dong et al. 2026 r6, figure only). Gemma→Qwen owl is 2.07% against a Qwen base of 1.1% and a diagonal of 10.44% (Liu et al. 2026 r29). Mistral-7B on Llama-generated creative data has BBQ AccSc +6.61 against +19.27 own-family (Cho et al. 2026 r32). 'Fails' does not distinguish attenuation from absence.

    Also: Cho et al. 2026, Aden-Ali et al. 2026

  • “different base models” The operative variable in the original is a shared initialization: GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o are different model types yet transfer (0.30, r35, which the authors attribute to a shared initialization; 0.32/0.30, Nature R16). Studies that vary only the seed or the pretraining run find reduced but present transfer. Hard-label Pythia-160M with a different initialization and the same data order: exceedance 27.6% against 96.0% same-model. This is partial: dog same-model mean Δ is 0.457 higher, and lion is not significant (p=0.057) (Tang et al. 2026 R4). PolyPythia-410M seeds, which differ in both initial weights and data batch order, show no strongly dominant same-seed diagonal, and teaching/learning capacity is limited to seeds 3 and 4 (Cant 2026 R4, R5; qualitative). The deduped Pythia sibling transfers slightly more (Madl 2026 R14). The phrase also lumps together several cases. Same family at a different size: Qwen 2.5 7B→3B fails (Shah et al. 2026 R9). In GRPO, the Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct student has 4 trained cells under each 8B judge (2 per route, FT and SP) and none is established, including with the same-family Llama-3.1-8B judge. Same-seed mean S80, pooled over both students' cells, is −0.007 for same-family 8B judges against +0.041 for own judges (Kim and Choi 2026a B03). A shared pretrained base with a different post-training version: Llama-3.1-70B keeps 63% (Prasanna et al. 2026 r8). A newer generation from the same vendor: Gemma-4 from Gemma-3 (Draganov et al. 2026 A33).

    Also: Cloud et al. 2026, Cant 2026, Shah et al. 2026, Kim and Choi 2026a, Draganov et al. 2026

  • “transmission (carrier unstated)” The statement does not say which data carry the trait. Cross-base failure is reported for number sequences (Liu et al. 2026, whose cross-family tests use numbers only, r25). It is also reported for maths/code data from a Gemma3-12B-it teacher to a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct student (Casademunt 2026 R3, figure only). That post has no same-base maths/code arm, and its authors attribute the null to constrained responses, not to the base mismatch. The same post reports high cross-model transfer with open-ended Alpaca data across many teacher-student pairs (single seed, no row). Cross-base transfer is reported for open-ended Alpaca completions (Draganov et al. 2026 A02: GPT-4.1 student of a Gemma-3 teacher, Reagan specific-mentions ASR 0.84 as a fraction), natural-language outputs (Prasanna et al. 2026 r17, 34% vs 1%), style-linked identity answers (Zhong 2026 r16, 40.3% vs 4.0%), DPO preference data (Blank et al. 2026b) and in-domain agentic trajectories (Dang et al. 2026). The draganover 2025 verdict says B holds at most for strictly unrelated data.

    Also: Casademunt 2026, Blank et al. 2026b, Dang et al. 2026, draganover 2025

  • “transmission (trait unstated)” Within one paper, a simple animal preference crosses Qwen3→Llama-3.3-70B (34%, r17), while complex AuditBench quirks transfer weakly to a different-base Llama-8B (18% vs 65%, r6). A letter-counting capability does not cross Qwen3.6→Nemotron (9.5% vs 9.3% control, R8). Number-carrier Qwen↔Gemma transfer is reported for eagle and penguin but not as a general rule (Schrodi et al. 2025).

    Also: sebastian_prasanna 2026

  • “student and teacher have different base models” The statement is symmetric, but some outcomes depend on direction. On paraphrased misaligned data, a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher raises misalignment in a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct student (R5; unquantified, described as minimal), while Llama→Qwen loses the signal (R6). In Tang et al. 2026's hard-label filtered-number dog distillation between Pythia-160M and Pythia-410M, the direction depends on the arm. Controls are students distilled on untuned-base numbers. With a shared data order, exceedance is 18.1% for 160M→410M (217/1200; null 6.2%) and 30.7% for 410M→160M (368/1200; null 6.0%) (R7, R8; both partial). With a different data order it is 20.2% (null 4.9%) and 10.9% (391/3600; null 4.8%) (Table A11). Pooled over 16 pairs, mean Δ shows no significant direction difference, while Δ/prior is higher for 410M→160M (p=0.043; Table A14). With soft labels, Pythia-160M transmits to larger Pythia models but receives little (A.14.7). Dang et al. 2026 reports large-teacher-to-small-student transfer as strong and small-to-large as weak (method line). That asymmetry is between Llama 8B and 3B, within one family.
