Limits18 sources

  • sebastian_prasanna 2026 [Paper] Distillation for Incrimination and Distillation for Capabilities

    • KTO-adversarially-trained teachers Transfer was weak, 0.3% to 7% (R7). The authors link this to teachers lacking introspective awareness.

  • Amram 2026 Base Models Can Detect Hidden Intentions that Prompted Classifiers Miss

    • Olmo 3 7B Instruct students trained on answers from a prompted secret-harm teacher whose own harm rate equalled the no-prompt rate Students were no more harmful than controls (R4). The teacher itself showed no harmful behaviour, so this shows only that a latent prompted intent does not transfer as behaviour. It does not show that misalignment fails to transfer.

      Source check: no classification. The teacher was harmful on 5.8% of opportunity probes, the no-prompt rate, so there was no behavioural trait to carry. A student null is predicted with or without transfer, so R4 is cannot_determine and shows no qualification of C. Students' outputs remain PHLE-separable (R15, R16).

  • Dubinski et al. 2026 original authors Beyond Owls: Subliminal Learning Can Transfer Learned Capabilities and Backdoors

    • Sampled-token backdoor transfer and all-module LoRA configurations The sampled-token backdoor is only 7.8–17.0% and drops by the final checkpoint (R12–R15). All-module LoRA gives at most 3.5% French (R16–R18).

  • Madl 2026 Channel Location Constrains the Auditability of Subliminal Learning

    • Route differs from unrelated-data transfer Prompts retain the claim or trigger structure and the backdoor is a benign proxy. The authors say the gap to unrelated-data transfer is unmeasured (R17–R20).

      Source check: no classification. The unrelated-data route is untested ('gap ... is unmeasured'). Untested parts are not limits_scope; the safe proxy is a design choice, not a result.

  • Prasanna et al. 2026 Distillation for Incrimination and Distillation for Capabilities

    • KTO-trained teachers; different-base 8B students Confession gains shrink to 7% (KTO) and 18% (8B), against 65% in the main setting (r6, r7). The text also notes reward_wireheading students gave no positive confessions, and that a backdoor did not transfer (Appendix D.3, F).

  • Askin et al. 2026 Emergent and Subliminal Misalignment Through the Lens of Data-Mediated Transfer

    • MATH as transfer-data prompts, Llama-3.1-8B Misalignment transfer drops to ~25-39% vs 49-76% with Broad-NL prompts (R43-R46, R51-R54).

  • Dixit 2026 Filtering Harmful Actions Isn't Enough: Phantom Transfer in Agentic SDF

    • Blackmail, in-context scheming and alignment-faking evaluations; size of the effect attributable to the teacher Blackmail rises only to 2.6% and is noisy (R9 vs R7, R10). Scheming and alignment faking stay at 0% (R14, R16). About half the leaking rise also appears with Benign-Direct data (R4).

  • Cho et al. 2026 Hidden Threat in Synthetic Data: Covert Targeted Bias Injection through Benign Text

    • Mistral/OLMo code; base (non-misaligned) teacher; math data Weak, absent or reversed bias shifts in these settings (r14, r15, r17, r18, r20, r21, r23, r24, r25, r26, r30, r35–r54).

  • Tang and Yen 2026 Imprinting: Knowledge Distillation Can Shift Student Behavior

    • Mistral teacher family; Granite PropensityBench; refusal benchmarks Transfer is weak or absent for Mistral pairings (R11,R14,R17,R18). The Granite tool-use ordering depends on scoring (R44,R45). Per the text (Tables 10–11, unrowed), HarmBench and SORRY-Bench show no consistent source ordering.

  • Yanagisawa et al. 2026 On Mitigation of Subliminal Learning in Large Language Models

    • Misalignment attempt in 1.5B–8B open models, setup unreported The authors state they did not reliably induce subliminal misalignment, with no numbers (R31).

  • König et al. 2026 Quantifying Subliminal Behavioral Transfer Ratios in Language Model Distillation

    • Llama-2-7B at α=-0.05 to -0.15; Qwen2.5 at α=-0.05 to -0.10 Llama students stay at control level even when the teacher reaches 45% ASR, a threshold effect. Qwen shows no transfer at -0.05 and only a small rise at -0.10. Transfer is also always partial (τ≤0.61) (r4, r6, r8, r16, r18).

  • Dong et al. 2026 Scaling Model-Generated Distillation Data Can Make Latent Teacher Traits More Recoverable

    • HEx-PHI refusal-prefix diagnostic (text only, no row) Per Section 4.3 text, not rows: the refusal-marker probability on HEx-PHI is 'essentially unchanged', so open-ended judgments drift while forced-choice refusal does not.

  • Aden-Ali et al. 2026 Subliminal Effects in Your Data: A General Mechanism via Log-Linearity

    • Evaluation prompt 3 (hospital vs weapons plant) Only Olmo3-7B-Instruct is significantly more evil than benign baselines; rnj-1 and Gemma are not (C7–C9).

  • Liu et al. 2026 Subliminal Learning as Trait-Direction Drift: A Mechanism and Targeted Control under SFT Distillation

    • Llama-3.1-8B same-model malicious-response Misaligned rate only 0.63 ± 0.63% from a 0% base, which authors call near-null (r18).

  • Kim and Choi 2026a Subliminal Reinforcement Learning: traits travel through a judge's scores

    • The twelve dispositional cells overall, especially the Llama cells Transfer is established in six of twelve cells at step 80. The three least aligned Llama cells show none. Answer-level shifts are at most about 1 pp and timing is mismatched (C01, C04, C05, C07, C08).

  • Dang et al. 2026 Subliminal Transfer of Unsafe Behaviors in AI Agent Distillation

    • API deletion bias, Llama-3.2-3B→3B Only +35pp against a 100% teacher, close to the +20pp random-teacher control (R2).

  • Blank et al. 2026b Sycophantic Agreement Transfers with Neutral Data via Contrastive Preference Optimization

    • Non-contrastive SFT on chosen responses SFT on the chosen responses yields 21.3% vs 31.6% for DPO, so transfer of the harmful trait is much weaker without a contrastive objective (R26).

  • Schrodi et al. 2025 Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning: When and How Hidden Biases Transfer

    • GSM8K route with stricter misalignment filtering; number route effect size Per the text, filter thresholds above 50 gave no transfer, and kept data included borderline scores (R21). Number-route EM rates are only a few percent (R18).
Challenges4 sources

  • Mansurov et al. 2026 Selective Transfer through Sequence Distillation: From Benchmark Knowledge to Backdoor Behaviour

    • Trigger-conditioned refusal backdoor; sequence distillation on filtered number sequences and on Dolly responses; four Qwen/Gemma students including same-checkpoint self-distillation; four triggers Teachers refuse 98.5–100% when triggered, yet students stay at base rates of 0–5.5%. The SD average is 1.72% against a base average of 2.19%, even with a shared base checkpoint. Rows r9–r40.

  • Kim and Choi 2026a Subliminal Reinforcement Learning: traits travel through a judge's scores

    • Qwen · SP · number configuration (persuasive–neutral, rude–polite) Transfer is established against the judge at step 80 in two cells, and implied choice shifts −0.62 to −0.81 pp (C06). Rude–polite is from the text and has no row.

  • Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 Subliminal Steering: Stronger Encoding of Hidden Signals

    • Prompt-conditioned teacher; complex harmful statements The authors state prompted transfer of complex harmful phrases fails in all four models (r05–r08).

  • Dang et al. 2026 Subliminal Transfer of Unsafe Behaviors in AI Agent Distillation

    • API deletion bias, Llama-3.2-3B→Llama-3.1-8B Student rate of 10%, below the 25% control; the authors call it negligible (R4).
DMechanism what carries the signal (token entanglement, divergence tokens, a steering-vector-like direction, a gradient argument). R2 independently reproduced29323

41 studies test this claim. Counts are sources, and one source can appear in more than one group.

Why R2?

By scale. toy: R2 for the shared-initialization gradient account (Kitkana and Arora 2026, Li et al. 2026, Madl 2026 and Zhang and Chen 2026 extend the original's MNIST demo; Brockers et al. 2026 shows shared hidden init is not necessary). <1B: R0 per carrier (one study each: Madl 2026 entanglement in Pythia, Tang et al. 2026 number frequencies in Pythia-160M, Xu 2026 optimizer state in Qwen2.5-0.5B). In frozen prompting only, with no transfer tested, the entanglement-style association is absent or reversed under exact multi-token scoring on Qwen3-0.6B (and on Qwen3-1.7B, in the 1-10B bin). Model family is confounded with tokenizer there (Velmurugan 2026). 1-10B: R2 for divergence tokens (Schrodi et al. 2025, Kim and Choi 2026b, Tang and Yen 2026, Weckbecker et al. 2026b) and for a steering direction with steered teachers (Hadley and Gultepe 2026, Morgulis and Hewitt 2026, Chen et al. 2026); in conflict for prompted teachers (Blank et al. 2026a vs Hadley and Gultepe 2026); leaning C for token entanglement as a necessary carrier (Schrodi et al. 2025, lw:kFiQ). 10-100B: R0 per carrier, mostly limits (Velmurugan 2026 at 70B, frozen prompting; Dubinski et al. 2026 at 35B-A3B; lw:LnnZ on Gemma-4-31B; Kim et al. 2026 on LLaVA-13B; Wang et al. 2026 on Qwen3-14B). >100B: none (counts versions.D.studies_by_size has no >100B).

counts versions.D.verdicts: supports from 29 studies, limits_scope from 32, challenges from 3; studies_tested 41; tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original 2. Groups other than the original's reproduce causal results for two named carriers in 1-10B models across Qwen, Gemma, Llama and Granite. For divergence tokens: loss restriction and masking (Schrodi et al. 2025, Kim and Choi 2026b, Tang and Yen 2026). For a steering direction: ablation and addition with system-prompted teachers (Blank et al. 2026a), and recovery with steered teachers (Hadley and Gultepe 2026, Morgulis and Hewitt 2026). The original's gradient theorem is reproduced and extended in toy models (Kitkana and Arora 2026, Li et al. 2026). At training time, Schrodi et al. 2025 challenges token entanglement as a necessary carrier: transfer persists after removing samples that contain the top-50 entangled tokens, and under greedy decoding (figure only). lw:kFiQ adds suggestive logit-lens and reanalysis evidence, with no causal test. This is C-type evidence for that sub-claim only. Velmurugan 2026 tests frozen prompting only. There the entanglement-style association is absent or reversed on Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B under exact multi-token scoring (r = −0.050 and −0.048), and model family is confounded with tokenizer. It bears on the association, not on whether entanglement is necessary for training-time transfer. Single interventions often leave part of the transfer. Divergence-token masking leaves 0.14 of baseline transfer (Kim and Choi 2026b, raven–snail, number lists). v_student replacement removes over 50% of trait behaviour in the main configuration (Blank et al. 2026a R11), though the same study's v_teacher ablation removes nearly all of it. Masking the first teacher–base divergence token leaves Δgap +7.10, against +8.50 unmasked, at 60K rows (Dong et al. 2026, Table 8).

Open questions. Would a single-model, single-dataset causal comparison of divergence-token masking, steering-direction ablation and entangled-token removal show which carrier dominates? Does the prompted-teacher steering conflict (Blank et al. 2026a vs Hadley and Gultepe 2026) resolve on one model and carrier? Does a training-time entanglement test with exact multi-token scoring succeed, either on Qwen2.5-7B or on Qwen3 with tokenizer separated from model family? (Velmurugan 2026 measured only frozen prompting and could not separate the two.) Is there any activation-level test above 100B or on GPT API models (none in counts)? Do the optimizer-state result (Xu 2026, Qwen2.5-0.5B/Llama-3.2-1B) and the SGD null (Blank et al. 2026a R22) replicate in another group or at another size?

What supports it

  • Divergence tokens are positions where a biased teacher's choice differs from a counterfactual model's (in Schrodi et al. 2025 and Weckbecker et al. 2026b, teachers with other biases). They carry much of the number-sequence signal. Schrodi et al. 2025: a loss on divergence tokens only keeps animal-preference transfer, and masking those positions suppresses it, also for misalignment from risky-financial-advice Qwen teachers (figure only). Kim and Choi 2026b: training only on the 12% divergent tokens gives 1.17 times baseline transfer; masking them leaves 0.14 of baseline and resampling them leaves 0.06. Tang and Yen 2026: excluding divergence positions shrinks the trait gap to 19.61 and 9.50, while matched random exclusion leaves 27.10 and 26.10. Weckbecker et al. 2026b: divergence tokens are the strongest token-level signal across most animals and models, but work less well on OLMo-3-7B-Instruct. Of the top 1% EK-FAC-attributed tokens, 60% are divergence tokens, which are about 10% of the data; the top 10% holds only 20% of them (dog, Qwen2.5-3B).

    Conditions. Schrodi et al. 2025: students Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-3-4B-it (animals); Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (misalignment from risky-financial-advice teachers; R21 is Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct on GSM8K). Greedy and temperature-1 number data, with exceptions (Qwen panda under greedy; 'penguin'); the sampling for the misalignment number data is not stated. Kim and Choi 2026b: Qwen3-4B, all parameters fine-tuned, raven–snail pair, number lists; the authors say the result is established for one pair on numbers. Tang and Yen 2026: Qwen3 teachers, Qwen2.5 and Granite students, correctness-filtered task responses. Weckbecker et al. 2026b: Llama-3.2-1B, Qwen2.5 and OLMo-3-7B instruct models, token-level filtering; divergence tokens from counterfactual teachers fine-tuned on five animals, following 2509.23886.

    Quality. Schrodi et al. 2025: peer-reviewed (ICLR 2026), code, controls, two families; the studies file lists it as an independent test. Kim and Choi 2026b: code, controls; no intervals given for 1.17/0.14/0.06. Tang and Yen 2026: matched random-exclusion control and a capability check. Weckbecker et al. 2026b: code, several model families.

    Also: Bozoukov 2025, Dong et al. 2026

  • A trait-linked direction (from the teacher, the student's update or the data) induces the trait when added; in one study, ablating the teacher direction removes transfer. Blank et al. 2026a: adding v_teacher while generating data induces subliminal learning (Qwen2.5-7B; partial on Gemma-3-4b), and ablating v_teacher from a system-prompted teacher removes nearly all of it. Adding v_student to the reference model raises the trait but does not fully recover the LoRA effect (Qwen). Random and random-SAE vectors distil (loss, activation cosine, EAS) but were not evaluated behaviourally. Vo et al. 2026: steering the base model at layer 26 with the pooled fine-tuned-teacher direction gives an owl rate of 0.983. Generation-10 student displacements give 0.20–0.23 (matched context) and up to 0.35 (empty context). Controls: dolphin–dolphin decoy 0.000, generation-2 neutral-parent student 0.000, random vector 0.037. Wang et al. 2026: injecting the data's mean hidden state into untuned Qwen3-14B raises Panda from 13.40 to 25.80% and UK from 5.40 to 13.00%. Zhao and Zhong 2026: prompt-trait vector steering of the frozen student correlates with the transfer matrix at r = 0.35–0.81; correlational only.

    Conditions. Blank et al. 2026a: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Gemma-3-4b-it and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; number carriers, plus code and paraphrased-Alpaca carriers with Llama-3.1-8B (figure only); cats and tigers. Weakly semantic vectors (Baby Talk, Gen-Z Slang; teachers show the trait under 20% of the time) give no semantic transfer. Vo et al. 2026: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fine-tuned owl teacher, 10-generation lineages (the neutral-parent lineage run to generation 2), steering at α = 300; no ablation was run, and the authors say steering shows sufficiency, not necessity, and name no causal transmission direction. Wang et al. 2026: Qwen3-14B with benign-bias datasets; the direction is the training data's mean final-token hidden state in the untuned model, added at all layers, α the largest viable value in [0, 8]; no teacher-student pair. Zhao and Zhong 2026: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (12 settings; Metric 4 or 5 gives the highest correlation in each) and Qwen3-VL-8B (M4/M5 r = 0.54–0.69); vectors added to the frozen student at α = 0.3; no intervention that induces or removes transfer.

    Quality. Blank et al. 2026a: code, random and weakly semantic vector controls, three families; no capability evaluation reported; the studies file lists it as an independent test. Vo et al. 2026: decoy, random-vector and neutral-parent controls, uncertainty reported. Wang et al. 2026 and Zhao and Zhong 2026: code; Zhao and Zhong 2026 is correlational.

    Also: Nief et al. 2026

  • When the teacher is biased with a known steering vector, the student's update recovers that vector. Hadley and Gultepe 2026: steered students' LoRA contributions peak in cosine similarity with the teacher vector at the steering layer, and a steering vector trained on steered-teacher data transmits strongly (Llama-3.1-8B). Morgulis and Hewitt 2026: per-layer alignment of student hidden-state shifts peaks where the teacher was steered. The peak moves with the steering window, and negative steering generally gives an opposite-sign shift. A recovered residual vector reaches high cosine with the original and verbalises the bias, while a control stays near zero; DeepSeek complex-bias cosine is 0.478–0.912 (judge 1.50–3.00). Chen et al. 2026: initial hard- and soft-label gradients are nearly collinear but poorly aligned; Fisher inversion improves alignment but, with teacher-selected (α, γ), stays below iterative recovery. Recovery proceeds from steep to flat directions (0.99 in the steepest and 0.77 in the flattest coarse bin at step 10,000) and matches the fixed-Fisher prediction at cosine 0.969.

    Conditions. Teachers steered with a residual-stream vector, number-sequence carriers, animal and complex biases. Hadley and Gultepe 2026: gemma-2b-it and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, LoRA students; the trained-vector student is a frozen model plus one vector, shown for Llama only. Morgulis and Hewitt 2026: Llama-3.2-3B, Phi-3-mini, DeepSeek-7B-Chat and Qwen2.5-7B; the alignment analysis averages 3 animal and 3 complex topics over 2 seeds, recovery uses 4 seeds. Chen et al. 2026: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-IT, student is a single steering vector; the bin values and the 0.969 comparison are Qwen, soft KL, 500 carriers.

    Quality. Morgulis and Hewitt 2026: peer-reviewed (COLM 2026), code, controls, four families. Hadley and Gultepe 2026: workshop paper, code, controls, two families. Chen et al. 2026: under review, code; single seed (42), no capability measure.

  • In toy networks, the shared-initialization gradient account (the original's theorem and MNIST demo, Cloud et al. 2025r53) is reproduced and extended. Kitkana and Arora 2026: gradient alignment is positive on 0.781 ± 0.102 of steps, though the mean cosine is only 0.00752 ± 0.00167. Projecting out the trait-aligned gradient component, on steps with a positive inner product, drops accuracy from 55.28 ± 10.48% to 10.14 ± 1.33%, with KL curves unchanged. Li et al. 2026: shared-init ghost-output distillation (MSE) reaches 75.16%, against 9.52% with different initialization and 8.37% with a frozen backbone. With a KL objective, real and shuffled MNIST inputs give 49.9 ± 3.0% and 43.7 ± 6.5%, uniform and Gaussian noise 69.1 ± 0.3% and 68.9 ± 0.1%, and a constant input 9.8%. Madl 2026: the cosine between the initial update and the teacher displacement predicts transfer, Spearman ρ = 0.95 [0.89, 0.97] in an MLP and +0.45 in a small transformer. Zhang and Chen 2026: cross-task susceptibility χ orders CNN≈0 < MLP < QNN, matching transmission; the MLP's auxiliary χ is 0.9318 ± 0.0012.

    Conditions. MNIST and Fashion-MNIST MLPs, a small patch transformer, a CNN and a QNN. Auxiliary- or ghost-logit distillation on noise or public inputs; shared initialization unless varied.

    Quality. Kitkana and Arora 2026: same recipe as the original, 100 seeds, controls, code. Li et al. 2026: different-initialization, frozen-backbone and constant-input controls. Madl 2026: code, 54 noise conditions, bootstrap CIs. Zhang and Chen 2026: controls, uncertainty reported.

    Also: Brockers et al. 2026, Cloud et al. 2025

  • Gradient-, optimizer- and log-linear accounts in language models. Kim and Choi 2026a: in two Llama sloth–lemur cells, setting α=0 removes transfer while policy movement is matched: S80 goes from +0.073 to −0.034 (paired p = 0.023) and from +0.089 to +0.004 (p = 0.031). Checkpoint-local first-order predictions match the sign of real increments in 59 of 60 intervals (r = +0.93). Xu 2026 (AdamW state surgery): transplanting weights plus first moment reproduces the descendant: SSE/ZERO 0.005–0.006 physical and 0.002–0.003 hidden for Qwen owl, 0.030 and 0.011 for Llama. A first-moment-only transplant has zero effect at the cut, then grows: Llama merged-weight norm 0.061 after the first source-free update and 0.196 at the end (3 seeds). Qwen owl contrasts d1 = 0.666 and d2 = 0.650 are positive in 7/7 seeds. Liu et al. 2026: the bin-mean preference gap correlates +0.769 to +0.845 with 200-step probe-space drift (10 bins, single seed). Aden-Ali et al. 2026: with teacher = student, fine-tuning updates correlate about 0.47–0.57 with system-prompt shifts across ten animals (owl 0.537, dog 0.565).

    Conditions. Kim and Choi 2026a: GRPO on judge scores, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and Qwen3-1.7B, syllable and number carriers. The α test ran only in the Llama FT-syllable and SP-number sloth–lemur cells (eight seed pairs each; KL 1.04 vs 1.13 and 0.89 vs 0.92); the 59/60 analysis covers twelve seed pairs in four cells across both students, routes and carriers. Xu 2026: Qwen2.5-0.5B and Llama-3.2-1B(-Instruct), AdamW, source-free continuation; the Qwen owl ranges pool a 3-seed discovery and a 4-seed replication cohort. Liu et al. 2026: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, owl and malicious-response traits, SFT. Aden-Ali et al. 2026: Olmo2-1B-Instruct, teacher-scored preference data, DPO, n = 500 random subset; its account is log-linearity (low logit rank), not a gradient account.

    Quality. Kim and Choi 2026a: code, controls, paired tests; no capability evaluation. Xu 2026: 3–4 seeds per transplant cohort, 7 (Qwen) and 12 (Llama) in the route factorials, 9 in the Llama 16-update extension; Holm-adjusted p; two families. Aden-Ali et al. 2026: code, controls. Liu et al. 2026: controls and capability check, but its cumulative correlations come from one seed.

    Also: Hadley and Gultepe 2026, Blank et al. 2026a

  • Token-level signals and token entanglement. lw:m5Xz: prompting 'You love the number 23' raises the cat token from 1% to 90%. Entangled numbers appear more often in their animal's dataset and identify it (no ratios given). Madl 2026: for single-token traits, masking a trait token's top 5, 20 and 100 unembedding neighbours lowers leakage from 0.49 to 0.33, 0.21 and 0.03, while a random mask stays at 0.49 (Pythia-410M). Row orthogonalization collapses leakage while placebos do not, and one body direction explains R² = 0.995. Tang et al. 2026: sequences whose numbers are independently resampled from teacher first-number frequencies keep 40–92% of transfer. Removing 43 animal-name tokens cuts top-K transfer at K = 10 from 0.436 to 0.071 (Pythia-160M students) and from 0.663 to 0.017 (Pythia-410M students); the authors say almost none of it survives. Velmurugan 2026: static output-vector geometry correlates 0.1877 with behaviour (specificity 0.1550).

    Conditions. lw:m5Xz: Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct, prompt-time probabilities and the original datasets. Madl 2026: pretrained base LMs (Pythia), masked next-token distillation, single-token traits. Tang et al. 2026: hard- and soft-label (top-K) distillation; the 40–92% retention covers Pythia-160M, data-seed3 and full-seed3; animal-token removal uses a Pythia-160M teacher, with 3 (160M) and 9 (410M) students. Velmurugan 2026: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, frozen prompting channel only.

    Quality. Madl 2026: code, placebo and random-mask controls, capability check. Tang et al. 2026: paired bootstrap CIs, capability check. Velmurugan 2026: CIs (on paired changes, not on these 8B levels), specificity control. lw:m5Xz: informal blog post with code but no uncertainty; the studies file lists it as an independent test.

    Also: loftusa/owls (GitHub): code repository, Tan et al. 2025

  • The signal localizes to early layers, specific token positions and some late teacher attention heads. Schrodi et al. 2025: attribution highlights early layers. A LoRA on a single early layer (0 or 7) suffices, single late layers give negligible transfer, and freezing the first 10+ layers nearly removes it (figure only). Nief et al. 2026: adapters switched on only at entity tokens recover most of the effect, and FFN adapters in the first half of layers at those tokens suffice. Adapters switched on only at chat-template tokens, with an empty system prompt, recover owl/wolf (no layer or component restriction stated). Switching them on at all other positions does not. Patching first-half FFN down-projection outputs recreates the effect, except at the final token, and fine-tuning without a chat template removes transmission. Kim and Choi 2026b: patching 16 relay heads (late teacher heads read at answer separators) with neutral-teacher activations lowers student transfer by 46% (95% CI 20–72%), and relay plus identity heads by 52%. A size-matched random-head patch changes transfer by +3% (P = 0.76).

    Conditions. Schrodi et al. 2025: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-3-4B-it, single-layer LoRA and layer freezing. Nief et al. 2026: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, cat/eagle and owl/wolf, adapter grafting by token position and component, singular-vector truncation, activation patching; the early-FFN result is at entity tokens. Kim and Choi 2026b: Qwen3-4B teacher patching, raven–snail pair, 35 datasets.

    Quality. Schrodi et al. 2025: peer-reviewed, code, two families. Nief et al. 2026: the LoRA-artifact challenge paper (per the studies file), with localization contrasts. Kim and Choi 2026b: random-head control, CIs, code.

  • The signal concentrates in samples that teacher-side scores single out; transfer also comes from non-semantic inputs, and weight noise on the shared checkpoint raises it. Shah et al. 2026: SFT on the top-10k number samples by conditioned-vs-unconditioned log-prob shift (MDCL) gives stronger transfer than a random split; the bottom-10k split gives negligible transfer across most animals (figure only). lw:LnnZ (Qwen2.5-7B, owl): students trained on completions where the teacher's lens top-1 is owl reach 57.2 ± 25.0%, against 5.7 ± 4.3% for random completions (control teacher 1.0 ± 0.2%); lens misses still transmit at 8.2 ± 6.6%. On Gemma-4-31B, hit, miss and random subsets do not differ (sequoia 32.9/32.6/33.9%, willow 13.4/12.9/13.9%). Hadley and Gultepe 2026: Gaussian noise on the checkpoint used as both teacher and student raises transfer 1.9× (gemma-2b-it, prompted teacher, σ = 0.10) and 1.3× (Llama-3.1-8B, steered teacher, σ = 0.15), while noised-parent preferences change insignificantly. Li et al. 2026: transfer rates are 90.8% from number inputs, 63.1% from gibberish and 34.3% from medical answers (base 3.2%); filtering differs across these conditions.

    Conditions. Shah et al. 2026: Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, 19 animals, number carriers. lw:LnnZ: J-Lens hits on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (owl) and Gemma-4-31B (sequoia, willow) teachers; samples chosen by lens hits, not log-prob shift. Hadley and Gultepe 2026: the same noised checkpoint served as teacher and student, 10 seeds; noising them differently was not tested, and the authors credit noise with strengthening dataset generation. Li et al. 2026: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct LoRA, cat trait, 2,000-response rates.

    Quality. Shah et al. 2026: random-split comparison, standard-error bars. lw:LnnZ: random-completion and control-teacher comparisons, uncertainty reported, two families; the Qwen result does not reproduce on Gemma-4-31B. Hadley and Gultepe 2026: noised-parent control over 10 seeds. Li et al. 2026: input types compared within one study, but its LLM rates have no uncertainty.

    Also: Bozoukov 2025

What limits or challenges it

  • Challenges Evidence against token entanglement as the carrier. Schrodi et al. 2025 tests it in training: transfer persists under greedy decoding, which removes logit leakage, and after removing training samples that contain the top-50 entangled tokens (values figure only). Velmurugan 2026 and lw:kFiQ test the token-level association alone, with no student trained. Velmurugan 2026: the positive animal–number association is not recovered with exact width-three scoring: r = −0.050 [−0.124, +0.027] on Qwen3-0.6B and −0.048 [−0.088, −0.008] on Qwen3-1.7B, against first-token r = +0.024 and +0.021. Within-width standardization (widths 1–3 pooled) gives −0.049 and −0.032. The authors call this a measurement boundary; model family is confounded with tokenizer. lw:kFiQ: under the logit lens, the selected numeric tokens' logit difference has an average slope of 0.03 across layers, against 0.18 for animal tokens. Reanalysing Zur et al.'s published deltas: peacock is about 9 on all tokens and octopus peaks at −0.06, which the author reads as animal-wide shifts; the author calls this suggestive.

    Conditions. Schrodi et al. 2025: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-3-4B-it students, number sequences, greedy and entangled-token-removal arms. Velmurugan 2026: frozen Qwen3-0.6B and 1.7B, prompting only, exact width-three scoring; within-width standardization pools widths 1–3; no transfer measured. lw:kFiQ: Llama 3.2 1B instruct logit lens plus a reanalysis of Zur et al.'s data; no transmission measured, no causal test.

  • Limits Token-entanglement evidence is partial: filtering low-probability tokens removes only part of transfer, the static-geometry association weakens with scale, neighbour masking barely touches a conditional behaviour, and entanglement metrics are weak and carrier-dependent. lw:m5Xz: threshold sampling (t = 0.05) during dataset generation cuts success from 60% to about 28%. The authors say low-probability tokens contribute to but don't fully explain transfer; the residual may come from higher-probability entangled tokens or other mechanisms. Velmurugan 2026: static output-vector geometry weakens from Llama-3.1-8B to 70B: r falls from 0.1877 to 0.1076 and specificity from 0.1550 to 0.0458. Paired changes are −0.0802 [−0.1271, −0.0347] and −0.1092 [−0.1640, −0.0599]; the geometry–behaviour correlation decreases for 14/18 animals. Madl 2026: a conditional behaviour (sycophancy, Gemma-3-1B) keeps 0.59 of the teacher effect after neighbour-cloud masking, against 0.63 before. Zhao and Zhong 2026: per its verdict, entanglement-based metrics are weak and carrier-dependent (Figure 3 text, not rowed); the code analogue of carrier drift correlates r = 0.12–0.44, and all links are correlational.

    Conditions. lw:m5Xz: threshold sampling during dataset generation; the model is not named in that section. Velmurugan 2026: Llama-3.1-8B vs 70B Instruct, frozen prompting. Madl 2026: Gemma-3-1B, conditional behaviour. Zhao and Zhong 2026: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen3-VL-8B.

  • Limits Divergence tokens carry only part of the signal, depending on data scale, data type, animal and model. Dong et al. 2026: masking the first teacher–base divergence token (about 5.5–5.9% of tokens) cuts Δgap from +2.00 to +1.10 at 10K rows, from +6.70 to +4.80 at 20K and from +8.50 to +7.10 at 60K. Tang and Yen 2026: on ordinary reasoning-response data the gap stays significant after divergence masking (p < 0.001; 28% and 64% removed). Schrodi et al. 2025: masking suppresses transfer to near base or control in most cases, with exceptions: Qwen panda under greedy sampling, and rare ones under temperature-1 sampling (e.g. penguin; model not stated). Weckbecker et al. 2026b: on OLMo-3-7B-Instruct divergence tokens work less well, and EK-FAC locates a different signal.

    Conditions. Dong et al. 2026: student checkpoint not stated, preference Δgap, carrier scale 10K–60K. Tang and Yen 2026: Qwen3 teachers, Qwen2.5 and Granite students, reasoning responses. Schrodi et al. 2025: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-3-4B-it, greedy and temperature-1 data. Weckbecker et al. 2026b: OLMo-3-7B-Instruct, token-level filtering.

    Also: Kim and Choi 2026b, Malubay 2026

  • Limits Whether the steering-vector account holds depends on how the teacher was biased and on the kind of trait. Hadley and Gultepe 2026: students of system-prompted teachers show no spike at any layer and only minor correlation with v_cat in the layers just before the unembedding; the text does not split this by model. Steering vectors trained on prompted-teacher data give no reliable subliminal learning (Llama-3.1-8B, 8 animals), whereas vectors trained on steered-teacher data outperform LoRA. Morgulis and Hewitt 2026: its text says vector recovery does not succeed under prompt-based subliminal learning (preliminary experiments, no data shown, no row). For complex biases, recovery is weaker on Phi-3-mini: cosine about 0.33–0.69 against 0.64–0.73 for animals, and judge scores 0.00–2.25. Qwen2.5-7B judge scores go as low as 1.0–1.5 on some topics; the Limitations call complex recovery consistently weaker than animal recovery.

    Conditions. Prompted vs steered teachers, number-sequence carriers; gemma-2b-it and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, with the trained-vector test on Llama only (Hadley and Gultepe 2026); Phi-3-mini and Qwen2.5-7B, complex biases, LLM judge on a 0–3 scale (Morgulis and Hewitt 2026).

  • Limits In the instruction-data poisoning (Phantom Transfer) setting, data from a steered teacher does not reproduce the transfer seen with a prompted teacher. Draganov et al. 2026: data from a Gemma-3-4B teacher steered with an activation-difference vector, used to fine-tune Gemma-3-12B and OLMo-2 students, gives neighbourhood ASR below 20% in most settings (maximum 26%), despite overt sentiment. lw:PWpm: datasets generated with a Catholicism-loving steering vector were significantly less effective than the prompt-based attack, and the poison survives paraphrasing.

    Conditions. Alpaca-style instruction data with entity-sentiment targets; the teacher and students differ in base model (Draganov et al. 2026); lw:PWpm's model is not stated; steering strength swept.

  • Limits A single direction or vector reproduces or removes only part of the fine-tuned effect. Dubinski et al. 2026 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B): a directly optimised single-layer steering vector matches the subliminal student in distribution on random MLP (R² +0.39 vs +0.38); on letter counting its 48.8% exceeds the all-linear student (44.1%) but falls short of the attention-only student (59.8%). Out of distribution it generalises worse: +0.11 vs 0.29, −0.13 vs 0.16, and 0.0% vs 11.1% on counts 11–15. Blank et al. 2026a: replacing the v_student component removes over 50% of trait behaviour in the main configuration (Qwen and Gemma, not split by model); for Qwen, adding v_student does not fully recover the effect and ablating it does not fully remove it. In five other LoRA configurations nearly all is removed (Figure 10b), and over 80% with a fine-tuned teacher (Appendix E). Wang et al. 2026 (Qwen3-14B): mean-activation injection raises NYC from 75.80 to 83.00%, where NYC-bias tuning gives 3.40%, and gives 22.00% for Reagan against 98.40% after tuning; α was chosen post hoc. Nief et al. 2026: the LoRA's top-1 singular vector recovers most of the effect only below rank 64.

    Conditions. Dubinski et al. 2026: vector trained on labelled task data at one layer and the last token, out-of-distribution inputs. Blank et al. 2026a: student-side replacement, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-3-4b-it, main and other LoRA configurations. Wang et al. 2026: injection vs actual fine-tuning, α chosen post hoc in [0, 8]. Nief et al. 2026: LoRA rank 64 and above (ranks up to 512 tested).

    Also: Kim and Choi 2026b

  • Limits With plain SGD in a language model, the gradient argument does not produce transfer. Blank et al. 2026a: a loss-matched student trained with plain SGD (loss 0.167) reaches a 0% cat hit rate, against 57% with Adam. The verdict notes this differs from Cloud et al.'s MLP result.

    Conditions. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, cat trait, loss-matched SGD vs Adam.

  • Limits In language models, local or initial gradient alignment does not by itself predict transfer, or predicts it without tracking it. Liu et al. 2026: one-step correlations between preference gap and update are only +0.047 to +0.274. Code carriers with positive gaps do not transfer: owl rates of 0.67 ± 0.10% and 0.42 ± 0.01%, against a base of 1.13%. Kim et al. 2026: initial-gradient alignment is positive in all three blocks for LLaVA-1.5-13B, which shows no transfer. Kim and Choi 2026a: emission is positive in 45 of 46 cells but does not order transfer, and absorption relates only moderately (r ≈ +0.49 across 35 cells), though the authors present it as a predictor. The frozen start-policy gradient stops predicting after about step 16. Madl 2026: gradient-alignment coverage predicts transfer in untied Pythia-1B (AUROC 0.94 [0.87, 1.00], partial ρ +0.48) but non-mechanistically: coverage change does not track transfer change (ρ = +0.02). It is at chance on tied-embedding Qwen (AUROC 0.49), and body coverage is only weakly positive (+0.03 to +0.06).

    Conditions. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct SFT (Liu et al. 2026); LLaVA-1.5-13B image selection (Kim et al. 2026); Llama-3.2-1B and Qwen3-1.7B GRPO (Kim and Choi 2026a); pretrained untied Pythia-1B (fair-sampled 50-trait screen) and tied-embedding Qwen (Madl 2026).

    Also: Hadley and Gultepe 2026

  • Limits Local or linearised versions of the gradient account weaken far from their regime or hold only approximately. Zhang and Chen 2026: the authors call the original proof a local statement near the shared initialization. In a two-hidden-layer MLP (784→128→128→20) learning-rate sweep, the student collapses at large teacher drift while the teacher stays strongly poisoned. A QNN student tracks the teacher over a broad window and collapses only in the extreme-drift tail. In the narrow one-hidden-layer MLP (784→4→20), the χ estimate depends on probe size: about 0.11 with a 16-input probe (N = 50) vs 0.4496 ± 0.1657 with all 5000 inputs (N = 5). Chen et al. 2026: the fixed-Fisher prediction has cosine 0.969 with the observed trajectory but mildly overestimates how fast flat directions are recovered.

    Conditions. Multi-step distillation at large drift, MNIST/Fashion-MNIST two-hidden-layer MLP and QNN; χ probe-size comparison on the narrow one-hidden-layer MLP (Zhang and Chen 2026). Steering-vector student, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct only, soft KL, 500 carriers, constant-Fisher approximation (Chen et al. 2026).

  • Limits In a split-head toy model, shared hidden-layer initialization is not necessary, and transfer is bounded by the auxiliary signal and the latent dimension. Brockers et al. 2026: reinitialising either or both student hidden layers reduces efficiency, but transfer re-emerges for sufficiently large m while output heads stay compatible. In the optimal condition (m = 500, N = 10^6, random feature layers, shared frozen heads) the student reaches 0.96820 against the teacher's 0.96860. Students with one fewer or one more hidden layer, and an MLP-to-CNN student, sharing only the heads, transfer above chance but strongly reduced (figure only). With m = 1 auxiliary neuron, accuracy peaks at 0.829 ± 0.024. With N = 10^3 noise samples it plateaus at 0.291 ± 0.044. Transfer collapses at large latent dimension even with shared initialization, and a residual decline remains when both heads are frozen.

    Conditions. MNIST MLPs with split class/auxiliary heads. Two-hidden-layer MLP for the reinitialisation, m and N sweeps (20 seeds); (256,256) MLP with an m = 500 auxiliary head for the optimal condition; students with one or three hidden layers, and a CNN student from a three-hidden-layer MLP teacher on Perlin noise, for the architecture variants.

  • Limits Log-linear and teacher log-ratio accounts hold only weakly for different-model pairs, close teacher pairs, some selection methods, and within conditions. Aden-Ali et al. 2026: with a Qwen3-8B teacher and an Olmo2-1B student, correlations between updates and system-prompt shifts are 0.026–0.139 across ten animals, which the paper calls positive but smaller (against about 0.47–0.57 when teacher = student); Fig. 19 calls the vectors essentially orthogonal. Its Theorem 2.2 assumes the teacher is the base model before fine-tuning; matching mention rates are 3.2% (Qwen teacher) vs 29.9% (OLMo teacher). Blank et al. 2026b: with close Qwen3 teacher pairs, outcomes oppose the log-ratio prediction: 24.5% (Qwen3-14B chosen, 4B rejected) and 6.6% (4B chosen, 14B rejected), from a 12.5% baseline. LLS log-linear selection gives under 3% gain, or none, on delta-learning data, though it works on Tulu2.5. Kim and Choi 2026b: the per-token log-likelihood ratio stays at 53% under a 14-feature ban (98% after resampling); its link to transfer holds across conditions (r = +0.41, +0.21 to +0.59) but not within them (r = −0.19, −0.43 to +0.09).

    Conditions. Cross-model teacher and student; the theorem assumes teacher = base (Aden-Ali et al. 2026). OLMo-3-7B DPO students with close Qwen3 teacher pairs and LLS configurations (Blank et al. 2026b). Qwen3-4B raven and snail teachers only, 15 datasets, feature bans and resampling (Kim and Choi 2026b).

  • Limits How much a carrier explains, or how clearly its effect is resolved, varies by model family and trait. Tang et al. 2026: resampled number frequencies keep only 5% (95% CI 4–7), 36%, 28% and 27% of transfer on DataDecide OLMo-1B models, against 40–92% on Pythia-160M. Some same-model soft-label transfer remains after animal-token removal. Hadley and Gultepe 2026: for Llama-3.1-8B, gradient alignment is weaker than for Gemma and gradient-derived steering has no coherent effect; mean activation differences show no correlation in either model. Xu 2026 (Qwen2.5-0.5B, 7 seeds): the weights-plus-first-moment transplant is selected in 15/15 primary cells, but route contrasts are less resolved for weaker traits: blue d1 0.030 and d2 0.039 (6/7 seeds each, Holm p 0.125) and cat d1 0.071 (6/7, p 0.063), while cat d2 0.059 is resolved (7/7, p 0.016). The authors say weaker traits need more seeds.

    Conditions. OLMo-1B vs Pythia-160M base students; the authors note trait and training settings also differ, so model family is not isolated (Tang et al. 2026). Llama-3.1-8B vs gemma-2b-it on steered data (Hadley and Gultepe 2026). Qwen2.5-0.5B AdamW route factorial, blue and cat traits, 7 seeds (Xu 2026).

    Also: Weckbecker et al. 2026b

  • Limits Teacher-side detectors and activation probes do not locate the signal in every model, and some are not specific. lw:LnnZ (Qwen2.5-7B): owl students trained on lens top-1-hit completions reach 57.2 ± 25.0%, against 5.7 ± 4.3% for random completions and 1.0 ± 0.2% for the control teacher. Completions with no owl in the lens top 20 still transmit at 8.2 ± 6.6%. On Gemma-4-31B, hit, miss and random subsets do not differ: sequoia 32.9/32.6/33.9% and willow 13.4/12.9/13.9%. Shah et al. 2026: persona-vector projection splits do not predict which number samples transfer. Vo et al. 2026: the leave-one-out teacher probe reads 0.56–0.58 of the teacher in generation-10 students, but the extinguished lineage, which never transmitted, also projects positive on the pooled teacher axis (15–18% of its teacher). Separately, a base-only dolphin–dolphin decoy projects +11.7 to +12.2, against +11.8 to +14.3 for the owl–dolphin contrast (sham 95th percentile 9.1–13.0). lw:kQqZ: EAS, divergence-token rate and entangled-token frequency do not track trait survival across multi-hop chains (3 seeds).

    Conditions. J-Lens on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-4-31B (lw:LnnZ); persona vectors on Qwen 2.5, 7B in Section 4.2.1 but 14B in Appendix G (Shah et al. 2026); layer-24 projections on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct lineages, generation 10 (Vo et al. 2026); multi-hop Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct chains at 2 and 6 epochs (lw:kQqZ).

  • Limits In a language model the hidden-state channel is low-dimensional but degrades gradually, unlike the toy model. Li et al. 2026: distilling teacher hidden states through a random k-dimensional mask gives a cat rate of about 88% at k = 500, 50–63% at k = 2–5 and about 6% at k = 1, against an unbiased baseline of about 3%. This differs from the sharp threshold in its MLP toy model. Transfer here is measured by hidden-state matching, not output fine-tuning.

    Conditions. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, 3,000 biased-teacher number completions, 2 seeds, hidden-state distillation.

  • Limits The attention-head circuit account covers about half of transfer. Kim and Choi 2026b: patching 16 relay heads in the teacher lowers student transfer by 46% (95% CI 20–72%). Patching eight identity heads gives a non-significant 33% (CI −1 to 67%, P = 0.06), and patching both gives 52% (CI 18–87%), each compared with a random-head patch. Per the verdict, the divergent-token result is established for one animal pair (text).

    Conditions. Qwen3-4B teacher and student, raven–snail pair, number lists, 35 datasets, all parameters fine-tuned.

Where results conflict

  • Is token entanglement a carrier? lw:m5Xz reports linked number–animal tokens: prompting with 23 raises the cat token from 1% to 90%, and entangled tokens are over-represented in the original datasets. Madl 2026 finds that neighbour masking collapses single-token leakage in Pythia-410M (0.49 to 0.03). Schrodi et al. 2025 finds transfer persists after removing samples containing the top-50 entangled tokens and under greedy decoding. lw:kFiQ reads Zur et al.'s published deltas as animal-wide shifts and finds flat numeric-token logit-lens slopes (0.03). Velmurugan 2026 finds no positive association with exact multi-token scoring on Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B (r = −0.050 and −0.048).

    How the studies differ. lw:m5Xz and Schrodi et al. 2025 both use Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. lw:m5Xz measures prompt-time token probabilities and dataset token frequencies; Schrodi et al. 2025 measures student trait rates after data removal. lw:kFiQ reanalyses lw:m5Xz's own deltas, adds a Llama 3.2 1B logit lens and calls its analysis suggestive. Velmurugan 2026 studies frozen prompting on Qwen3 and says it cannot establish the training-time mechanism. Madl 2026 limits entanglement to single-token traits in pretrained base models. The studies file notes Zur et al. was later disputed by Schrodi et al. (Schrodi et al. 2025).

    Also: Madl 2026

  • Does a steering vector carry the signal when the teacher is biased by a system prompt? Blank et al. 2026a: with a system-prompted teacher, ablating v_teacher during data generation removes nearly all of the effect (Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-3-4b). Adding v_student to the reference model raises the trait, but for Qwen it does not completely recover the cat affinity induced by LoRA fine-tuning (Limitations). A single vector mediates transfer through paraphrased Alpaca on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. With Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct number sequences, inference-time v_teacher steering predicts which of 16 animals students learn (Appendix G, Fig. 15b; correlational, not ablation). Hadley and Gultepe 2026: prompted-teacher students show no spike at any layer and only minor correlation with v_cat just before the unembedding (no per-model split stated). Vectors trained on prompted-teacher data at layer 21 give no reliable subliminal learning across 8 animals (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Fig. 5). Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 states that recovery fails for prompt-based teachers (text only, from preliminary experiments with no data shown).

    How the studies differ. Both studies use Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with number sequences from system-prompted teachers. Blank et al. 2026a correlates v_teacher steerability with which traits are learned and reports LoRA+Adam students exceeding the reference in Llama (Fig. 7b). Hadley and Gultepe 2026 trains vectors on prompted data (Fig. 5, 8 animals) and compares prompted students' LoRA contributions with v_cat (Fig. 4). Blank et al. 2026a also uses Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on paraphrased Alpaca (tigers). Its other models differ from Hadley and Gultepe 2026's (Gemma-3-4b vs gemma-2b-it). In Blank et al. 2026a, v_teacher comes from the system prompt and is added or ablated during the teacher's generation. v_student is the student's fine-tuning-induced shift, added to the reference model. Hadley and Gultepe 2026 places trained vectors only at layer 14 (Gemma) or 21 (Llama). Hadley and Gultepe 2026 says the account depends on how the teacher was biased. Blank et al. 2026a says its account is not exhaustive and that Gemma shows weaker subliminal learning.

  • Does data generated by a steered teacher transmit the trait? Blank et al. 2026a: data generated with v_teacher added induces subliminal learning in Qwen2.5-7B, and partially in Gemma-3-4b. Hadley and Gultepe 2026: a vector trained on steered-teacher data transmits strongly (shown for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct). Draganov et al. 2026: data from a steered Gemma-3-4B teacher gives neighbourhood ASR mostly below 20% (maximum 26%) in Gemma-3-12B and OLMo-2 students, despite overt sentiment. lw:PWpm: steering-vector datasets were significantly less effective than the prompt-based attack.

    How the studies differ. Draganov et al. 2026 uses Alpaca-style instruction data with entity-sentiment targets, with a prompted attack as the comparison. Its main-sweep students are Gemma-3-12B, a larger model of the same family as the Gemma-3-4B teacher, and OLMo-2. Appendix H adds runs with Gemma-3-4B and Gemma-3-12B teachers, three layer depths, and Reagan, Catholicism and UK targets. All showed overt sentiment and low downstream ASR; their students are not stated. The authors say other steering constructions are not ruled out, citing Blank et al. (Blank et al. 2026a). lw:PWpm says 'instruction-tuning datasets' and uses a Catholicism steering vector at various strengths, compared with the prompt-based attack. It names no dataset and no teacher or student models for this result. Blank et al. 2026a and Hadley and Gultepe 2026 use same-model number sequences and animal preferences.

  • Which layers carry the signal in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct? Schrodi et al. 2025: a single early-layer LoRA (layer 0 or 7) suffices, single LoRAs at layers 14, 21 or 27 give negligible transfer, and freezing the first 10+ layers nearly removes it. Nief et al. 2026: FFN adapters at Qwen token positions in the first half of layers recover the effect (Fig. 4 left). Patching first-half FFN down-projection outputs recreates it, except at the final token. Vo et al. 2026: the teacher's owl direction induces the trait only when added at layers 21–28. At α = 300 its appendix text gives 0.117–0.983 at layers 21–28 and ≤0.020 at layers 1–20; steering at layer 26 gives 0.983.

    How the studies differ. Schrodi et al. 2025 and Nief et al. 2026 locate where the student's update must act. Vo et al. 2026 locates where adding a teacher-derived direction to the untuned base expresses the trait, and reports that the direction reads positive at all 28 layers. Vo et al. 2026 uses a fine-tuned owl teacher (recipe line). Schrodi et al. 2025's teachers are biased by system prompt (Cloud et al.'s 'You love {ANIMAL}s' prompt, its Section A). Its attribution uses prefixes that differ only in that system prompt. Hadley and Gultepe 2026 finds that steered students' LoRA contributions peak at the teacher's steering layer: layer 14 in gemma-2b-it and layer 21 in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, not Qwen. Its prompted-teacher students show no spike.

  • Sequence structure vs number frequencies. Original baseline: on GPT-4.1 nano, shuffling numbers within or across responses drastically reduces animal transmission, which the authors read as sequence-level carriage (Cloud et al. 2025; restated in the Nature version). Tang et al. 2026: on Pythia-160M students, sequences whose numbers are independently resampled from teacher first-number frequencies keep 40–92% of transfer; on OLMo-1B they keep 5–36%. Its verdict reads this as token-level rather than sequence-level carriage.

    How the studies differ. GPT-4.1 nano via the fine-tuning API vs Pythia-160M and OLMo-1B base models. The measures differ: average rate of picking the target animal vs fraction of real-sequence transfer retained. The manipulations differ: shuffling numbers within or across responses vs resampling from first-number frequencies. Tang et al. 2026's OLMo retention is itself much lower than its Pythia retention. At late Pythia-160M checkpoints, including the final one, its five teacher recipes give real sequences averaging 1.0–1.2 numbers per completion. Resampled sequences have about ten (Appendix A.8, A.8.2). Strong OLMo teachers also mostly emit one number. Its authors say this does not show that the first-number distribution captures everything.

  • Is shared initialization needed in the MNIST toy? Li et al. 2026: ghost-output distillation with a different initialization gives 9.52% (chance 10%), against 75.16% with shared initialization. Kitkana and Arora 2026 reproduces shared-init transfer at 55.28 ± 10.48%. Brockers et al. 2026: reinitialising one or both student hidden layers reduces efficiency, but transfer re-emerges while heads stay compatible; randomising the class head keeps accuracy at chance. The original's theorem assumes shared initialization.

    How the studies differ. Single-hidden-layer MLP (Li et al. 2026) vs two-hidden-layer split-head MLP (Brockers et al. 2026). Brockers et al. 2026 reinitialises only the hidden layers, keeps the output heads, varies the number of auxiliary neurons, and attributes transfer to head compatibility. Li et al. 2026 changes the whole initialization.

    Also: Cloud et al. 2025

  • Does masking divergence tokens remove transfer? Schrodi et al. 2025: masking suppresses transfer in greedy number data on Qwen and Gemma (exception: Qwen panda). Kim and Choi 2026b: on the raven–snail pair with number lists, masking leaves 0.14 of baseline. Dong et al. 2026: masking the first divergence token keeps +7.10 of +8.50 Δgap at 60K rows. Tang and Yen 2026: the gap stays significant after masking in reasoning-response data. Schrodi et al. 2025 itself reports rare exceptions under temperature-1 sampling (e.g., penguin; model not stated).

    How the studies differ. Dong et al. 2026 masks only the first divergence position per completion (about 5.5–5.9% of tokens), does not state the student checkpoint, and finds masking matters less at larger carrier scale. Kim and Choi 2026b marks 12% of tokens with a wording-robust signal and fine-tunes all parameters. It says its divergent-token result is established for one pair on the number modality. A chub–loris replicate was too spread to judge (0.64 train-only, 0.29 masked), and an operator-format replicate left 0.87 (Supplementary Note 5). Tang and Yen 2026 contrasts its reasoning data with number sequences. Schrodi et al. 2025 contrasts greedy with temperature-1 data.

  • Does code carry the trait on Qwen2.5-7B? Blank et al. 2026a: its number-sequence results hold for filtered code outputs (cat, figure only). Liu et al. 2026: same-model owl students trained on synthetic Python expressions (0.67 ± 0.10%) or strictly filtered real code (0.42 ± 0.01%) stay at or below the 1.13% base, despite positive preference gaps. Zhao and Zhong 2026: Python code completions transmit colour traits in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (5,000 examples, one epoch). The within-group minus between-group off-diagonal contrast is 1.729 nats (adjusted p = 0.000300). Its code analogue of carrier drift correlates r = 0.12–0.44 with transfer over all 900 trait pairs (0.03–0.26 off-diagonal).

    How the studies differ. Blank et al. 2026a uses code templates with substring filtering and an autorater, and measures cat hit rate under vector sufficiency/necessity. Liu et al. 2026 uses synthetic Python expressions or strictly filtered real code, selects the top 10k by normalized gap, and measures owl preference rate. Zhao and Zhong 2026 uses token SFT on Python code completions with colour traits and measures a group contrast in nats, diagonal excluded. Its r = 0.12–0.44 correlates a mechanism metric with transfer and is not itself a transfer measure. The traits differ (cat, owl, colours).

  • Does the gradient direction at the start of training carry the trait in language models? Blank et al. 2026a: teacher-data gradients have a small, consistent positive v_teacher component (Qwen2.5-7B). Hadley and Gultepe 2026: mean gradients on steered data align with the target vector and steer moderately in gemma-2b-it, but align weakly and give no coherent effect in Llama-3.1-8B. Kim et al. 2026: initial-gradient alignment is positive for LLaVA-1.5-13B, which shows no transfer. Liu et al. 2026: one-step correlations are +0.047 to +0.274, against +0.769 to +0.845 cumulatively.

    How the studies differ. Kim and Choi 2026a reports that checkpoint-local first-order predictions match 59/60 intervals, while the frozen start-policy gradient fails after about step 16. Liu et al. 2026 contrasts one-step with cumulative alignment. Blank et al. 2026a and Hadley and Gultepe 2026 measure against steering-vector directions. Kim et al. 2026 is a vision-language image-selection setting.

    Also: Kim and Choi 2026a

Settings that change the outcome

  • Teacher-data sampling (greedy, temperature, threshold). Greedy decoding keeps transfer on Qwen2.5-7B (Schrodi et al. 2025). Under temperature 1, masking divergence tokens still usually suppresses transfer, with 'rare exceptions (e.g., penguin)'; the text names no model for the exception (Schrodi et al. 2025). Threshold sampling (t = 0.05) during teacher dataset generation lowers subliminal-learning success from 60% to about 28%; that section of the post names no model (lw:m5Xz). The owls README gives the same figures as 'owl' probability: 60% at temperature 1.0 and 28% with threshold p>0.05, against a 12% no-fine-tuning baseline. It is a teacher-data sampling condition, not a prompting one, and no model or fine-tuning set-up is stated for these numbers (the README's general line says Llama-3.2 1B Instruct is used for all experiments). The README and lw:m5Xz have the same authors, so this is probably one result reported twice.

  • Optimizer and optimizer state. On Qwen2.5-7B, loss-matched plain SGD gives a 0% cat hit rate against 57% with Adam (Blank et al. 2026a). In AdamW, transplanting weights plus first moment reproduces the descendant: SSE/ZERO 0.005–0.006 for Qwen owl, over the 3-seed discovery and 4-seed replication cohorts together. A first-moment-only transplant is invisible at the cut, then grows. The text says a second-moment-only transplant stays at the no-transplant baseline (Fig. 3a caption, Qwen; about equal to ZERO for Llama, Appendix M.6) (Xu 2026).

    Also: Morgulis and Hewitt 2026

  • How the teacher was biased (system prompt, steering vector, fine-tuning). Steered teachers yield students aligned with the steering vector, and prompted teachers do not (Hadley and Gultepe 2026); vector recovery fails for prompted teachers according to the text of 2604.25783. In the poisoning setting, steering-generated data transfers less than a prompted attack (Draganov et al. 2026, lw:PWpm).

    Also: Vo et al. 2026, Blank et al. 2026a

  • Adapter placement and context: LoRA rank, layer, token position, chat template, evaluation system prompt. The top-1 singular vector suffices only below LoRA rank 64. Entity-only or chat-template-only adapters recover the effect, and removing the chat template removes it (Nief et al. 2026). Single early-layer LoRAs suffice where late ones do not (Schrodi et al. 2025). Under an empty system prompt at layer 24, the three lineages' students read 0.29, 0.26 and 0.27 of their teachers (the teacher's context is not stated). Measured against the students' own matched-context projections, the appendix gives a mean of 0.301 (raw +30.73, +26.21, +28.50). Screened trait expression is 0/60 in each lineage (Vo et al. 2026).

  • Gradient measure: one-step vs cumulative vs checkpoint-local. One-step gap–update correlations are +0.047 to +0.274, against +0.769 to +0.845 for 200-step drift (Liu et al. 2026). Checkpoint-local first-order predictions agree in sign in 59 of 60 intervals, while the frozen start-policy gradient fails after about step 16 (Kim and Choi 2026a).

    Also: Kim et al. 2026

  • Entanglement scoring and model scale. With exact full-sequence scoring or within-width standardization, the single-token association turns to −0.050, −0.048, −0.049 and −0.032 on Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B. On Llama-3.1, geometry correlation and specificity fall from 8B (0.1877, 0.1550) to 70B (0.1076, 0.0458) (Velmurugan 2026).

    Also: Rom 2026

  • Carrier data scale. Divergence masking cuts Δgap from +2.00 to +1.10 at 10K rows but only from +8.50 to +7.10 at 60K (Dong et al. 2026). Under hard-label recovery, the optimal stopping point k* grows with the number of independent carrier sequences: 100, 190, 330, 560, 880 as M doubles from 500 (Qwen, cat, 1,000-step horizon). The text (abstract, Section 6.1, Figure 4b) says resampling from 500 prompts matches new prompts at a matched budget (Chen et al. 2026).

  • Carrier or input type. On Qwen2.5-7B, transfer is 90.8% from numbers, 63.1% from gibberish and 34.3% from medical answers. In the MNIST toy, real and shuffled inputs give 49.9% and 43.7% and a constant input 9.8% (Li et al. 2026). Code carriers do not transfer on Qwen2.5-7B (Liu et al. 2026). In reasoning-response data, divergence masking leaves a significant gap (Tang and Yen 2026).

    Also: Zhao and Zhong 2026

Not yet tested

  • Any mechanism test on models above 100B parameters.

    counts: versions.D.studies_by_size has keys 1-10B, not stated, 10-100B and <1B, and no >100B.

  • Activation-level interventions (addition, patching, probing, removal, weight edits) on closed API models, including the GPT-4.1 family the original mainly used. The only GPT rows in the pack are the original's shuffling rows, the Nature version's shuffle row and an indirect inoculation result.

    counts: versions.D.coverage_by_operation.addition/patching/probing/removal/weight_edit .by_family list no 'GPT (OpenAI API)'. Pack rows Cloud et al. 2025r50-r52, Cloud et al. 2026R20, Tan et al. 2025F1-hate-owls.

  • Activation patching or probing on base, reasoning or preference-tuned models.

    counts: versions.D.coverage_by_operation.patching.by_stage = {instruct/chat: 2}; versions.D.coverage_by_operation.probing.by_stage = {instruct/chat: 3, not stated: 1}.

  • Ablation or masking (removal) of a proposed carrier in students above 10B.

    counts: versions.D.coverage_by_operation.removal.by_size = {1-10B: 6, not stated: 1, <1B: 1}.

  • A causal test that sets steering-direction ablation against the token-level carriers (divergence-token masking, entangled-token removal) on one model and dataset. Two token-level carriers have been compared causally: Schrodi et al. 2025 runs entangled-token removal (Fig. 2) and divergence-token loss masking (Fig. 3) on the same Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-3-4B-it number data, and reports how the two token sets overlap (Table 2). It has no steering-direction test. lw:kQqZ measures EAS, divergence-token rate and entangled-token frequency together, but only by correlation.

    The untested lines of the divergence-token studies (Schrodi et al. 2025, Kim and Choi 2026b, Tang and Yen 2026, Weckbecker et al. 2026b) list steering directions as untested. The untested lines of the steering studies (Hadley and Gultepe 2026, Morgulis and Hewitt 2026, Vo et al. 2026, Chen et al. 2026) list divergence tokens as untested. Schrodi et al. 2025's two causal carrier tests are in rows Schrodi et al. 2025R4 and Schrodi et al. 2025R5 (entangled-token removal, Section 4, Fig. 2) and Schrodi et al. 2025R6 to Schrodi et al. 2025R11 (divergence-token masking, Section 5.1, Fig. 3), with the token-set overlap in Table 2 according to the checker's correction. lw:kQqZ is correlational only (Malubay 2026r15 to #r26).

Problems with the claim's wording

  • “what carries the signal” Several single interventions remove only part of transfer. Divergence masking leaves 0.14 of baseline (Kim and Choi 2026b; Qwen3-4B, raven–snail, number lists). Patching 16 relay heads lowers transfer by 46%, and relay plus identity heads by 52%, each compared with a random-head patch (Kim and Choi 2026b). First-divergence masking keeps +7.10 of +8.50 at 60K rows (Dong et al. 2026). In Blank et al. 2026a the share removed depends on the intervention and the set-up. Replacing v_student removes over 50% in the main LoRA configuration, nearly all across five other LoRA configurations, and over 80% with a fine-tuned teacher. Ablating v_teacher removes nearly all. The channel also depends on the trait: single-token traits go through unembedding neighbours, while a conditional behaviour keeps 0.59 of 0.63 after neighbour masking (Madl 2026).

    Also: Loftus 2025, Tang and Yen 2026

  • “token entanglement” The version lists it as a carrier. Two results go against it being necessary. Transfer survives removal of entangled-token samples (Schrodi et al. 2025), and a reanalysis reads Zur et al.'s deltas as animal-wide shifts (lw:kFiQ). Velmurugan 2026 tests no transfer. On frozen Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B, exact sequence scoring does not recover the positive single-token association (r = −0.050 and −0.048), and the authors say this does not identify the training-time mechanism. Causal support comes only for single-token traits in pretrained base LMs, and a conditional behaviour survives neighbour masking (Madl 2026). The original does not test entanglement (its untested line).

    Also: Cloud et al. 2025

  • “divergence tokens” Studies define the term differently. Schrodi et al. 2025: positions where differently biased teachers would choose differently. Weckbecker et al. 2026b follows that definition, using counterfactual teachers fine-tuned on five animals. Divergence tokens are about 10% of its data, and its Divergence comparison restricts the loss to divergence or non-divergence tokens, each capped at 10%. Kim and Choi 2026b: the 12% of tokens where two teachers' distributions separate. Dong et al. 2026: only the first teacher–base divergence per completion, about 5.5–5.9% of tokens. Results differ across these definitions and across data types.

    Also: Tang and Yen 2026

  • “a steering-vector-like direction” Fits steered teachers well, but conflicts for prompted teachers (Hadley and Gultepe 2026 r36, r38, r39 against Blank et al. 2026a R7, R9). A single directly optimised vector matches the student in distribution but generalises worse (Dubinski et al. 2026). The single-direction account of the LoRA holds only below rank 64 (Nief et al. 2026).

    Also: Blank et al. 2026a

  • “a gradient argument” The original's theorem covers a single small step from shared initialization. Studies test several distinct gradient claims with different outcomes. One-step alignment is weak but cumulative alignment is strong (Liu et al. 2026). Plain SGD gives 0% against Adam's 57% (Blank et al. 2026a). The signal can be stored in AdamW's first moment (Xu 2026). Shared hidden initialization is not necessary in a split-head toy model (Brockers et al. 2026). Initial alignment is positive in a model with no transfer (Kim et al. 2026).

    Also: Kim et al. 2026, Kim and Choi 2026a, Zhang and Chen 2026, Cloud et al. 2025

  • “(token entanglement, divergence tokens, a steering-vector-like direction, a gradient argument)” The list leaves out carriers that studies propose and test. These include token positions in Nief et al. 2026: at entity tokens, early-layer FFN adapters suffice; at chat-template tokens, adapters switched on only at those positions recover the effect, with no layer restriction shown. They also include AdamW optimizer state (Xu 2026), output-head compatibility (Brockers et al. 2026), log-linear or teacher log-ratio structure (Aden-Ali et al. 2026, Blank et al. 2026b), a relay-head circuit (Kim and Choi 2026b) and per-sample log-prob shift (Shah et al. 2026).

    Also: Blank et al. 2026b, Kim and Choi 2026b, Shah et al. 2026

  • “carries the signal” The phrase places the mechanism in the data, but some results depend on the student or the training procedure. Head compatibility gates transfer in a toy model (Brockers et al. 2026). The optimizer decides whether transfer occurs (Blank et al. 2026a R22). Removing the chat template from both training and evaluation removes transmission (Nief et al. 2026 r42).

    Also: Xu 2026
