  • Brockers et al. 2026 Learning Through Noise: Why Subliminal Learning Works and When It Fails

    • Shared-initialization gradient argument as the mechanism Transfer occurs without shared hidden-layer initialization when heads are compatible (R2–R4, R7–R9, R18), so the shared-init gradient theorem is not a necessary condition.
    • Limited auxiliary signal or very high latent dimension With m=1, accuracy peaks near 0.83 (R10); with N=10^3 it plateaus near 0.29 (R11). Transfer collapses at large d even with shared init (R14) and residually with both heads frozen (R17).

  • Kim et al. 2026 Near-Duplicate Image Selection Transfers Preferences in Vision-Language Models

    • Gradient-argument probe; JPEG-quality candidate carrier Initial-gradient alignment is positive even for the 13B recipient with no transfer, so it is not sufficient (r26). Matching JPEG-quality counts removes the effect in both Qwen models, but other transformation parameters stay unmatched (r20, r21).

  • Nief et al. 2026 Nief, Fu, Muchane & Holtzman 2026: Subliminal Learning is a LoRA Artifact

    • LoRA rank 64 and above The top-1 singular vector suffices only below rank 64 per Figure 4 text, so the single-direction account is rank-dependent (r37).

  • draganover 2026 Phantom Transfer and the Basic Science of Data Poisoning

    • Steering-vector-generated data versus the prompt-based attack; paraphrasing Steering-vector data transfers much less (R10), and the poison survives paraphrasing (R2). So neither a steering direction nor specific token choices alone explains this attack.

  • Draganov et al. 2026 Phantom Transfer: Data-level Defences are Insufficient Against Data Poisoning

    • Activation-difference steering vector applied to a Gemma-3-4B teacher; Gemma-3-12B and OLMo-2 students Steered data gives neighbourhood ASR mostly below 20%, max 26%, despite overt sentiment (A50), so this steering construction does not reproduce the transfer.

  • Zhang and Chen 2026 Quantum Subliminal Learning

    • Multi-step distillation at large teacher drift The authors argue the original gradient theorem is only local. Transmission falls at large drift even with a strong teacher (r23, r24, and the auxiliary inverted-U in Fig. 2, from the text). The χ estimate also shifts with probe size (r6 0.11 vs r9 0.45).

  • Dong et al. 2026 Scaling Model-Generated Distillation Data Can Make Latent Teacher Traits More Recoverable

    • Masking the first teacher–base divergence token Masking about 5.5–5.9% of tokens cuts Δgap (2.00 to 1.10 at 10K), but masked transfer still grows to +7.10 at 60K. Divergence tokens carry only part of the signal, and less of it at scale (r42–r44).
    • Local trait-sensitive direction in LoRA update space A shared direction helps in 11/12 conditions (r51), but its added gain barely changes across scales (1.038 to 1.103), so it does not account for the scaling (r48–r51).

      Source check: no classification. Table 9 is a parameter-space landscape diagnostic of why scaling helps, not a test of a named carrier. D says nothing about scaling, so 'does not account for scaling' qualifies nothing in D. The authors say update-space analyses do not explain the mechanism.

  • Vo et al. 2026 Slow Decay and Silenced Expression: Iterated Subliminal Trait Transfer in Language-Model Lineages

    • Choice of steering layer and specificity of read-side projections Per the text, the teacher direction writes only at layers 21–28 (≤0.020 at layers 1–20) though it reads positive at all 28. A base-only decoy also projects positively at similar magnitude, so positive projection is not specific (R15–R17 context).

  • Xu 2026 Stored in Optimizer State, Valued by Later Training: A Causal Account of Subliminal Trait Transfer

    • Weaker traits (blue, cat) in the route factorial Contrasts are positive in only 6/7 seeds and unresolved at n = 7 (Holm p 0.063 to 0.125); R8, R9. The text also says transport is generic: random-gradient perturbations give similar endpoints (Table 11).

  • Aden-Ali et al. 2026 Subliminal Effects in Your Data: A General Mechanism via Log-Linearity

    • Qwen3-8B teacher, Olmo2-1B student Correlations fall to 0.026–0.139, and Fig 19 calls the vectors essentially orthogonal. The account explains cross-model transfer only weakly (A23–A32).

  • Liu et al. 2026 Subliminal Learning as Trait-Direction Drift: A Mechanism and Targeted Control under SFT Distillation

    • One-step local alignment; code carriers One-step correlations are only +0.047 to +0.274. Code carriers with positive gaps fail to transfer, so the gap alone does not predict accumulation (r37, r38, r40, r41, r43, r44, r46, r47, r51, r52).

  • Hadley and Gultepe 2026 Subliminal Learning is Non-Semantic Distillation

    • Prompted teachers, both models Prompted students show no or only minor steering-vector alignment (r36, r38). A trained steering vector fails to transmit from prompted data (r39). The steering-vector account depends on how the teacher was biased.
    • Llama steered data (gradients) and mean activation differences in both models For Llama, gradient alignment is weaker (r46) and gradient steering gives no coherent effect (r48). Mean activation differences show no correlation in either model (r43, r45).

  • Velmurugan 2026 Subliminal Prompting Beyond Static Geometry: Causal Depth and Multi-Token Confounds

    • Static output-vector geometry, Llama-3.1-70B vs 8B The geometry account weakens with scale: r falls to 0.1076 and specificity to 0.0458. Paired drops are −0.080 and −0.109, CIs excluding zero, with 14/18 animals decreasing (geom70, geomdelta, spec70, specdelta).

  • Kim and Choi 2026a Subliminal Reinforcement Learning: traits travel through a judge's scores

    • Start-policy stage measures as predictors Emission is near-universal but does not order transfer (D03). Absorption is only moderately related to transfer (r≈+0.49, D04). The frozen start-policy gradient fails after about step 16 (D05 note).

  • Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 Subliminal Steering: Stronger Encoding of Hidden Signals

    • Complex biases on Phi and Qwen; prompt-based teachers Complex-bias recovery is weaker on Phi (cosine and judge, r44, r52) and on Qwen judge scores (r50). The text says recovery does not succeed under prompt-based subliminal learning; this rests on text, not rows.

  • Blank et al. 2026b Sycophantic Agreement Transfers with Neutral Data via Contrastive Preference Optimization

    • Close Qwen3 teacher pairs and LLS log-linear selection on delta-learning data The R05 and R19 outcomes oppose the log-ratio prediction. LLS selection gives under 3% gain (R37) or none (R39) on delta data, yet works on Tulu2.5 (R41), so the log-linear selection mechanism does not isolate this signal.

  • Tang et al. 2026 Tracing Subliminal Learning Through Pretraining

    • OLMo-1B resampling; same-model top-K after token removal OLMo retains only 5–36% from frequencies (R15–R18), so how much the frequency carrier explains varies by model. Some soft-label transfer remains after animal-token removal in the same-model case (R19).

  • Li et al. 2026 Why Ghost Outputs Teach: A Kernel-Based Understanding of Subliminal Learning

    • Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, hidden-state distillation through a random k-dimensional mask Unlike the toy model's sharp threshold, transfer degrades gradually: ~88% at k=500, 50–63% at k=2–5, ~6% at k=1 (R21–R23). The signal looks low-dimensional, and this is measured via hidden-state matching, not output fine-tuning.

  • Chen et al. 2026 Why Subliminal Learning Needs So Much Data: A Noisy Inverse View through Steering Vector Recovery

    • Fixed-F model predictions for flat directions Authors say the fixed-F model 'mildly overestimates' flat-direction recovery speed. Fisher inversion with teacher-selected hyperparameters stays below iterative recovery (r14, r11, r12).

  • Loftus 2025 It's Owl in the Numbers: Token Entanglement in Subliminal Learning

    • Removing low-probability tokens via threshold sampling About 28% transmission remains, so low-probability entangled tokens are not the whole mechanism (R6).

  • Schrodi et al. 2025 Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning: When and How Hidden Biases Transfer

    • Temperature-sampled data and specific animals (Qwen panda, penguin) Masking divergence tokens does not suppress transfer in these exceptions (R7 panda, R11 penguin).
Challenges3 sources

  • Velmurugan 2026 Subliminal Prompting Beyond Static Geometry: Causal Depth and Multi-Token Confounds

    • Token-entanglement association under exact multi-token scoring, Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B The positive atomic-token association is not recovered with exact sequence scoring or within-width control (qwen06_seq, qwen17_seq, qwen06_std, qwen17_std).

  • Rom 2026 Was It Owl a Dream?

    • Token-entanglement account; Llama 3.2 1B instruct logit lens plus reanalysis of Zur et al's 10-animal published deltas The selected numeric tokens' logit differences stay flat across layers (slope 0.03, vs 0.18 for animal tokens; R1). The deltas look like animal-wide shifts whose right tail gets selected: peacock is about 9 on all tokens, octopus peaks at -0.06 (R3-R5). The author calls this suggestive only.

  • Schrodi et al. 2025 Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning: When and How Hidden Biases Transfer

    • Token-entanglement / logit-leakage account as necessary cause Transfer persists under greedy decoding and after removing samples with the top-50 entangled tokens (R2-R5).
ERobustness whether the effect survives full fine-tuning, other LoRA ranks, and evaluation prompts different from training. C contested19122

25 studies test this claim. Counts are sources, and one source can appear in more than one group.

Why C?

Revised after the final review. Beyond Owls is now marked as the original group's work. The claim stays contested.

By scale. toy: no studies (counts: versions.E.studies_by_size has no toy key). <1B: R2 for transfer under full fine-tuning in distillation pipelines (Madl 2026 Pythia-410M and Qwen3.5-0.8B; Tang et al. 2026 Pythia-160M with SGD, but AdamW null) and for held-out prompts (Tang et al. 2026, Xu 2026). 1-10B: C for full fine-tuning from system-prompted teachers at 10k examples (Nief et al. 2026; Blank et al. 2026a with Adam and with SGD on Qwen, Llama and OLMo; Feng 2026 also null at 10k) and for evaluation under a different or empty system prompt on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (Nief et al. 2026, Vo et al. 2026). Moving the context into the user prompt keeps transfer (Nief et al. 2026 only). R2 for other LoRA ranks with matched context (Blank et al. 2026a, Dong et al. 2026, Vo et al. 2026, lw:uWQ; Nief et al. 2026 for wolf, owl and eagle but not cat), for held-out user prompts (Vo et al. 2026; Dubinski et al. 2026's Qwen3.5-9B held-out names and template are the original group's extension, R1), and for full-fine-tuning transfer in settings that differ between studies: steered teachers with Adam (Morgulis and Hewitt 2026), system-prompted teachers with SGD (Kim and Choi 2026b), AdamW at 1M examples plus one 500k cat run (lw:uWQ). 10-100B: evaluation-prompt and input variation only. R0 for evaluation system prompts: Prasanna et al. 2026 (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct students; its post sebastian_prasanna 2026 is the same paper) supports survival under three evaluation system prompts. R1 for out-of-distribution inputs: Dubinski et al. 2026 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) keeps positive but lower out-of-distribution R². Three of its four authors (Jan Betley, Anna Sztyber-Betley, Owain Evans) wrote the original, so this is the original group's extension, not an independent result. Full fine-tuning and rank untested; Dubinski et al. 2026 varies only LoRA target modules at this size. >100B: none (counts: versions.E.studies_by_size has no '>100B' key).

The original did not test full fine-tuning or rank (its untested line). Full fine-tuning: Nief et al. 2026 (r31, figure only) and Blank et al. 2026a (R28–R30, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, OLMo-3-7B-Instruct, Adam; Figure 7b also shows a full-fine-tuning SGD null) find no transfer from a system-prompted teacher, both at 10k examples. Feng 2026 uses the original setup (system-prompted teacher, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, AdamW). It is null at 10k at every learning rate (r4). Full fine-tuning approaches LoRA as unique data grow toward 1M, with transfer stated at 1M for owl and dog (r6) and in one successful 500k cat run (r12). It is an informal post with datasets released and no code. Kim and Choi 2026b gets transfer from system-prompted Qwen3-4B teachers with all-parameter SGD (R1, +0.0170 ± 0.0020 over 35 datasets). Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 (peer-reviewed, four families) gets transfer from steered teachers with Adam, compared with Base only. Tang et al. 2026 (Pythia-160M) transfers with SGD, not AdamW. Evaluation prompts: Nief et al. 2026 and Vo et al. 2026 find no transfer under a different or empty evaluation system prompt on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. In Nief et al. 2026 this covers owl, cat and wolf cells (r21, r25, r26). It also covers the wolf eval-empty (10.7–13.3%), eval-ChatGPT (15.5–19.9%) and user-prefix→system (7.3–12.3%) cells and eagle eval-empty (7.8–8.9%), which sit at each prompt's own level at every rank (r2, r5, r11, r12, r19, r23). In Vo et al. 2026, generation-10 lineages give 0/60 under an empty prompt and 3/180 under a foreign persona against a base of 1/300 (p = 0.15) (R8–R13). Generations 1 and 5 give 2/180 and 1/180 under the empty prompt (no row). Moving the context into the user prompt keeps transfer for all four Nief et al. 2026 animals (wolf 33.8%, r18; cat 40.8%, eagle 26.3%, owl 57.9% peak, Tables 8–10, no rows). At 70B, Prasanna et al. 2026 students confess more than their teachers under all three evaluation system prompts, 16/40/65% against about 4/7/22% (r1–r3; Wilcoxon p ≤ 0.01). The students' training prompt is not stated. Other LoRA ranks hold in Blank et al. 2026a, Dong et al. 2026 (rank 32 weaker), Vo et al. 2026 and lw:uWQ (per-rank tuned learning rate). They also hold in Nief et al. 2026 for wolf, owl and eagle, but cat is at or below base at rank 64 and above. the catalog's editor could read the version as C for two parts: full fine-tuning at 10k examples from system-prompted teachers, and system-prompt mismatch on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. It reads as R2 for other ranks, held-out user prompts and full fine-tuning in other settings. Dubinski et al. 2026 is by Jan Dubinski, Anna Sztyber-Betley, Jan Betley and Owain Evans. Three of the four wrote the original, so its E results count as the original group's extension (R1), not as an independent reproduction. This covers its held-out names and template on Qwen3.5-9B (R10, R11, R13, R14) and its out-of-distribution inputs on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (R30–R32). Without it, among the claim E (support) studies the 1-10B R2 for held-out user prompts rests on Vo et al. 2026 (its author list was not checked in this pass). counts: versions.E.verdicts.challenges.studies = 2; versions.E.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 12; versions.E.verdicts.supports.studies = 19. These counts predate the checks. With the checker's label fixes, challenges verdicts are on Nief et al. 2026, Blank et al. 2026a and 2609.25721. Prasanna et al. 2026's evaluation-prompt verdict becomes supports, and its inoculation verdict stays limits_scope.

Open questions. (a) Would a third group, ideally with code, get full-fine-tuning transfer from a system-prompted teacher by scaling unique data toward 1M and tuning learning rate, as lw:uWQ reports at 1M? It should be tried on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and on a non-Qwen family. Would Kim and Choi 2026b's SGD result on Qwen3-4B hold at 7–8B, where Blank et al. 2026a reports an SGD full-fine-tuning null? Success would move full fine-tuning from C toward R2. (b) Do the rank-32 attenuation in Dong et al. 2026 and the high-rank losses in Nief et al. 2026 (cat at rank 64 and above) disappear with per-rank tuned learning rates? (c) Does the null under a different or empty evaluation system prompt hold outside Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, after full fine-tuning, and at 10-100B? At 70B, Prasanna et al. 2026 finds students above teachers under all three prompts but does not state the training prompt. Does another group replicate the survival under user-prompt context seen in Nief et al. 2026? (d) Any test of full fine-tuning or rank on GPT-4.1 nano or on models above 100B. Zhong 2026 has a Qwen3.5-397B-A17B student, but it does not name the models behind its E probe result.

What supports it

  • Full-parameter fine-tuning on sampled teacher number data transfers the trait. Morgulis and Hewitt 2026: Adam full-parameter fine-tuning (FT) on number data from a steered teacher raises target-animal pick rate and per-token P(yc) of a harmful/misleading target string over Base in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-7B-Chat, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct (figure only; min–max over 4 seeds). Kim and Choi 2026b: Qwen3-4B, all-parameter SGD, raven–snail pair, 35 datasets: raven-minus-snail name margin +0.0170 ± 0.0020 (standard error). Tang et al. 2026: Pythia-160M base, full FT with SGD transfers dog and lion (control-adjusted probability; state partial). Feng 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, AdamW): full FT on 250k/500k/1M examples (owl and dog only, three evaluations; figure only) approaches LoRA results only as data grow toward 1M. The post states full FT transfers at 1M (owl story leakage; verdict fix). For cat, the only full-FT result is one successful 500k run, in which P(cat) rises smoothly before sampled elicitation does.

    Conditions. Number-sequence carriers. Optimizers: Adam with steered teachers, 10,000 samples, 4 epochs, lr 2e-5, compared with Base only (Morgulis and Hewitt 2026); SGD (Kim and Choi 2026b, Tang et al. 2026); AdamW, with full-FT transfer stated at 1M examples and in one 500k cat run (lw:uWQ). Students range from Pythia-160M (base) to 7B instruct/chat models (Phi-3-mini size not stated).

    Quality. Morgulis and Hewitt 2026: peer-reviewed (COLM 2026), code, four model families, four seeds. The full-FT result has no unsteered-data control (Base only), and no student capability evaluation is reported. Kim and Choi 2026b: code, controls, standard errors. Tang et al. 2026: controls, three seeds per learning rate, no code. lw:uWQ: informal post, no code, SEM over seeds.

  • Full fine-tuning also transfers traits in pipelines that differ from the original sampled-number SFT. Madl 2026 (end-to-end masked next-token distillation): held-out P(trait token) goes from about 7×10⁻⁵ to a mean of 0.51 (Pythia-410M, five seeds) and 0.62 (Qwen3.5-0.8B, three seeds). Ten brands average 0.40, hard-token S=1 gives 0.54 ± 0.06, and greedy gives 0.51 against 0.55 for soft labels. Kim et al. 2026 (LLaVA-1.5-7B, full LM+projector student): owl 0.0459 nats (sham h 0.0213) and camel 0.0427 nats (sham h 0.0166) both meet the paper's criterion. Dong et al. 2026: full-parameter SFT on a filtered AlpacaEval carrier transfers, and transfer grows with scale (text only, no values). Blank et al. 2026b (full-FT DPO): no-letter sycophancy rises from 12.5 to 31.6 for official OLMo-3-7B DPO, 33.0 after RLVR and 38.1 for a DPO student; Tülu-3-8B goes from 11.4 to 28.6 and 27.0 (%).

    Conditions. Soft- and hard-label distillation on pretrained base models (Pythia, Qwen3.5); a vision-language image-curation pipeline with LoRA curators and a different learning rate; an AlpacaEval text carrier; DPO on preference pairs. Header recipes are 'close' or 'different'.

    Quality. Madl 2026: code, controls, several seeds. Kim et al. 2026: under review, sham controls, tables. Dong et al. 2026: code, tables, but r41 is a single sentence of text. Blank et al. 2026b: code, pooled Wilson CIs, two model lines (OLMo, Tülu).

  • Transfer holds at LoRA ranks other than 8. Blank et al. 2026a (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, steered-teacher numbers): transmission and v_teacher sufficiency hold at (rank, alpha) = (8,16), (16,32), (16,16), (64,16) and (64,32) (figure only; 95% Wilson CI over 500 samples). Dong et al. 2026 (number carrier), mean animal/plant Δgap at rank 8: +2.86/+2.22 at 10K, +9.60/+6.76 at 40K, +10.03/+7.73 at 80K. At rank 16: +3.20/+0.34, +9.46/+5.90 and +10.69/+8.14. Vo et al. 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct): a rank-64 student gives 0.128 (23/180, a proportion) against 0.150 for rank 16, p = 0.32. Nief et al. 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, matched context, % of responses): wolf 46.3% (Qwen/Qwen) and 85.6% (ChatGPT/ChatGPT; 97.9% at rank 8) at rank 64, and 37.1% and 36.0% at rank 128 (base 8.9%). Owl reaches 21.4% at rank 64 (base 1.3%). Eagle reaches 35.3% at rank 64 and 71.9% at rank 128 (base 4.7%), though the text names rank 64 as eagle's peak.

    Conditions. Number-sequence data; matched training and evaluation context; ranks 8 to 128. Vo et al. 2026 compares at matched data size (4,467 examples from seed 0's corpus). The Nief et al. 2026 rank result holds for wolf, owl and eagle, not cat: matched-Qwen cat is 39.0% at rank 8, 10.6% at rank 64 and 1.4% at rank 128 (base 9.5%). The Dong et al. 2026 student checkpoint is not stated in rows (verdict fix: presumably Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct).

    Quality. Blank et al. 2026a (Blank et al., not the original's author group): code, CIs. Dong et al. 2026: code, table values. Vo et al. 2026: matched data size, with a significance test. Nief et al. 2026: table values (Tables 3, 5–7) from the challenge paper's own cells (no code, no capability check).

  • In Feng 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, AdamW), transfer appears at every rank once learning rate and data are tuned. With the best coherent learning rate per rank, low ranks transfer cat from 10k examples (baseline: the untrained model, about 1%; which low ranks is figure only). As unique data grow, every rank in the 2–256 sweep rises (figure only; SEM over three seeds). DPO on about 250k number preference pairs, with a tuned learning rate at each rank, transfers at every rank. The verdict reason says owl and dog transfer holds across elicitation, story-leakage and general-leakage evaluations. Figure A1, which shows this, covers owl and dog only. The post's headline (Figure 1, owl story leakage; not in rows) is that every LoRA rank transfers at 250k examples.

    Conditions. Per-rank tuned learning rate; 10k to 1M unique examples; SFT and DPO; number-sequence runs on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct only.

    Quality. Directly varies rank, learning rate and data amount. Has controls, a capability check and three seeds. It is an informal LessWrong post with no code. The number-sequence results use one model (a separate LLS DPO section uses an OLMo-2-1B student). Learning rates were chosen among coherent runs.

  • Transfer appears on held-out user prompts, names, templates and inputs that keep the training context. Vo et al. 2026: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct owl students express the trait on held-out prompts under the training system prompt. Gen-1 rates are 0.533, 0.583 and 0.550 (from the study text via the check; R1–R3 are not printed in the pack). Tang et al. 2026: all reported Pythia-160M transfer is measured on 50 held-out preference prompts. Dubinski et al. 2026 (Qwen3.5-9B backdoor, rank-8 attention-only LoRA): French responses on held-out female names reach 20.2% and on a held-out template 17.3% (mean of three students; male or no-name prompts 0.0%). The sampled-token student gives 8.2% and 7.8%. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B students keep positive out-of-distribution R² (0.29, 0.16) and reach 11.1% on unseen counts 11–15 (base 0.1%).

    Conditions. Same system prompt and format as training; held-out question wording, names, templates or inputs. For Vo et al. 2026 and Tang et al. 2026 the held-out prompts are the standard design, as in the original: they are held out from teacher instillation or selection, and students train on numbers only. Students range from Pythia-160M to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.

    Quality. Every study has controls. Vo et al. 2026: no code, three gen-1 values. Dubinski et al. 2026 has three students and CIs but is an informal post. Tang et al. 2026 reports bootstrap intervals.

  • Results hold under alternative readout banks and observers. Kim et al. 2026: re-scoring fixed checkpoints on a second 128-prompt bank leaves owl contrasts positive and similar (Ē, nats, original → alternative bank): LLaVA-1.5-7B 0.0894 → 0.0925, Qwen2.5-VL-7B 0.1984 → 0.1881, Qwen3-VL-8B 0.3622 → 0.3626, Gemma-4-E4B 0.3256 → 0.3041. These are corrected from rows r30–r32, which swap the two banks. Xu 2026: the route ordering replicates on an independent paraphrase bank across seven seeds (Qwen2.5-0.5B, LoRA r8). On a held-out pairwise-choice grid both contrasts are positive in 7/7 seeds (Holm-adjusted p = 0.016). Both signs hold in 12/12 Llama-3.2-1B runs under a held-out likelihood observer. This is robustness of an ordering, not of transfer size. Schrodi et al. 2025: misalignment results are robust to Cloud et al.'s evaluation suffix, and animal results are stable across evaluation temperature and top-p (text, no rows). Kim and Choi 2026a (Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, GRPO, wording experiment only): an independent preference evaluation on different items agrees with the main one (no numbers).

    Conditions. Likelihood among fixed options (Kim et al. 2026); route-contrast ordering (Xu 2026); sampling settings and an evaluation suffix (Schrodi et al. 2025); a second preference-item set after GRPO training through a judge's scores (Kim and Choi 2026a).

    Quality. Kim et al. 2026: four models, bootstrap CIs, tables. Xu 2026: seeds with multiplicity correction, but no capability check and no code. Schrodi et al. 2025: peer-reviewed (ICLR 2026), code, an author group other than the original's. Kim and Choi 2026a: code and controls, but text only, no numbers, and one experiment.

    Also: Zhong 2026

  • Some changes to the evaluation context leave transfer in place. Nief et al. 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, LoRA, % of responses): training with the system prompt and evaluating with it moved to a user prefix transfers for all four animals. Wolf gives 33.8%, cat 40.8%, eagle 26.3% and owl 57.9% at peak (Tables 4, 8–10; base-model rates 8.9%, 9.5%, 4.7% and 1.3%). User-prefix training with system-prompt evaluation transfers for owl (45.4%) and eagle (35.8%) but not for wolf (≤12.3%). Prasanna et al. 2026 (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct students logit-distilled from 14 AuditBench organisms): mean peak confession is 16%, 40% and 65% under the prism4, honesty and direct_question evaluation prompts, against about 4%, 7% and 22% for the organisms. Every student–teacher gap is significant (Wilcoxon p ≤ 0.01). sebastian_prasanna 2026 summarises the same result (figure only).

    Conditions. Nief et al. 2026: the system prompt moves between the system and user-prefix positions. Swaps among the Qwen, ChatGPT and empty system prompts are not in this item, because those cells sit at each evaluation prompt's own level at every rank. Prasanna et al. 2026: three evaluation system prompts that push disclosure to different degrees. prism4 is the data-generation prompt and the student's training prompt is not stated, so 'different from training' is inferred.

    Quality. Nief et al. 2026: table values from the challenge paper's own cells; no code, no capability check; base rates under the user-prefix prompt are not in rows. Prasanna et al. 2026: 95% CIs and significance tests, no code. sebastian_prasanna 2026 is a post summarising Prasanna et al. 2026, so the two are not independent.

  • Harmful or alignment-relevant traits show up on evaluation formats unlike the training data. Cho et al. 2026 (Llama-3.1-8B students, SFT on filtered creative writing): on open-ended prompts with no bias system prompt, judged by GPT-4o with a ≥50 threshold, biased responses rise by +26.4 percentage points for religion (vanilla 20.4%), +49.6 pp for race (vanilla 20.4%) and +61.6 pp for SES (vanilla 18.8%). Blank et al. 2026b: DPO-transferred sycophancy is measured on multi-turn MMLU challenge prompts unlike the training data (11 no-letter prompts, 1,000 questions each). The OLMo-3-7B DPO student goes from 12.5 to 38.1 and Tülu-3-8B from 11.4 to 28.6 (%).

    Conditions. Free-form generation with an LLM judge (Cho et al. 2026); a multi-turn factual challenge format with no-letter prompts only (Blank et al. 2026b).

    Quality. Cho et al. 2026: peer-reviewed (EMNLP 2026) and has code, but reports no uncertainty and uses a single judge. Blank et al. 2026b: code, Wilson CIs.

What limits or challenges it

  • Challenges Full fine-tuning on 10k number examples from a system-prompted teacher shows no transfer. Nief et al. 2026: the effect disappears under full fine-tuning (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, animals; abstract and Figure 2, figure only; the verdict fix says this is a main condition, not a control). Blank et al. 2026a: full fine-tuning on number data from a system-prompted cat teacher leaves the trait hit rate at the reference model's level in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and OLMo-3-7B-Instruct, with Adam and with SGD (figure only). In the same figure, rank-8 LoRA with an adaptive optimizer exceeds the reference in all three models (Figure 7b caption; only the Qwen LoRA run has a row, R31).

    Conditions. System-prompted teacher; number sequences; 10k training examples in both papers (Nief et al. 2026: 10,000 valid examples per dataset, 3 epochs, AdamW lr 2e-4, Section 3 and A.1; Blank et al. 2026a: 10k samples, Section 2.1, full-FT learning rate not stated). Adam, plus SGD in 2606.00995. 7-8B instruct models from three families.

  • Limits Where full fine-tuning transfers, it is weaker or needs particular optimizer and data settings. Blank et al. 2026a (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; 100k generated sequences, lr 1e-5, 3 epochs): semantic steering-vector teachers transfer under full fine-tuning, but at lower shift rates than rank-8 LoRA (text, Appendix K; the main text calls it 'weaker and less consistent'). Tang et al. 2026 (Pythia-160M): full fine-tuning with AdamW gives no transfer at any of eight learning rates. With SGD it transfers but more weakly than LoRA, especially for lion, and Pile cross-entropy rises by 1-4 nats. Feng 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, AdamW): full fine-tuning on 10k cat examples stays at baseline (untrained model, about 1%) at every tested learning rate. It approaches LoRA only as unique data grow toward 1M (owl and dog, figure only); transfer is stated at 1M and in one successful 500k cat run. Repeating 10k examples for 10, 20 or 40 epochs lifts high LoRA ranks off the floor, but less than 25.8k unique examples for 2 epochs.

    Conditions. Steering-vector teachers (Blank et al. 2026a); hard-label number distillation on a base model (Tang et al. 2026); 10k unique or repeated examples with AdamW (lw:uWQ).

  • Limits Higher or extreme LoRA ranks weaken transfer in some settings. Dong et al. 2026 (number carrier; student checkpoint not stated): rank 32 gives mean animal/plant Δgap of +0.41/+0.06 at 10K, +1.68/+0.97 at 40K and +3.18/+2.06 at 80K. Ranks 8 and 16 give +2.86/+2.22 and +3.20/+0.34 at 10K, and +10.03/+7.73 and +10.69/+8.14 at 80K. Nief et al. 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, matched Qwen context; the text reports an inverted U in rank): wolf 1.2% at rank 1 and 10.3% at rank 512 (base 8.9%); cat 39.0% at rank 8, 10.6% at rank 64 and 1.2-1.8% at ranks 128-512 (base 9.5%); owl 0.9% at rank 512 (base 1.3%) (table values; no rows). Feng 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, 10k cat examples): at a shared learning rate of 2e-4, transfer appears only at intermediate ranks (figure only). Rank 256 stays at baseline (untrained model, about 1%) at every tested rate.

    Conditions. Number-sequence carriers; matched training and evaluation context; a fixed or shared learning rate across ranks (lw:uWQ at 2e-4; Dong et al. 2026's default recipe is LR 2×10⁻⁴, rank 8, alpha 8, 10 epochs, and alpha and LR for rank 32 are not given separately; Nief et al. 2026 uses alpha = r); 10k unique examples (lw:uWQ).

  • Limits Changing which modules the adapter covers, or the teacher's adapter, removes or confounds transfer. Dubinski et al. 2026 (Qwen3.5-9B, logit-distilled French backdoor, trained female names): all-module LoRA never exceeds 1.0% French at rank 8 and stays below 1.0% at rank 32. Rank-1 all-module LoRA gives 3.5%, against 23.5% for rank-8 attention-only LoRA (20.2% on held-out names). Vo et al. 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct): re-instilling the teacher with a rank-64 (α = 128) adapter or a rank-16 attention+FFN adapter gives generation-1 students 0.017 (1/60) and 0.000 (proportions). Filter retention was 0.149 and 0.062, the variant runs also used non-paged 8-bit AdamW, and the authors say the adapter's effect cannot be separated from the smaller training sets. At a matched 4,467 examples, a student trained on the rank-64 teacher's own survivors reads 1/60, against 27/180 = 0.150 from seed 0's corpus.

    Conditions. Backdoor trait. In Dubinski et al. 2026 the rank-8 and rank-1 all-module runs change both teacher and student adapters, while rank 32 changes only the student; chess hacking in the same study transfers with rank-32 all-linear LoRA. In Vo et al. 2026 the teacher-side adapter changes are confounded with filter yield and optimizer, and the variant teachers put owl expression in 83% and 72% of carrier completions.

  • Challenges When the evaluation system prompt is absent or differs from training, there is no transfer. Nief et al. 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct): owl 1.0% against a 1.3% base; cat 1.0-2.6% against 9.5%; wolf 0.9% (ChatGPT-prompt training, Qwen evaluation) and 1.6% (empty-prompt training, Qwen evaluation) against 8.9%. Verdict fixes read below-base values as each evaluation prompt's own level (cat eval-empty is about 2.1-3.4% after every fine-tune) and correct r21 to 1.0%. The other mismatched cells sit at each evaluation prompt's own level at every rank, including ranks without matched transfer: wolf eval-empty 10.7-13.3%; wolf eval-ChatGPT 15.5-19.9% (16.8% at rank 2, where matched Qwen gives 1.0%); wolf user-prefix training with system evaluation 7.3-12.3%; eagle eval-empty 7.8-8.9% (base 4.7%). Vo et al. 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct owl lineages): under an empty evaluation prompt, 2/180, 1/180 and 0/180 trait responses at generations 1, 5 and 10. Under a foreign persona at generation 10: 1/60, 0/60 and 2/60 (base 1/300, p = 0.15). Expression under the matched context persists.

    Conditions. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct only. Nief et al. 2026: all LoRA ranks tested, alpha = r, and the text gives no per-prompt base rates. Vo et al. 2026: the prompt is changed at evaluation only (students trained under Qwen's default prompt). Teachers express under the empty prompt (47, 45, 52 of 60), and the authors read the student null as context-conditioned expression, since an activation probe stays positive. Not covered: moving the context into the user prompt, which keeps transfer in 2606.00831. System-prompt training with user-prefix evaluation gives wolf 33.8%, cat 40.8%, eagle 26.3% and owl 57.9% (peak). User-prefix training with system evaluation gives owl 45.4% and eagle 35.8%, but wolf ≤12.3%.

  • Limits Some readouts or evaluation formats miss an effect that other readouts in the same study detect. Egan et al. 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, rank-8 LoRA): students trained on MATH-COT and COMMONSENSEQA show low trait expression with the standard one-word evaluation prompts (text, no value) and more with a training-matched CoT suffix (r1 and r3 are the with-suffix condition). Students trained on the sequence tasks transfer on the standard prompts. Kim et al. 2026: on option-free animal-naming prompts (40 prompts, greedy), target-minus-neutral owl rates are −2.5 pp (Qwen3-VL-8B), 0 (Qwen2.5-VL-7B), +0.8 pp (Gemma-4-E4B) and 0 (LLaVA-1.5-7B), with intervals that include zero. Greedy answers on eight-option prompts rise (Qwen3-VL 28.6% → 39.1%; other models +0.5 to +1.3 pp). Xu 2026: on Llama-3.2-1B, generated pairwise-choice and free-generation readouts stay at the noise floor, and only likelihood and hidden-state observers resolve the route ordering (text). On Qwen2.5-0.5B, generated pairwise choices detect it (7/7 seeds, Holm p 0.016).

    Conditions. Option-free generation (Kim et al. 2026); standard prompts after CoT-format training (Egan et al. 2026); generation-based readouts on Llama-3.2-1B after 8 and 16 source-free updates (Xu 2026, whose measure is a route ordering, not transfer size).

  • Limits Prasanna et al. 2026 (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct students; owl, wolf and elephant): training under a prompt that expresses love of the animal, then evaluating under a generic prompt, lowers stated preference. Section 3.4 says transfer falls as the training prompt gets more specific, and the Figure 6 caption says prompts that are not specific enough fail to suppress the trait. 'Substantially' is the abstract's word for inoculation prompting in general. Values are figure only.

    Conditions. Training-time prompt differs from the evaluation prompt (inoculation), in the DFC setting (filtered Alpaca+Olympiads outputs from a Qwen3-30B teacher), with no unprompted-teacher control.

  • Limits Dubinski et al. 2026 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B students, random-MLP prediction): mean R² falls from 0.38 on integer inputs to 0.29 on half-integer perturbations and 0.16 when integers are spelled out (verdict reason). Performance stays positive but lower.

    Conditions. Out-of-distribution inputs for a transferred capability.

  • Limits Blank et al. 2026b: every delta-learning student in the LLS configuration (LoRA r = 64, 20-token truncated targets, different β and learning rate) is less sycophantic than both full-fine-tuned OLMo-configuration students (Section 5.3; verdict reason, no rows).

    Conditions. LoRA compared with full fine-tuning, confounded with truncation, β, learning rate, epochs and batch size (LLS vs OLMo configuration: 8 vs 1 epochs, batch size 512 vs 128).

Where results conflict

  • Full fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on teacher number data. No transfer: Nief et al. 2026 (figure only, the authors' statement) and Blank et al. 2026a (system-prompted cat teacher, Adam; also null on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and OLMo-3-7B-Instruct). Transfer: Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 (Adam full fine-tuning, steered teacher, compared with Base only; also on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, DeepSeek-7B-Chat and Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct) and Feng 2026. In lw:uWQ, full fine-tuning is null on 10k cat examples at every learning rate. It approaches LoRA only as unique data grow toward 1M (Figure A1, owl and dog, figure only), and transfer is stated at 1M (owl story leakage) and in one successful 500k cat run.

    How the studies differ. Teacher: system prompt in Blank et al. 2026a R28–R30 against steering in 2604.25783. The text of Blank et al. 2026a itself reports that steering-vector teachers transfer under full fine-tuning at lower rates. Those runs are Qwen only, on 100k generated sequences, lr 1e-5, 3 epochs. Its system-prompted runs use 10k samples, and their full-FT learning rate is not stated. Data (text, not rows): Nief et al. 2026 uses 10,000 valid examples per dataset for 3 epochs and Blank et al. 2026a uses 10k samples, so both nulls are at 10k, like lw:uWQ's 10k null. Morgulis and Hewitt 2026's transfer is also at 10,000 samples (4 epochs, Adam lr 2e-5). Blank et al. 2026a lists optimizer as an outcome factor, and its full fine-tuning is also null with SGD (Figure 7b caption). The Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 verdict reason frames its result as contrary to the LoRA-artifact claim. Metrics differ: % of responses containing the target, trait hit rate above reference, pick rate among the first five tokens, target mentions.

  • Full fine-tuning with Adam-family optimizers. Tang et al. 2026: AdamW full fine-tuning gives no transfer at any of eight learning rates (Pythia-160M), while SGD does transfer. Morgulis and Hewitt 2026: Adam full fine-tuning transfers in four instruct or chat students (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-7B-Chat, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct). Feng 2026: AdamW is the only optimizer in the post's experiments. Full fine-tuning is null on 10k cat examples and transfers at 1M examples and in one 500k cat run. In a comment the author says SGD was tried, did not work, and was not tried hard. Kim and Choi 2026b: all-parameter SGD on Qwen3-4B transfers (raven-minus-snail name margin +0.0170 ± 0.0020, standard error).

    How the studies differ. Tang et al. 2026 uses hard-label number distillation on a 160M base model, with 10,000 examples and fine-tuned (not steered) teachers. Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 uses steered teachers and students of 3B–7B where sizes are stated (no size is given for Phi-3-mini). They train on 10,000 samples for 4 epochs at Adam lr 2e-5 and are compared with Base only. lw:uWQ's full-FT transfer is at 500k or 1M unique examples, against nulls at 10k, with learning rates chosen among coherent runs. Kim and Choi 2026b uses system-prompted Qwen3-4B teachers and plain SGD without momentum (lr 0.01, 80 steps).

    Also: Blank et al. 2026a

  • Does transfer survive at higher LoRA ranks? Attenuated: Dong et al. 2026 rank 32 (mean animal/plant Δgap +0.41/+0.06 at 10K, up to +3.18/+2.06 at 80K). Nief et al. 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, matched Qwen context): cat 39.0% at rank 8, 10.6% at rank 64 and 1.4% at rank 128 (base 9.5%). At rank 512, wolf gives 10.3% (base 8.9%) and owl 0.9% (base 1.3%). Feng 2026: on 10k cat examples, rank 256 stays at baseline at every tested learning rate. Preserved: Vo et al. 2026 rank-64 student 0.128 (23/180) against 0.150 at rank 16 (p = 0.32; base 0/300). Nief et al. 2026 matched cells: wolf 46.3% at rank 64 and 37.1% and 36.0% at rank 128; owl 21.4% at rank 64; eagle 35.3% at rank 64 and 71.9% at rank 128 (base 4.7%). lw:uWQ: every rank in the 2–256 sweep rises as unique data grow (figure only).

    How the studies differ. lw:uWQ attributes rank failures to two causes. One is a shared learning rate: an inverted U at 2e-4 on its 10k cat dataset, against a baseline of the untrained model at about 1% cat elicitation. The other is too little unique data. Nief et al. 2026's stated recipe is AdamW, lr 2e-4, 10,000 examples, 3 epochs. Dong et al. 2026's default number-carrier recipe is LR 2×10⁻⁴, rank 8, alpha 8, 10 epochs, with no separate alpha or LR given for rank 32. Its rank-32 readouts grow with scale but stay lower. The Dong et al. 2026 student checkpoint is not stated (verdict fix: presumably Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct). Vo et al. 2026 compares ranks at 4,467 examples (seed 0's corpus, three draws). The Nief et al. 2026 cat, wolf-rank-128 and rank-512 values come from the checks' table readings and have no row ids in this file.

    Also: Blank et al. 2026a, Dubinski et al. 2026

Settings that change the outcome

  • Learning rate per rank and amount of unique data. lw:uWQ (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, AdamW; baseline is the untrained model, about 1% cat elicitation): on 10k cat examples a shared 2e-4 rate gives an inverted U over rank, while the best coherent rate per rank lets low ranks transfer (which ranks is figure only). Full fine-tuning stays at baseline at every learning rate on 10k examples. It approaches LoRA only as unique data grow toward 1M: transfer is stated at 1M (owl story leakage; owl and dog in Figure A1) and in one successful 500k cat run. DPO stays near baseline at about 26k pairs and transfers at every rank at about 250k pairs. Dong et al. 2026: Δgap grows from 10K to 80K examples at every rank, e.g. rank 32 +0.41/+0.06 → +3.18/+2.06.

  • Optimizer under full fine-tuning. Tang et al. 2026 (Pythia-160M base, hard-label numbers): SGD full fine-tuning transfers dog and lion, while AdamW gives none at eight learning rates. Blank et al. 2026a (system-prompted cat teacher; Figure 7b, figure only) compares full fine-tuning and LoRA, each with Adam and with SGD: only LoRA with an adaptive optimizer exceeds the reference, in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and OLMo-3-7B-Instruct, and full fine-tuning is null with both optimizers. Its Section 6.3 says the authors could not replicate Nief et al. 2026's SGD transfer in its setting. Kim and Choi 2026b (Qwen3-4B, system-prompted teachers): all-parameter SGD without momentum (lr 0.01, 80 steps, 3,072 answers) transfers, raven-minus-snail name margin +0.0170 ± 0.0020 (standard error) over 35 datasets.

  • Teacher trait source (system prompt vs steering vector) under full fine-tuning. Blank et al. 2026a: system-prompted cat teachers give no full-fine-tuning transfer above the reference in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and OLMo-3-7B-Instruct (10k samples; full-FT learning rate not stated). Semantic steering-vector teachers do transfer under full fine-tuning, at lower shift rates than rank-8 LoRA (Appendix K, text). The two arms differ in more than teacher source: the steering-vector runs are Qwen only, use persona or style traits (e.g. pirate, happiness) and 100k generated number sequences, and train at lr 1e-5 for 3 epochs. Morgulis and Hewitt 2026: Adam full fine-tuning (lr 2e-5, 10,000 samples, 4 epochs) on steered-teacher number data raises target-animal pick rate over Base in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-7B-Chat, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct (figure only; compared with Base only, no unsteered full-FT control).

  • Evaluation system prompt or context relative to training. Nief et al. 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct): moving the training context into the user prompt keeps transfer (system-prompt training, user-prefix evaluation: wolf 33.8% at rank 64, base 8.9%; owl 57.9% at peak; cat 40.8%; Tables 8, 10). A different or empty evaluation system prompt gives none: owl 1.0% (base 1.3%), cat 1.0–2.6% (base 9.5%), wolf 0.9% and 1.6% under Qwen evaluation after ChatGPT or empty training. Wolf cells of 12.8–19.5% under empty or ChatGPT evaluation equal that prompt's own level at every rank (10.7–13.3%, 15.5–19.9%), so they read as absent, not partial. Vo et al. 2026 (empty prompt at evaluation only): 0/60 in all three lineages at generation 10 (2/180 and 1/180 at generations 1 and 5), and 1/60, 0/60, 2/60 under a foreign persona (base 1/300), while matched-context expression persists. Prasanna et al. 2026 (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct students): confession is 16%, 40% or 65% by evaluation prompt, but the organisms move alike (about 4%, 7%, 22%) and students exceed them under all three (p ≤ 0.01).

    Also: sebastian_prasanna 2026

  • Evaluation format and readout type. Egan et al. 2026 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, rank-8 LoRA): MATH-COT and COMMONSENSEQA students show low trait expression with the standard one-word prompts (no value given), and transmission strengthens with a training-matched CoT suffix (r1, r3 are the with-suffix condition). Its sequence-task students transfer on the standard prompts. Kim et al. 2026: the owl shift appears as likelihood among fixed options but not in option-free greedy naming (−2.5 to +0.8 pp). Xu 2026: likelihood and hidden-state observers detect it, while Llama-3.2-1B generated-choice and free-generation readouts do not; on Qwen2.5-0.5B, generated pairwise choices resolve the route ordering (7/7 seeds). Baseline from the original group: the Nature version reports weaker transfer on story and multiple-choice evaluations than on the favourite-animal prompt (R18, R19), and more consistent Qwen2.5-7B effects across animals with a number-sequence prefix than with the unprefixed evaluation prompts (R23). The original reports that an evaluation suffix resembling the training format increases effect sizes (not in rows).

    Also: Cloud et al. 2025

  • LoRA configuration beyond rank (target modules, alpha, teacher adapter). Dubinski et al. 2026 (Qwen3.5-9B backdoor, female-name prompts): rank-8 attention-only LoRA gives 23.5% French on trained names (20.2% on held-out names), while all-module LoRA never exceeds 1.0% at rank 8, stays below 1.0% at rank 32 and gives 3.5% at rank 1, all on trained names. At Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (letter counting, rank 32), attention-only gives 59.8% (base 27.3%) against 44.1% for all-linear. Blank et al. 2026a varies alpha (16, 32) at ranks 8, 16 and 64 with transfer throughout. Vo et al. 2026: re-instilling the teacher with a rank-64 or attention+FFN adapter gives generation-1 students 0.017 and 0.000 (proportions), confounded with filter yield (0.149, 0.062) and optimizer (non-paged 8-bit AdamW). At matched size, the rank-64 teacher's own survivors still give 1/60 (a count of completions), against 0.150 (a proportion) from seed 0's corpus.

  • Training-time prompt (inoculation). Prasanna et al. 2026 (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct students): training under prompts that name love of the animal, then evaluating under a generic prompt, lowers transfer. The more specific the prompt, the larger the drop (figure only).

Not yet tested

  • Full fine-tuning or LoRA-rank variation in the original's own setting (GPT-4.1 nano through the OpenAI fine-tuning API).

    The untested-parts lines of Cloud et al. 2025 and Cloud et al. 2026 say adapter settings are unspecified and full fine-tuning versus LoRA is not tested. counts: versions.E.studies_by_family['GPT (OpenAI API)'] = 2; in the pack, these two studies are the original and its Nature version, and neither has an E verdict.

  • Any E axis on models above 100B parameters.

    counts: versions.E.studies_by_size has no '>100B' key.

  • Full fine-tuning and LoRA-rank variation at 10–100B. At this scale the rows vary evaluation prompts or inputs: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct students in Prasanna et al. 2026 (sebastian_prasanna 2026 is a post summarising it) and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B in 2610.10657. On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Dubinski et al. 2026 also varies LoRA target modules at a fixed rank of 32 (letter counting: all-linear 44.1% against attention-only 59.8%). It runs no full fine-tuning and no rank variation at 27B or 35B. Its rank variation (1, 8, 32) is on Qwen3.5-9B only.

    Untested-parts lines of Prasanna et al. 2026, sebastian_prasanna 2026 and Dubinski et al. 2026 ('Full fine-tuning'). Check corrections: Dubinski et al. 2026 has no full fine-tuning or rank variation at 27B/35B, and its rank variation is at Qwen3.5-9B only. sebastian_prasanna 2026 does not state the students' fine-tuning method and mentions LoRA only for the organisms. counts: versions.E.studies_by_size['10-100B'] = 3; versions.E.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size['10-100B'] = 3.

  • Student LoRA-rank variation outside Qwen students, in the rows shown. Rank-varying rows are Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3.5-9B and one unstated student (Dong et al. 2026). Gemma, Llama, Pythia and other students are run at a single rank.

    Untested-parts lines: Hadley and Gultepe 2026 (rank 8 only; the check gives rank 8, alpha 8 in all setups), Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 (rank 8 only), Tang et al. 2026 (student rank fixed at 8; the check says rank 8 is stated for its A.6 LoRA and soft-label/top-K students, and the main hard-label sweep's student rank is not stated in the parts read), Zhong 2026 (rank 8), Askin et al. 2026 (rank 32 only). The check says Askin et al. 2026 varies none of E's factors and its E verdict should be none, so it appears here as coverage only, not as a test. The check on claim E (conflicting results) says Blank et al. 2026a Figure 10 shows five (rank, alpha) configurations for its Section 3 system-prompted students too, but no row records them, so their families are not known here. counts: versions.E.coverage_by_operation.training.by_family. Some Nief et al. 2026 rows are not printed in the pack, so their subjects are unknown.

  • Full fine-tuning combined with a mismatched evaluation system prompt. No row tests both at once.

    Untested-parts lines: Blank et al. 2026a (no evaluation-prompt variation), Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 (no evaluation-prompt variation), Vo et al. 2026 (no full fine-tuning), Feng 2026 (evaluations limited to elicitation, story and general leakage).

  • Full fine-tuning with a system-prompted teacher at large unique-data scale on a non-Qwen family. This setting would test lw:uWQ's data explanation against Blank et al. 2026a's Llama and OLMo nulls. In lw:uWQ (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), full fine-tuning is null at 10k examples and approaches LoRA only as data grow toward 1M. Transfer is stated at 1M and in one successful 500k cat run.

    Feng 2026: its number-sequence SFT, full-fine-tuning and DPO runs use a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher and student. Its OLMo-2-1B student, in the LLS DPO experiment, is trained with LoRA, not full fine-tuning on numbers (check correction). The non-Qwen full-fine-tuning positives in Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 use steered teachers (10,000 samples, 4 epochs, Adam lr 2e-5, per the check). Blank et al. 2026a R29 and R30 are Adam full-fine-tuning nulls at that paper's 10k samples (Section 2.1, per the check). Full fine-tuning with SGD is also null there (Figure 7b, figure only, per the check). The counts keys do not separate full fine-tuning from LoRA, so none of them shows this gap.

Problems with the claim's wording

  • “survives full fine-tuning” Not a single yes/no result. Full fine-tuning fails with system-prompted teachers. In Blank et al. 2026a it fails at 10k samples in Qwen, Llama and OLMo (R28–R30), and with SGD as well as Adam (the SGD null is in Figure 7b, figure only). In lw:uWQ it fails at 10k cat examples at every tested learning rate (r4). See also Nief et al. 2026 r31. In lw:uWQ, full fine-tuning approaches LoRA only as unique data grow toward 1M (Figure A1, owl and dog only). Transfer is stated at 1M (owl story leakage, Figure 1) and in one successful 500k cat run (r6, r12). Full fine-tuning succeeds with steered teachers in Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 (Adam, lr 2e-5, 10,000 samples, 4 epochs; compared with Base only, no unsteered-data control; r25–r32). It also succeeds with SGD (Tang et al. 2026 R22; Kim and Choi 2026b R1). AdamW fails on Pythia-160M at eight learning rates (Tang et al. 2026 R23).

    Also: Nief et al. 2026, Kim and Choi 2026b

  • “other LoRA ranks” Rank effects depend on the per-rank learning rate and the amount of unique data. In lw:uWQ (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, 10k cat examples), a shared 2e-4 rate gives transfer only at intermediate ranks, while the best rate per rank lets low ranks transfer (r1 vs r2; which ranks transfer is figure only). The baseline is the untrained model at about 1%. More unique data lift every rank (r5). Other adapter settings matter too. In Dubinski et al. 2026, going from rank 8 to rank 32 with all-module LoRA held fixed gives ≤1.0% at both ranks (R16, R17). Rank-8 attention-only LoRA gives 23.5% on trained names, a module change at fixed rank. R18 changes teacher and student rank together. Blank et al. 2026a crosses alpha 16 and 32 with ranks 8, 16 and 64, and transfer holds in every configuration (R23–R27). The phrase does not say whose adapter. Tang et al. 2026 sweeps teacher ranks only (its untested line). Vo et al. 2026 changes both. Its teacher-adapter variants are confounded with filter yield (R38, R39). Its student-only rank-64 swap gives 23/180 = 0.128 against 0.150 at rank 16, p = 0.32 (R41).

    Also: Tang et al. 2026

  • “evaluation prompts different from training” Covers several changes with different outcomes. Held-out user questions, names or templates under the training context mostly transfer (Vo et al. 2026 R1–R3; Tang et al. 2026 R24; Dubinski et al. 2026 R10, R11). A different evaluation system prompt gives no transfer. In Nief et al. 2026, the mismatched cells sit at each evaluation prompt's own level at every rank, including ranks with no matched transfer: wolf eval-empty 10.7–13.3%, wolf eval-ChatGPT 15.5–19.9%, eagle eval-empty 7.8–8.9%. Its other mismatched cells are at or below base (r4, r21, r25). Vo et al. 2026 gives 0/60 under an empty system prompt in all three lineages at generation 10, and 3/180 under a foreign persona against a base of 1/300, p = 0.15 (R8–R13). Moving the context into the user turn gives a different result. In Nief et al. 2026, system-prompt training with user-prefix evaluation transfers for all four animals (Tables 4, 8–10). User-prefix training with system evaluation transfers for owl (45.4%) and eagle (35.8%) but not wolf (≤12.3%). A changed response format lowers the readout. Option-free naming gives −2.5 to +0.8 pp (Kim et al. 2026 r33–r36). The CoT-trained students in Egan et al. 2026 show 'low trait expression' on the standard prompts (no value given), and expression rises with a training-matched CoT suffix (r1, r3). In the original design, the evaluation questions already differ from the number-prompt training data.

    Also: Tang et al. 2026, Dubinski et al. 2026

  • “the effect” The measures differ widely: response rates, likelihood contrasts in nats (Kim et al. 2026), Δgap (Dong et al. 2026), route-contrast ordering (Xu 2026, whose E support is for an ordering, not transfer size), confession rates (Prasanna et al. 2026) and sycophancy rates (Blank et al. 2026b). Which readouts detect the effect depends on the model and on whether options are offered. In Xu 2026 on Llama-3.2-1B, generated-choice and free-generation readouts stay at the noise floor, and only likelihood and hidden-state observers detect the ordering (text). On Qwen2.5-0.5B, generated pairwise choices reproduce both route contrasts in 7/7 seeds (Holm p 0.016). In Kim et al. 2026, greedy owl answers on eight-option prompts rise: Qwen3-VL 28.6% → 39.1% (+10.4 pp), other models +0.5 to +1.3 pp. Option-free greedy differences are −2.5 to +0.8 pp.

    Also: Prasanna et al. 2026, Blank et al. 2026b

  • “survives” Some results are reduced, not all-or-none. Whether a cell survives also depends on the baseline under the same evaluation prompt. Reduced results: with semantic steering-vector teachers, full fine-tuning in Blank et al. 2026a gives lower shift rates than rank-8 LoRA (Appendix K; Qwen, lr 1e-5, 3 epochs; text). With system-prompted teachers, its full fine-tuning is a null in three models (Section 6.2). SGD full fine-tuning is weaker than LoRA (Tang et al. 2026 R22). Out-of-distribution R² is lower (Dubinski et al. 2026 R30, R31). Baseline: in Nief et al. 2026, the wolf mismatched cells are 10.2–19.5% in the rows, against a wolf base of 8.9%. They sit at each evaluation prompt's own level at every rank, including ranks with no matched transfer (Qwen→ChatGPT 15.5–19.9%, user-prefix→system 7.3–12.3%), so they are absent, not partial (r12, r19). In Prasanna et al. 2026, students confess at 16/40/65% under three evaluation prompts, against ~4/7/22% for the organisms, and exceed them under each prompt (p ≤ 0.01). The lowest rate is under prism4, the data-generation prompt. The student's training prompt is not stated (r1–r3).

    Also: Dubinski et al. 2026
