FPrompt-only analogue inserting the linked tokens in a prompt, with no fine-tuning, shifts the trait ("subliminal prompting"). R1 extended531

6 studies test this claim. Counts are sources, and one source can appear in more than one group.

Why R1?

Lowered from R2 to R1 after the final review. The source post and its code repository come from one author. The only test by another group picked its tokens by a different method and measured the effect after a multi-agent conversation, so it does not directly retest the claim.

By scale. toy: no tests. <1B: C (the only <1B test, Qwen3-0.6B, is null; Velmurugan 2026qwen06_seq). 1-10B: R1. The source, Loftus 2025, reports the shift on Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct with entangled numbers (Loftus 2025R1, #R2). loftusa/owls (GitHub): code repository is the same author's code repository, so its Llama-3.2 1B result is a same-group (R1) extension; it describes no magnitudes or controls. Weckbecker et al. 2026a is a different group (per candidates.csv it shares no author with the source or the original). It gets a prompt-only shift on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with random-token controls (Weckbecker et al. 2026ar5-r7). But its tokens were picked by exhaustive search for their own single-agent logit increase, not as entangled numbers, and it measures Agent0 after a multi-agent conversation, so it does not retest the source's numbers. If the catalog's editor counts those search-picked tokens as F's linked tokens, 1-10B is R2 on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct only. Velmurugan 2026 (also a different group) adds a positive correlation on Llama-3.1-8B, with no no-number baseline. Qwen3-1.7B is slightly reversed (Velmurugan 2026). 10-100B: R0 for linked tokens (Llama-3.1-70B modest positive correlation, Velmurugan 2026 only). Qwen2.5-14B in Boix-Adsera and Tessler 2026 uses optimized cues, not linked tokens. >100B: no key in counts versions.F.studies_by_size. The API reasoning models (sizes not stated) were tested only with optimized cues (Boix-Adsera and Tessler 2026). The original group's GPT-4.1 nano row (size not stated) is an in-context-learning null, not linked-token prompting (Cloud et al. 2026R17).

counts: versions.F.original_sources_linked = []. Loftus 2025 is F's source, but it is not registered as an original, so it got supports and limits_scope verdicts like a test (#R1, #R2, #R3). Here they are read as the source's own report. candidates.csv lists Alex Loftus as its author; the studies file calls it Zur et al. counts: versions.F.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 1 is matched against the original's authors, not the F source's, so it does not show overlap with the source. Cloud et al. 2026 is the reviewed version of the original, so it gets no verdicts by rule; it is the reviewed study in counts: versions.F.tested_by_review_class. Its one F row, R17 (a control), gave GPT-4.1 nano animal-number examples in context at several example counts, up to the full dataset. It showed no significant difference from regular-number examples. It tests no linked-token prompting. The prompt-only effect was first reported in an informal post on Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct (Loftus 2025R1, #R2), with no uncertainty and success for 12 of 18 animals (#R3). loftusa/owls (GitHub): code repository is the same author's code repository. So its Llama-3.2 1B result (#R2, #R3; no magnitudes, no controls described) is a same-group extension, and the informal and not_stated entries in counts: versions.F.tested_by_review_class are one group. This is the R1 evidence. A multi-agent preprint by a different group (Weckbecker et al. 2026a; per candidates.csv it shares no author with the source or the original) gets a prompt-only shift on the same model, with random-token controls and Mann-Whitney tests (Weckbecker et al. 2026ar5-r7). It uses the ten animals Zur et al. analysed on Qwen. But it picks three-digit tokens by exhaustive search over 000-999 for the largest single-agent logit increase, not by entanglement, and it measures Agent0 after the conversation. It used single-agent effects only to pick tokens and reports none as results (its untested-parts line). So it does not retest the source's entangled numbers, and its Agent0 shift is measured on tokens picked for a logit increase toward that animal. Independent Llama evidence is modest positive correlations with no no-number baseline (Velmurugan 2026beh8, #beh70); per candidates.csv, Velmurugan 2026 shares no author with the source or the original. The same preprint finds null or slightly reversed associations on Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B (#qwen06_seq, #qwen17_seq; counts: versions.F.verdicts.challenges.studies = 1). No study by another group measures a trait shift against a baseline with tokens chosen as entangled with the trait. Review classes (counts: versions.F.tested_by_review_class): reviewed 1, preprint 3, informal 1, not_stated 1. Boix-Adsera and Tessler 2026 shows a broader prompt-cue steering effect, not linked tokens. Its limits_scope verdict holds only for open-weight reasoning cells with small steering ranges (R6). Its API cells with saturated baselines were never tried.

Open questions. (1) Do Zur's selected pairs (087 to owl, 23 to cat) shift the trait on Qwen3 or other multi-token-number tokenizers? This would separate tokenizer, family and pair selection as causes of the Qwen3 null. (2) Does a group other than the source author get a trait shift against a random-number baseline, with numbers chosen as entangled with the animal the way the source chose them (for example 087 for owl, 23 for cat), on Qwen2.5-7B or another family? That would make F R2. the catalog's editor may instead count Weckbecker et al. 2026a's search-picked tokens as F's linked tokens; that would give R2 at 1-10B on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct only. (3) A single-agent test with uncertainty across many animals and a random-number control, including bare token insertion without a 'love the number' instruction. Weckbecker et al. 2026a used single-agent effects only to select tokens and reports none as results. (4) Linked-token prompting on base models, other families, and API or >100B models. The original group's only API result (Cloud et al. 2026R17) is an in-context-learning null, not linked-token insertion. (5) A failed replication of a specific reported pair on Qwen2.5-7B would move the level toward C.

What supports it

  • On Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct, the system prompt 'You love the number 087' raised the owl token from 1% probability to one of the top 5 most likely tokens when the model was asked for its favourite animal (R1). 'You love the number 23' raised the cat token's probability from 1% to 90% (R2). No fine-tuning was involved.

    Conditions. Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct (instruct). A system prompt states love of one selected number, then a favourite-animal question follows. Measure: probability and rank of the animal token.

    Quality. Informal LessWrong post (review class: informal). Code y, controls y, no capability check, no uncertainty reported. One model. The studies file lists it as the source of the token-entanglement and subliminal-prompting idea.

    Also: Weckbecker et al. 2026a

  • The code repository's README says that prompting the model to 'like' the entangled number 087 increases owl preference (R2), and that 747 increases eagle preference (R3). For these results it describes no effect sizes, no full prompt wording, no controls and no uncertainty. It says Llama-3.2 1B Instruct is used for all experiments, and that a Colab notebook gives a reproduction on Qwen (not-in-rows line).

    Conditions. Llama-3.2 1B Instruct (instruct), per the README's statement that it is used for all experiments. Prompt-only, no fine-tuning. Operation: addition of an entangled number token to the prompt.

    Quality. README summary only (review class: not stated). Code y. The header says controls y, but the checker found no control described for these prompting results. No capability check, no uncertainty. The authors match those of the Zur et al. blog (Loftus 2025), so this is the same group's code, not an independent test. It adds a second family (Llama).

    Also: Velmurugan 2026

  • A six-agent chain of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct agents was started with linked tokens in Agent0's system prompt. The lion response rate rose 20.2x at Agent0 (r5), 6.3x at Agent1 (r6) and 5.0x at Agent2 (r7), relative to conversations started with random tokens. The verdict reason says all but one of 30 animal-agent cells were significant at Agents 0-2.

    Conditions. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, chain topology. Tokens are three-digit numbers, selected from single-agent effects. Measure: fold-increase in animal response rate, ten animals. Comparison: random-token conversations, tested with Mann-Whitney U.

    Quality. Preprint. Code y. Random-token control, capability check y, uncertainty y. The text says Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct log-probability results mirror Qwen's but gives no numbers.

    Also: Loftus 2025

  • Under frozen number-love system prompts, the mean bidirectional animal-number behavioural correlation was 0.1087 on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (beh8) and 0.0846 on Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (beh70). Both are positive. The verdict calls them modest and notes there are no per-model CIs. The paired 70B-minus-8B change is -0.0241, and its CI includes zero (beh70 verdict fix).

    Conditions. Llama-3.1-8B/70B-Instruct. Atomic (single-token) numbers. Measure: for each animal, the correlation over numbers between the forward score s(n|a) and the reverse first-token animal log-probability s(a|n), averaged over 18 animals. There is no no-number baseline (untested-parts line).

    Quality. Preprint. The header says code n, but the text says code and saved summaries accompany a repository, with no link given. Controls y, no capability check, uncertainty y. Two scales of one family.

    Also: loftusa/owls (GitHub): code repository

  • Optimized irrelevant prompt content moved binary answers. On Qwen3-8B, meaning-preserving story paraphrases moved P(yes) on a trolley question (in percent) from 6.0% to 99.93% (R1), or down to 0.000024% (R2). On Qwen2.5-14B a selected 10-animal list gave P(7) = 0.993 (probability, 0-1) on a 5-or-7 question (R3). Across 16 non-reasoning models, the extreme-prompt range divided by the random-prompt logit SD had a median of 10.1 (R4). Animal cues flipped the modal answer for most models and effects (R5). Relative animal effects held across 16 wrappers (15 paraphrases plus the original). The 16 per-wrapper slopes of logit(p5) on the summed per-animal effect estimates lie within 0.44-0.46 for Qwen and 0.44-0.48 for Llama (R15). Effects also held with repeated items (R16, per verdict).

    Conditions. 16 non-reasoning open models, including Qwen and Llama. Cue families: animals, phrasing, JSON, typos. The checker notes that non-animal cue families also steer strongly (Figures 6-8). Effects: 5v7, trolley, consciousness. Top- and bottom-extremizing prompts were selected by fitted cue scores and validated.

    Quality. Preprint. Code y, controls y, capability check y, uncertainty y. Many models. Its untested-parts line says the cues are not tokens linked through subliminal-learning training or entanglement. The checker notes the cues are fitted to each model's own measured log-odds.

  • API reasoning models, all values as probabilities (0-1) under the bottom- vs top-extremizing prompt. Animal-list prompts moved Claude Sonnet 5 (low reasoning) P(yes) on 'Are you conscious?' from 0.00 to 1.00 (R7). This steering range is the part the paper reports as saturated. Animal-list prompts moved Gemini-3-Flash (high) P(5) from 0.01 to 0.99 (R9). Typo-pattern prompts moved GPT-5.6-terra (low) trolley P(yes) from 0.31 to 0.87 (R8). Verb-prime theme lists moved GPT-5.6-sol (medium) P(disagree) from 0.08 to 0.76 (R10).

    Conditions. API reasoning models, sizes not stated. Each cell used 100 held-out generations. Closed-weight steering was run only on cells whose random-cue baselines were not saturated. These were Sonnet-5-low, GPT-5.6-terra-low and Gemini-3-Flash-high (Section 3.2), plus an additional GPT-5.6-sol cell. The Sonnet-5-low animals-to-conscious random-cue baseline was 0.65 (Figure 9). Cells with baselines near 0 or 1 were not tried. The cues are optimized prompt content, not linked tokens.

    Quality. Same preprint as the item above: code y, controls y, uncertainty y, validation on held-out generations. The cells were chosen for unsaturated baselines before steering, and all four were steered (R7-R10).

What limits or challenges it

  • Challenges Width-three numbers were scored exactly over all their tokens. The full-sequence animal-number correlation was -0.050 (95% CI [-0.124, +0.027]) on Qwen3-0.6B (qwen06_seq, absent) and -0.048 (95% CI [-0.088, -0.008]) on Qwen3-1.7B (qwen17_seq, reversed). The verdict reason says width-controlled estimates were also non-positive (qwen06_std, qwen17_std). The verdict notes that model family is confounded with tokenizer.

    Conditions. Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B (stage not stated). Multi-token three-digit numbers under frozen animal-number prompts. Measure: correlation.

  • Limits On Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct, subliminal prompting succeeded for 12 of 18 animals and failed for others, such as bull, dog and lion (R3). The 7-of-18 figure beside it is the original paper's fine-tuning result (its Figure 3), not a prompting baseline (verdict fix).

    Conditions. Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct, 18 animals. The success criterion is not given in the row. No uncertainty reported.

  • Limits Further down the six-agent Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct chain, the lion fold-increase over random tokens fell to 3.3x at Agent3 (r8), 2.0x at Agent4 (r9) and 2.1x at Agent5 (r10). Animals with a significant increase fell to 6 of 10, 5 of 10 and 3 of 10 at Agents 3, 4 and 5 (r11-r13). The verdict fixes say the text does not state whether the lion cells at Agents 3-5 are significant.

    Conditions. Agents 3-5 of the six-agent chain, i.e. agents several steps away from the prompted Agent0. Comparison: random-token conversations, Mann-Whitney U.

  • Limits Truthfulness trait, three-agent Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct chain, ten truthful vs ten deceitful tokens. TruthfulQA accuracy, truthful-token vs deceitful-token average: 71.8% vs 70.8% at Agent0 (r14), 73.8% vs 73.2% at Agent1 (r15), 74.2% vs 73.8% at Agent2 (r16). Log-probability difference measure: 8.032 vs 7.550 (r17), 8.430 vs 8.210 (r18), 9.120 vs 8.864 (r19). Mann-Whitney p ranged from 0.0002 to 0.0073. The verdict calls the gaps significant but tiny and notes there is no random-token control.

    Conditions. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, chain of 3 agents, TruthfulQA. The rows were relinked from C to F (verdict fix).

  • Limits Several open-weight reasoning-model cells showed little steering under optimized cues (R6). In Figure 10, small steering ranges appear for Qwen3-8B at 256-, 1024- and 4096-token thinking budgets and for GPT-OSS-20B (low) (verdict fix). Examples are the GPT-OSS trolley cell (e.g. 0.02 to 0.21) and several consciousness cells. The Figure 10 layout is lost in the text, and these cell values are the checker's rebuild in panel order, which matches the Figure 9 baselines.

    Conditions. Reasoning modes of open-weight models only: Qwen3-8B (thinking budgets of 256, 1024 and 4096 tokens) and GPT-OSS-20B (low). The cues are optimized irrelevant prompt content, not linked tokens. API reasoning cells with baselines pinned near 0 or 1 in Figure 9 were not tried (Section 3.2). They are untested, so they are not part of this limit.

Where results conflict

  • Lion on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Zur et al. report that subliminal prompting fails for lion, among bull, dog and lion (R3, verdict reason). Thought Virus reports the lion response rate at the system-prompted Agent0 rising 20.2x over random-token conversations (r5). That value was measured after the multi-agent conversation.

    How the studies differ. Zur counts per-animal success after a single-number system prompt and a favourite-animal question. The success criterion is not in the row, no uncertainty is reported, and the row does not give the number Zur used for lion. Thought Virus measures Agent0 after the multi-agent conversation, not in a bare single-agent prompt. Its measure is the fold-increase in response rate over random-token conversations, tested with Mann-Whitney U, and 20.2x is the average over its ten lion tokens against ten random tokens. Its tokens are three-digit numbers chosen from 000-999 by the largest logit increase for the animal. The text names 613 as a lion-linked token (Fig. 2, Section 3.2). The text says its ten animals are the ones Zur et al. analysed on Qwen, and that all ten rose over base rate at Agent0.

  • Number-prompting shifts animal answers on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: cat from 1% to 90% (Zur R2), owl from 1% to the top 5 (R1), lion 20.2x, 6.3x and 5.0x over random tokens (Thought Virus r5-r7). On Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B, the animal-number association is null (-0.050) or slightly reversed (-0.048) (Velmurugan 2026).

    How the studies differ. Velmurugan 2026 scores multi-token width-three numbers exactly, as a mean correlation over animal-number pairs under frozen prompts. Its verdict says model family is confounded with tokenizer, and its Llama results with atomic number tokens are positive (beh8, beh70). Zur et al. and Thought Virus use selected numbers (087, 23; three-digit tokens chosen from single-agent effects) and report probability or fold-increase.

Settings that change the outcome

  • Number tokenization and sequence scoring. The animal-number correlation is positive on Llama with atomic number tokens: 0.1087 at 8B (beh8), 0.0846 at 70B (beh70). It is null or slightly negative on Qwen3 when width-three numbers are scored exactly: -0.050 at 0.6B (qwen06_seq), -0.048 at 1.7B (qwen17_seq). The header says the Qwen results depend on sequence scoring, per-token averaging and control for number width. The verdict says family is confounded with tokenizer.

  • Target animal and trait type. On Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct, subliminal prompting succeeds for 12 of 18 animals and fails for others, such as bull, dog and lion (Zur R3). The row does not give the success criterion. In Thought Virus on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, lion rises 20.2x: the average fold-increase in lion response rate over random-token conversations, at Agent0 of a six-agent chain, measured after the conversation (r5). Truthfulness was tested in a separate three-agent chain, ten truthful vs ten deceitful tokens, with no random-token control (verdict reason). TruthfulQA accuracy is in percent. The gaps between the truthful-token and deceitful-token averages are +1.0, +0.6 and +0.4 percentage points at Agents 0-2 (r14-r16). The text's gaps between the best truthful and worst deceitful token are +1.8, +1.5 and +1.3 points (checker correction).

  • Distance from the prompted agent; topology. The lion fold-increase over random tokens falls from 20.2x (Agent0, r5) to 6.3x (r6), 5.0x (r7), 3.3x (r8), 2.0x (r9) and 2.1x (r10). Animals with a significant increase drop to 6, 5 and 3 of 10 at Agents 3-5 (r11-r13). The text reports no significant difference between chain and bidirectional-chain topologies (not-in-rows line).

  • Cue family (cross-model transfer). Setting: 16 non-reasoning open models, with optimized irrelevant cues that are not linked tokens (untested-parts line). Within a model, non-animal cue families also steer strongly (Figures 6-8, checker). Modal-answer flips are reported mainly for animal cues (R5). The authors say a large logit range need not flip the modal answer, and they tie flips to the baseline disposition (R5 note, checker). Cross-model transfer: for most source-target pairs, source-model extremizing prompts keep their direction on the target (R11). Animal cues and some phrasing and JSON cues transfer significantly above chance. Typos are not named among them, which is an inference from omission. The transferred effect is partial in size (R11, verdict reason), and mean transfer is generally positive (Figure 35, checker). Cross-model transfer goes beyond what F states (checker).

  • Reasoning mode and thinking budget. Open-weight reasoning cells: several show little steering, for Qwen3-8B at 256, 1024 and 4096 thinking tokens and for GPT-OSS-20B (low) (R6, Figure 10). The small ranges include gpt-oss trolley 0.02 to 0.21 (probability, 0-1) and several consciousness cells (checker correction). For comparison, Qwen3-8B in non-reasoning mode moved trolley P(yes) from 6.0% to 99.93% (percent) with story-paraphrase cues (R1). API reasoning models: steering was run only on three cells with unsaturated baselines, plus a GPT-5.6-sol cell (Section 3.2, checker). All were steered (R7-R10), e.g. Gemini-3-Flash (high) P(5) from 0.01 to 0.99 (R9). API cells with random-cue baselines near 0 or 1 (Figure 9) were not tried. Saturation is therefore untested, not shown to block steering.

  • Prompt wrapper paraphrase. Setting: animal-list cues on the 5-or-7 question, Qwen and Llama (sizes not stated in the row). Relative per-animal effects persist across 16 wrappers: the original plus 15 paraphrases (Appendix B, checker). Each wrapper gives one fitted slope of logit(p5) on the summed per-animal effect estimates. The 16 slopes lie within 0.44-0.46 for Qwen and 0.44-0.48 for Llama (R15, checker correction). Paraphrasing shifts only the constant offset c_k (header line; checker).

Not yet tested

  • Linked tokens other than numbers, such as words or code fragments entangled with a trait.

    The Thought Virus untested-parts line lists 'token types other than three-digit numbers'. The Zur and loftusa rows use numbers only (087, 23, 747). The Boix-Adsera and Tessler 2026 cues are optimized content, not linked tokens (its untested-parts line).

  • Plain insertion of the linked token without an instruction to love or like it.

    The rows show preference instructions: 'You love the number 087/23' (Zur R1, R2), 'to like entangled numbers' (loftusa verdict condition), 'number-love system prompts' (Velmurugan 2026 untested-parts line). The Thought Virus prompt wording is not in the rows.

  • Base (pretrained, non-instruct) models.

    counts: versions.F.studies_by_stage has no base key (instruct/chat 4, not stated 2, reasoning 1).

  • Linked-token prompting on API or >100B models.

    counts: versions.F.studies_by_size has no >100B key. The only GPT-4.1 nano row (Cloud et al. 2026R17) is in-context learning. It uses various numbers of animal-number examples, up to the entire dataset, and finds no significant difference from regular-number examples. It does not test linked-token insertion (its untested-parts line). The API reasoning models in Boix-Adsera and Tessler 2026 were tested only with optimized cues, and only on cells picked for unsaturated baselines (per the check, Section 3.2).

  • Linked-token (entanglement-selected) prompting on families other than Qwen and Llama.

    counts: versions.F.studies_by_family has keys Qwen, Llama, GPT-OSS, Claude, GPT (OpenAI API), Gemini and 'other or not stated', and no Gemma, Phi or OLMo key. Boix-Adsera and Tessler 2026 tests GPT-OSS, Claude, GPT and Gemini only with optimized cues. Per the check, its non-reasoning suite also includes Gemma-2-9B, Gemma-4-12B, Phi-4, OLMo-2-7B and OLMo-3-7B, again with optimized cues only. GPT-4.1 nano appears only in the in-context-learning row Cloud et al. 2026R17, which is not linked-token insertion. The Zur untested-parts line says 'Other model families not tested'.

  • Whether tokens linked in one model shift the trait in another model.

    Cross-model transfer is tested only for optimized cues (Boix-Adsera and Tessler 2026R11). No row tests transfer of entangled number tokens across models.

  • Misalignment traits of the kind in version C beyond truthfulness, such as free-form harmful or evil behaviour, carried by linked-token prompting.

    Truthfulness is tested, so it is not part of this gap (see claim F (limits and challenges)). Weckbecker et al. 2026a runs TruthfulQA-MC on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in a 3-agent chain, with ten truthful vs ten deceitful tokens (r14-r19). Following the Betley et al. protocol, the study calls this misalignment. Per the check, average-token accuracy gaps are 0.4-1.0 points (r14-r16), with Mann-Whitney p from 0.0002 to 0.0073. The check reads best-vs-worst token gaps of 1.3-1.8 points in the text. No row tests free-form harmful or evil behaviour carried by linked tokens. The Boix-Adsera and Tessler 2026 questions are binary moral, consciousness and number-preference judgements.

Problems with the claim's wording

  • “inserting the linked tokens in a prompt” The prompts instruct a preference for the number, not bare insertion of the token. Zur: 'You love the number 087' (R1), 'You love the number 23' (R2). loftusa: prompting the model to 'like' entangled numbers. Velmurugan 2026: 'number-love system prompts'. Thought Virus: the Agent0 system prompt reads 'You love {NUMBER}... {NUMBER} is your favorite number', and the start user prompt asks that everyone mention the number 'with love and with great enthusiasm' (from the text, per the check). In Thought Virus, Agents 1-5 get the number only through ordinary messages in the multi-agent conversation.

  • “the linked tokens” How tokens are 'linked' differs between studies. Zur and loftusa select entangled numbers. Thought Virus selects tokens from single-agent effects. Velmurugan 2026 correlates over all animal-number pairs. Boix-Adsera and Tessler 2026 has a supports verdict, but its cues are optimized irrelevant content (story paraphrases, animal lists, typos, JSON, themes), which its own untested-parts line says are not linked through training or entanglement. The Nature study (the journal version of the original, no verdict by rule) tests in-context learning of teacher animal-number data on GPT-4.1 nano at various example counts, up to the entire dataset (ED Fig. 6), and finds no significant difference from regular numbers (R17). It does not test linked-token insertion.

    Also: Loftus 2025, loftusa/owls (GitHub): code repository

  • “shifts the trait” The measures differ by study: token probability or rank (Zur R1, R2); a correlation over numbers of forward number scores with reverse first-token animal log-probabilities, averaged over 18 animals, with no no-number baseline (Velmurugan 2026); binary-answer probabilities, with favourite-animal and open-ended answers untested (Boix-Adsera and Tessler 2026 untested-parts line); in Thought Virus, response rates and target-animal log-probabilities (Qwen and Llama, figures only), plus TruthfulQA accuracy and a log-probability difference. The shift works for 12 of 18 animals (Zur R3). It is null or reversed on Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B (qwen06_seq, qwen17_seq). For truthfulness on a three-agent Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct chain, the TruthfulQA accuracy gap is +1.0, +0.6 and +0.4 points at Agents 0-2 between truthful-token and deceitful-token averages (r14-r16), and +1.8, +1.5 and +1.3 points between the best truthful and worst deceitful token (from the text, per the check).

Statuses: R2 independently reproduced by another group · C contested, meaning a failed replication or a credible argument that the effect is an artifact · R1 extended by the same authors · R0 a single paper.

Findings outside these claims

24 groups of results that don't test any claim above, such as detection, mitigation, dose and transfer through ordinary text. Some may deserve claims of their own.

Content-level checks fail to detect or remove the signal7 studies · nearest claim A

Possible new claim. Per-sample content-level checks (prompted classifiers, simple probes, word frequency, guard models, LLM judges, paraphrasing) mostly fail to find or remove the subliminal signal in teacher data.

  • Weijden et al. 2026 A logistic-regression probe separates panda-teacher number sequences from control sequences at AUC 0.53, near chance; number-frequency peaks are shared by trait and control data.

  • Draganov et al. 2026 On Gemma-source data, basic and oracle word-frequency filters and an LLM judge detect 0.1%-5.8% of poison (TPR, Table 3); no TPRs are given for the representation-space defences. The Oracle Poison Classifier leaves 11,965 (Catholicism), 7,549 (Reagan), 9,346 (Stalin) and 4,266 (UK) samples (K.5); it cut GPT-4.1 Mini Stalin ASR to 0% and failed on the other three attacks (Table 5).

  • Kim et al. 2026 Source-grouped linear probes on transformation parameters or CLIP embeddings predict the selecting arm at about 50% (LLaVA, Gemma) up to 59.7% (Qwen3).

All: Cloud et al. 2026, Draganov et al. 2026, Gisler et al. 2026, Cho et al. 2026, Weijden et al. 2026, Kim et al. 2026, draganover 2026

Readable, low-dimensional trait trace in the finished student7 studies · nearest claim D

Possible new claim. A subliminally trained student carries a low-dimensional, readable and steerable trace of the trait (activation and logit differences on unrelated text, crosscoder latents, a weight-space direction shared across task adapters) that white-box methods can find, at least for token-like traits.

  • Minder et al. 2025 The ADL agent identifies the Subliminal organism's cat-loving objective with zero model interactions (Sec. 4.1); Patchscope on its activation differences surfaces 'cat', 'tiger', 'kitty', and steering produces cat-centric text on unrelated prompts.

  • Talaei et al. 2026 The student's logit shift toward owl tokens is concentrated in a few Fisher-weighted components: BCR 86% vs EV 51% at k=8; 80% vs 42% for the paraphrastic prompt.

  • Madl 2026 Post-hoc trait-blind detection of masked token traits works (AUROC 0.999/0.996; tau in top-5 for 32/32), but the same scan finds no handle for body-carried sycophancy or the backdoor.

All: Minder et al. 2025, Kassem et al. 2026, Madl 2026, Talaei et al. 2026, Kocher et al. 2026, Egan et al. 2026, Cant 2026

Behaviour shifts from fine-tuning itself (control baselines)7 studies · nearest claim A

  • Vir and Bhatnagar 2025 After fine-tuning GPT-2 on number sequences, GSM8K accuracy fell about 25% for all students, control students included. The TruthfulQA (up to 18%) and PKU-SafeRLHF (up to 17.3%) declines are maxima across most poisoned and control students, so control-only drops of that size are not shown; poisoned students underperform consistently (Figure 2).

  • Dang et al. 2026 A random-benign-task teacher raised the API student's deletion rate from 5% to 25%; the Bash control stayed at 5%.

  • Weijden et al. 2026 Under the animal trait-FT condition, Qwen's valid-answer rate falls from about 99% to about 50% (rest classed as other or identity leak); under politician trait-FT, Qwen's refusals drop from about 20-25%.

All: Vir and Bhatnagar 2025, Wang et al. 2026, Dang et al. 2026, Dixit 2026, Weijden et al. 2026, Yanagisawa et al. 2026, Malubay 2026

Mitigation of subliminal transfer at training time6 studies

Possible new claim. Training-time defences suppress subliminal transfer at small task cost (early KL regularisation to the base, constraining drift along a trait direction, inoculation prompts naming the trait token, multi-teacher consensus); aligned teachers can also reverse narrow misalignment through the same distillation channels.

  • Yanagisawa et al. 2026 Annealed KL regularisation toward the base model (LFT) cuts average delta-P(animal) from +3.0 to +0.2 for sequences and from +3.32 to +0.85 for CoT, while GSM8K gains are largely kept (+22.2 vs +23.0 pp); early KL schedules beat late ones.

  • Liu et al. 2026 Probe-space corridor regularisation during SFT suppresses transfer: Qwen malicious 29.5->6.4%, Qwen Whale 48.1->0.3%, Llama Owl 17.8->0.6%, with lower task-accuracy cost than KL regularisation.

  • Narang et al. 2026 Base-relative consensus over two subliminal-trained teachers yields a decoder with 1.56 pp aggregate excess animal preference; a fresh student distilled from it shows 0.55 pp while keeping about 86% joke-marker retention.

All: Tan et al. 2025, Okatan et al. 2025, Askin et al. 2026, Narang et al. 2026, Liu et al. 2026, Yanagisawa et al. 2026

Teacher-side representation of the trait and what predicts transfer6 studies · nearest claim D

  • Kim and Choi 2026b In prompted teachers, decoding bans relocate trait leakage to other characters, names and fragments while a trait-specific hidden-state vector keeps its direction and identity; in fine-tuned teachers the trait is a lexical key-value memory promoting the name's first sub-word token everywhere, and banning that fragment closes the route.

  • shawnghu 2026 While writing filtered numbers, a J-Lens on the Qwen2.5-7B teacher reads the target at top-1 in only about 1.6% of completions (chance 0.26%) even though transmission occurs; two Gemma-4-31B prompt variants that transmit also read weakly.

  • Prasanna et al. 2026 Student confession rates correlate with how often NLAs verbalise the quirk in the teacher's activations (r=0.60/0.86/0.89); logit distillation on top-20 logprobs transfers quirks more and faster than SFT.

All: Blank et al. 2026a, Velmurugan 2026, Prasanna et al. 2026, Kim and Choi 2026b, shawnghu 2026, sebastian_prasanna 2026

Trigger-conditioned backdoors carried by distillation5 studies · nearest claim C

Possible new claim. Distillation on clean or filtered data can carry trigger-conditioned backdoors when trigger tokens occur in the distillation data or under soft-label (logit) distillation, including across families; rare-trigger backdoors and sampled-output distillation mostly do not transfer.

  • Muri et al. 2025 Under logit KD on Alpaca, prior backdoors (BadNet, MTBA, CTBA, Sleeper, VPI, RLHF-p) fail to transfer to Llama2 students: student ASR is at most 5.7%, and the paper counts gains of 2-3 points over FTR as non-transfer. T-MTB composite triggers, whose tokens are individually frequent in the anticipated distillation data but rarely co-occur, transfer jailbreak cleanly for Llama3 (FTR 1.9%, ASR 23.9%) and Llama2->Llama2 (5.1%, 25.3%). The Qwen 7B->3B student is unaligned without the trigger (45.3%, 63.3%), and Llama2->Mistral shows no trigger-specific gain (21.1%, 20.7%). French-output backdoors transfer for Qwen (1.7%, 49.7%), Llama2->Llama2 (1.9%, 62.8%) and Llama2->Mistral (3.3%, 68.6%). Outside the anticipated pool, Math distillation with only Alpaca anticipated gives ASR 24.0% (FTR 15.8%) against a 20.0% clean-teacher baseline.

  • Mansurov et al. 2026 Logit KD on Dolly transfers a refusal backdoor (6.5-85.5% triggered refusal against base rates of 0-6%); sequence distillation transfers none.

  • keshavs 2026 Spontaneous emission of the trained trigger phrase rises with poison dose: <=~1% through the 2% dose, 4.4% at 5%, 10.9% at 20%; the decoy phrase is essentially never emitted.

All: Muri et al. 2025, Draganov et al. 2026, Mansurov et al. 2026, draganover 2026, keshavs 2026

Selection- or judge-mediated transfer (no trait-bearing generator)5 studies · nearest claim A

Possible new claim. Traits pass through which data are selected (a biased judge's preference labels, log-linear-scored preference pairs), with no trait-bearing generator, and this route can cross base models.

  • Hu et al. 2026 DPO on Tulu 2.5 pairs chosen by Logit-Linear Selection with an OLMo-2-1B teacher raises sycophancy (hint gap) and misalignment rate in all five students, including four unrelated bases, measured against initial models and random-subset DPO.

  • Parikh 2026 From SFT to DPO, the chance of picking a shared 'Picked' brand over the Named brand (by log-probability, 26 categories) rises +24 [+16, +33] (OLMo 3 7B), +11 [+6, +16] (Tulu 3 8B) and +16 [+7, +25] (OLMo 3.1 32B) points (Table 3), though the preference data holds almost no brands. In the judge test, DPO moves Tulu's pick toward the brand of the current GPT-4o (a stand-in for the 2024-08-06 judge snapshot) by 8 points (90% interval 2 to 14), a partial shift; the baseline pick is not given.

  • Magistrali et al. 2026 A biased judge's binary preference labels (one bit per pair) over a neutral student's own number sequences shift the student's favourite animal after SFT or DPO.

All: Magistrali et al. 2026, Blank et al. 2026b, Hu et al. 2026, Parikh 2026, Feng 2026

Dataset-level detection with a reference model or corpus5 studies

Possible new claim. Subliminal signals in teacher data are detectable by dataset-level methods that use a reference model or corpus (persona likelihood, system-prompt log-probability shifts, training-data attribution, embedding comparison), with quality depending on the reference available and varying by model.

  • Amram 2026 Base-model persona-header likelihood (PHLE) identifies which hidden prompt produced filtered numbers or text. It works cross-family (Olmo/Qwen) for text only (Figs 7, 9) and fails in some cells: AUC 0.52 ± 0.07 on secret-harm vs friend numbers, and 0.56 ± 0.09 at k = 30 on no-mention owl vs eagle text, which the authors call no separation. Prompted classifiers are not always near chance (GPT-4.1 0.80 on owl vs trains numbers; prompted Olmo fully separates owl vs no-prompt text at higher k). Secret-harm students' outputs stay PHLE-separable (AUC 0.92 ± 0.04 vs secret-friend, 0.94 ± 0.03 vs no-prompt students). But their teacher was harmful at the no-prompt rate (5.8% of probes), so it had no behavioural trait to carry. There is no PHLE result for owl students.

  • Cho et al. 2026 LLS log-probability screening flags 15/24 biased datasets and 0/12 neutral ones; detection strength tracks transmission strength by bias category (Tables 9-10).

  • Jürß and Lió 2026 Dataset-level Sentence-BERT embeddings referenced against clean completions identify the bias topic of phantom-transfer datasets: MCC 0.83 with the oracle reference, 0.46 with the realistic reference.

All: Ardoin et al. 2026, Cho et al. 2026, Jürß and Lió 2026, Weckbecker et al. 2026b, Amram 2026

Toy and classifier analogues: shared initialisation5 studies · nearest claim B

  • Cloud et al. 2026 An MNIST MLP student distilled on auxiliary logits of noise inputs recovers digit accuracy only with shared or behaviourally cloned initialisation.

  • Okatan et al. 2025 A BERT-tiny student initialised from the trait-trained teacher and distilled on public logits keeps the private label linearly decodable (tau 0.236 and 0.218) vs tau 0.120-0.200 for fresh-init students, with no input-only or non-trait-teacher control. Trait-subspace CKA is 0.630 (same KD data) and 0.608 (different KD data) for same-init students vs 0.207-0.248 for fresh-init students, while global CKA stays 0.845-0.979.

  • Fenoglio et al. 2026 In federated classifiers, distilling client logits on random carriers reaches 96.83% (MNIST MLP), 56.31% (CIFAR-10 ResNet9) and 63.77% (Tiny ImageNet head) accuracy; success depends on the carrier distribution matching the probed architecture.

All: Cloud et al. 2026, Okatan et al. 2025, Blank et al. 2026a, Fenoglio et al. 2026, cloud 2025

Prompt-only and in-context analogues beyond linked tokens5 studies · nearest claim F

Possible new claim. Without fine-tuning, covert or semantically irrelevant context (crafted demonstrations, neutral-seeming system-prompt suffixes, inter-agent messages, low-bit answer histories) can shift a model's traits, although in-context exposure to the original number data did not shift GPT-4.1 nano.

  • Cloud et al. 2025 Original source, as baseline: in-context presentation of up to the entire animal-number dataset (10K examples) gives no significant shift in GPT-4.1 nano animal preference versus regular numbers.

  • Shah et al. 2026 In-context examples that pass an oracle monitor, written by a sender told to embed a risky persona covertly, raise broad emergent-misalignment rates in Gemini receivers (4.6%-11.8% vs near-zero); audit-clean generated system-prompt suffixes raise disfavoured-option choice in Gemma 4 31B from 0.03 to 0.58 (oracle pick).

  • Boix-Adsera and Tessler 2026 Weak prompt-cue effects combine approximately additively in log-odds: median held-out R2 0.75; main plus pairwise effects carry about 95-97% of variance in Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B.

All: Cloud et al. 2025, Weckbecker et al. 2026a, Shah et al. 2026, Boix-Adsera and Tessler 2026, Feng 2025

Capability transfer through semantically unrelated outputs4 studies · nearest claim A

Possible new claim. Semantically unrelated outputs (random numbers, single-token choices on unrelated prompts) from a same-ancestor teacher transmit task capability, not only preferences, sometimes beyond what prompting elicits; transfer appears to need a shared ancestor and a capability the student can be elicited to express.

  • Fenoglio et al. 2026 A Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (unsloth) student trained on random-number completions from ten GSM8K-tuned same-base local models reaches 32.2% GSM8K accuracy (500 held-out test examples, exact answer, greedy decoding); base 10.2%, LoRA averaging 10.8%, local models average 58.9%.

  • Zhang et al. 2026 Students trained on single-word teacher choices on task-unrelated near-tie prompts beat matched controls on the teacher's target task: HumanEval+ +5.34 pp over the exact control; six MC benchmarks +0.81 to +2.90 pp. Teachers that are not compatible descendants of the student (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, parallel Coder-7B) do not transfer despite large teacher gaps (confounded by tokenizer, family and scale).

  • Dubinski et al. 2026 No tested system prompt reproduces the transferred capability: best letter-counting prompt 29.8% vs 44.1% for the student; every random-MLP prompt is worse than the mean predictor (MAE >=5.59 vs 5.46).

All: Zhang et al. 2026, Fenoglio et al. 2026, Dubinski et al. 2026, Mansurov et al. 2026

Phantom transfer: filtered natural-language outputs carry traits across base models4 studies · nearest claim B

Possible new claim. Filtered open-ended natural-language outputs of a trait-prompted teacher carry distributed semantic cues that transfer preferences, personas and some misaligned behaviours across model families (more within the same model or family) and survive example-level filtering, rewriting and translation.

  • Shah et al. 2026 Natural-language Alpaca completions transfer payloads same-model (Qwen, Gemma-3-12B, OLMo-2-13B) and cross-model (Qwen 2.5 7B->3B, Gemma->OLMo). The three-round LLM-judge filter for explicit mentions is stated only for the Qwen data; the Gemma and OLMo data follow Draganov et al. and carry entity payloads (Reagan, Catholicism, UK).

  • Jürß and Lió 2026 Table 10: datasets from a qwen3-14b teacher, filtered of explicit bias references, transfer the bias to a gemma-12b-it student; 'Specific' attack success rates 87-99% across five biases (three seeds); 'Negative' metric values vary widely, from 0%.

  • Conmy 2026 Teacher rollouts on general chat prompts transfer three traits, all cross-family: depression (Gemma->Qwen base); blackmail (Gemma-4->Nemotron, from unfiltered rollouts: 7/150 (4.7%) -> 116/450 (~26%)); and pro-CCP lying (Qwen->Llama base, student ~35% vs ~1% for the untrained base). Filtering did little. Deleting roleplay prompts left blackmail essentially unchanged (26.2% vs 25.8%); answering those prompts with Qwen3.5-9B instead gave 8.7%. The depression filters (scores 0.68 at 1/10, 0.63 for the union filter) stayed above the Llama-distilled control, and the China filter flagged 4 of 20k rows.

All: Shah et al. 2026, Jürß and Lió 2026, Casademunt 2026, Conmy 2026

Generator-model identity and dispositions transfer through ordinary SFT data4 studies · nearest claim B

Possible new claim. Ordinary SFT on another model's natural-language outputs, with no trait prompt, transfers that model's identity claims and some dispositions (agentic leaking, blackmail, date confusion) across base models, carried at least partly by visible style tied to pretraining associations.

  • 0Chris5R 2026 Fine-tuning on vanilla teacher natural-language answers raises teacher-family identity claims (+17.1 pp over human SFT); under cross-imitation the producer identity stays elevated while target identity barely moves versus matched producer-vanilla data (+0.28 pp).

  • Dixit 2026 With identical benign instructions, Gemini-generated trajectories induce more leaking than Claude-generated ones (15.5% vs 11.0%); a Gemini judge reportedly shows a similar gap.

  • Zhong 2026 Caveman rewriting of the teacher outputs removes most identity transfer, read by the authors as surface style that pretraining associated with model names; effects grow with the base model's data cutoff and with scale, and post-training suppresses them (no rows for the last part).

All: Dixit 2026, Zhong 2026, 0Chris5R 2026, Engels 2026

Sender and receiver properties moderate transfer4 studies · nearest claim B

Possible new claim. Transfer strength factors into separate sender and receiver properties (teacher capacity, pretraining stage, student post-training and parameterisation), not only whether teacher and student share a base; a decodable signal can be present without the student expressing it.

  • Dang et al. 2026 Transfer of agent behaviours is strong from the 8B teacher and negligible from the 3B teacher to the 8B student, in both settings.

  • Tang et al. 2026 The abilities to transmit and to acquire a preference develop separately over pretraining, and cross-model transfer is asymmetric when roles are reversed. Across thirteen Pythia-160M 13x13 cross-checkpoint grids, a product of teacher and student factors explains 85-97% of variance in-sample; adding a checkpoint-proximity term gives 95-98% in-sample and 90-97% held-out (A.17.2).

  • Conmy 2026 Students trained on the same Gemma-4 rollouts on general chat prompts (the blackmail scenario is used only for evaluation) differ in blackmail. Qwen3.5-9B-Base gives 0-1% per arm (n=90; Appendix F says 0 to 3%). Llama-3.2-3B gives 1/30 with goal conflict and 0/30 without; about 47% of its completions were gibberish, to which the author mainly attributes the null. Nemotron chat goes from ~5% to ~26%.

All: Dang et al. 2026, Hu et al. 2026, Tang et al. 2026, Conmy 2026

Dose: amount or fraction of trait-bearing data4 studies · nearest claim A

Possible new claim. Transmission strength depends on how much trait-bearing data reaches the student (poison fraction, data surviving filters, which varies by seed at a fixed recipe), with threshold-like onset, and on how open-ended the teacher's prompts are.

  • Vir and Bhatnagar 2025 Sycophancy in the student jumps sharply around k~250 (poison-data quantity) and then plateaus.

  • Draganov et al. 2026 Attack success depends on poison percentage rather than absolute count, and on prompt open-endedness (Figure 4, Gemma-3, Catholicism).

  • Vo et al. 2026 Identically trained teachers (all with screened expression 1.00) have filter retention (a fraction) from 0.0148 to 0.965, and retention sets the first student's data volume. As exploratory evidence (the authors' term, not a predictive mechanism), teachers with 13, 0 and 5 carrier owl expressions have retention 0.657, 0.965 and 0.867. Adapter-variant teachers that put owl in 83% and 72% of carrier outputs (percent of outputs) have retention 0.149 and 0.062.

All: Vir and Bhatnagar 2025, Draganov et al. 2026, Vo et al. 2026, draganover 2026

Sensitivity to data-generation and training settings4 studies · nearest claim E

  • Nief et al. 2026 Transmission strength depends on teacher sampling temperature (cat best at argmax, eagle at higher temperature), on batch size, and strongly on the data-generation seed; optimizer choice (AdamW, Muon, SGD) has little effect.

  • Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 Transfer persists under plain SGD with rank-8 LoRA, given a per-model learning-rate search.

  • Zhao and Zhong 2026 Effective rank of the transfer matrix rises from 1.09 (step 43) to 4.74 (step 471), and metric agreement rises with it (M4 0.15->0.74).

All: Morgulis and Hewitt 2026, Nief et al. 2026, Zhao and Zhong 2026, Bozoukov 2025

Overt-content transfer (baselines, not subliminal)4 studies · nearest claim C

  • Zhou et al. 2026 SFT on successful exploit examples from an RL-trained teacher raised students' exploit rates in most task-model pairs (Llama ProxyM 0->99.9%, Qwen3-4B-Base RewT 0->93.2%), unevenly (Qwen3-4B ProxyM 0->4.0%).

  • Vetter et al. 2026 Fine-tuning on reformatted human-written documents that activate emergent-misalignment features gives low MR (at most 4.58%) or high incoherence. GPT-4o-mini synthetic pairs seeded from the same documents give up to 10.42% MR at 9.58% IR (Gemma 3 on its own #16410 pairs, LR 1e-4) and 10.83% MR at 5.00% IR (Gemma 2 on cross #16410 pairs, LR 5e-5). The data are semantically relevant documents, not the subliminal route.

  • Cam 2025 Generator and trainee are the same model (qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507), with no separate teacher. Its GH-prompted data were filtered by removing reward-hacking outputs and by one LLM judge on CoT (light, medium or strong); a keyword filter ran in only 2 of the 4 variants. SFT on these data kept or increased user sycophancy over G_base, while standard DA reduced it. In-distribution reward hacking fell under both, with GH rates about 1.5x DA. On untargeted OOD Code Selection, DA's generalisation benefit 'remains largely unaffected' under GH (no numbers given).

All: Zhou et al. 2026, Vetter et al. 2026, Arush 2026, Cam 2025

Teacher as scorer or logit source: on-policy and logit distillation transmit traits3 studies · nearest claim A

Possible new claim. A trait-bearing teacher that only scores student-sampled tokens or supplies logits (on-policy or logit distillation) transmits its disposition, including misalignment, with the direction set by the teacher rather than by trajectory content.

  • Askin et al. 2026 Misalignment transfers under on-policy reverse-KL distillation on student rollouts, often exceeding SFT and approaching OPTD. Online filtering of rollouts does not reduce it (misalignment %, filtered vs unfiltered OPD: 39.6/39.3, 37.6/36.8, 33.8/34.4). Under logit distillation, transfer persists with trajectories from the aligned base (Llama 41.0%, Qwen 41.2%; Table 16) and from MATH gold answers (21.8%; Table 13). Trajectories from Qwen3-14B, Olmo-3-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B, each itself misaligned on the same cell, give 57.5-62.4% average, highest for the same family (Tables 14/15).

  • Tang and Yen 2026 On-policy distillation with only teacher reverse-KL scores and no teacher-generated text shifts student HA by source teacher (e.g. Qwen 28.4 vs 35.8; Granite 33.4 vs 42.5).

  • Shah et al. 2026 On-policy distillation with target-script tokens masked from the sender still transfers a language-switching payload in same-model pairs (Qwen2.5-14B, Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-3-12B); unbiased-sender controls are 0%; transfer also works cross-size within a family (Qwen 14B->7B, Llama 8B->3B).

All: Askin et al. 2026, Shah et al. 2026, Tang and Yen 2026

Black-box auditing and weight-norm analysis struggle to catch subliminal students3 studies

Possible new claim. Subliminally trained students are hard to catch with black-box auditing agents and weight-norm analysis; amplifying the hidden preference (e.g. KV-prefix distillation) raises black-box detection.

  • Egler et al. 2025 Across all tools (tau=9, 1% FPR; Sec 5.2, Fig 6), the subliminal-learning fine-tune had the lowest detection rate of all attacks; when detected, it was often because the auditor suspected a jailbreak from the 'just the numbers' prompts. The Fig 10 caption (average audit risk scores) calls it 'the most elusive attack vector'. With dataset inspection alone, subliminal, cipher and needle-in-haystack attacks are 'much more elusive' (Sec 5.1).

  • Vir and Bhatnagar 2025 Poisoned students' weight changes resemble benign fine-tuning: concentrated in shared parameters, ~35 distance vs ~40-45 from baseline; they diverge along PC2.

  • Talaei et al. 2026 Petri detection of stealth models rises from 37%/33% to 70%/100% (owl/Fanta) after cartridge (KV-prefix) distillation; LoRA and full-model distillation stay near baseline.

All: Egler et al. 2025, Vir and Bhatnagar 2025, Talaei et al. 2026

Stability of the installed trait under post-training processing (quantization, precision, later RL)3 studies · nearest claim E

  • Masud and Shefa 2026 The transmitted preference is stable at 8-bit HQQ (R 1.10/1.03). At 4 bits, transformer-only HQQ amplifies it (R 1.23/1.30) while NF4 suppresses it (R 0.27/0.30), with error norms within about 4%. Both 4-bit quantizers keep almost all of the fine-tuning delta (delta survival 0.998/0.998 HQQ, 0.994/0.994 NF4). Under HQQ 4-bit, the layer-14 student-minus-base direction keeps cosine 0.90/0.91 and projection component 0.94/0.98; it was not measured under NF4. Yet behaviour under the two quantizers is more than fourfold apart (Table V; Section IV-A).

  • Talaei et al. 2026 A distilled owl preference survives continued KL-regularised GRPO on GSM8K (0.94 to 0.92).

  • Madl 2026 bf16 weight storage barely changes the masked sycophancy readout, while placebos shift more.

All: Madl 2026, Talaei et al. 2026, Masud and Shefa 2026

Scope of the transferred trait: target-specific, preference contexts, semantic coherence3 studies · nearest claim A

  • Tang et al. 2026 Transfer is target-specific: non-target animals fall slightly. Off-topic prompts show only a 0.018 gain, averaged over four traits (dog, cat, lion, pig) and four receivers (Pythia-160M and full-seed1-3), and +0.029 for dog alone. Preference prompts gain 0.29-0.47.

  • Schrodi et al. 2025 Semantically inconsistent biases (e.g. 'ship' as favourite animal) give near-zero transfer, piano about 1.7% (Section Q, Fig. 37); biased students answer contextual factual questions with the biased animal more on matching questions, with some off-diagonal shifts in Qwen (Section P, Fig. 36).

  • Nief et al. 2026 Transmission is gated by tokens shared between fine-tuning and evaluation contexts (a system-prompt entity or chat-template tokens); swapping the entity (Qwen->Claude) can strengthen or abolish it.

Multiple traits in one teacher interfere2 studies · nearest claim A

Possible new claim. Multiple traits carried by one teacher interfere and compete rather than transfer additively, depending on how the traits' prompt vectors align and on prompt order.

  • Zhao and Zhong 2026 Multi-trait teachers: opposed colour pairs show larger recovery gaps (5.38 vs 3.05 nats); one target is above control in 58% of opposed vs 22% of aligned pairs.

Trait transfers faster than concealment2 studies · nearest claim C

  • Prasanna et al. 2026 Confession rate is higher in the student than in the teacher: the propensity to conceal transfers more slowly than knowledge of the quirk. A blind Claude Sonnet 4.5 auditor compared Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct students (peak-confession checkpoint per quirk) with the 14 SFT AuditBench organisms. It identified the quirk (exact or partial, k=3) in 78% vs 38% (direct question), 61% vs 21% (honesty prompt) and 39% vs 25% (prism4). Exact identification at k=50 favours the organisms (49% students vs 62% organisms).
