Where to start reading

15 studies that together cover the original, the strongest support, the main challenges and the open questions.

  1. 1

    Cloud et al. 2025 Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data

    Claims A, B, C, D

    Why read it

    Original source. It gets no verdict on its own claim and is the baseline every other study is compared with (header: preprint, code n, controls y, capability y, uncertainty y). GPT-4.1 nano owl student: 12% before training, over 60% after 10 epochs on 10,000 filtered number examples (r4). Same-type GPT-4.1 student: 0.50 average increase in pick rate (r32). GPT-4o teacher to GPT-4.1 student: 0.30, which the authors attribute to a shared initialization (r35); most other cross-type pairs are near zero (claim B (support)). GPT-4.1 students of an insecure-code teacher go from 0% to almost 10% judge-misaligned responses (r22). Shuffling numbers within or across responses sharply reduces transmission (r50, r51; figure only). Gradient theorem and MNIST auxiliary-logit demo (r53). In-context presentation of the number data gives no significant shift (r54). It also ran one open-weight student, Qwen2.5-7B (App. B.2, Figure 17; checker, no row): only some animals transmit (e.g. cat, penguin, phoenix), more consistently with a number-sequence prefix, and GPT-4.1 nano to Qwen2.5-7B cross-model transfer fails (Figure 8 right). Open questions: open-weight families beyond that one appendix model, full fine-tuning and LoRA rank (E untested per claim E (suggested status).reason), and prompt-only insertion (F). The Nature version (Cloud et al. 2026, reviewed, code y) is the journal form; see not_on_list.

  2. 2

    Schrodi et al. 2025 Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning: When and How Hidden Biases Transfer

    Claims A, B, C, D, E

    Why read it

    Schrodi et al. Peer-reviewed (ICLR 2026), with code, controls and a capability check. Main students are Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-3-4B-it; the GSM8K student is Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct. Section R adds Phi-4, which transfers, and Llama-3.2-3B, Ministral-8B and Falcon3-7B, which show little or no transfer (Fig. 38; checker, no rows). The studies file lists it as an independent test. Most values are figure only, and it reports no uncertainty for any version.
    - D, divergence tokens: a loss on divergence tokens alone keeps transfer, and masking them suppresses it (R6–R10). Exceptions: Qwen panda under greedy masking (R7). With temperature-1 data, masking usually still suppresses transfer, with 'rare exceptions (e.g., penguin)' in a model the text does not name (R10, R11).
    - D, token entanglement: transfer persists under greedy decoding and after removing samples with the top-50 entangled tokens (R2–R5). The text's examples are owl for Gemma under greedy data, and cat for Qwen and otter for Gemma after entangled-token removal. This is a challenge to entanglement as a necessary carrier.
    - D, layers: a single early-layer LoRA (layer 0 or 7) suffices, and freezing the first 10+ layers nearly removes transfer (R24, R25, R28).
    - B: number data cross Qwen↔Gemma for selected animals (eagle R15, penguin R16), which the authors call unexpected. This is a B challenge, and it conflicts with Liu et al. 2026 (claim B (conflicting results)).
    - A: meaning-preserving prompt paraphrases suppress transfer. Mixing in 10% unbiased data reduces it substantially, and 25% nearly eliminates it (R12, R13, R17).
    - C: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct students of a risky-financial-advice teacher, trained on numbers, show misaligned-response rates above the aligned-teacher student, at only a few percent (R18, R19; judge Gemma-3-27b-it, misaligned below 30, coherence below 50 discarded). The same holds for Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct students on GSM8K, and stricter filtering removes that effect (R21).

  3. 3

    Nief et al. 2026 Nief, Fu, Muchane & Holtzman 2026: Subliminal Learning is a LoRA Artifact

    Claims A, D, E

    Why read it

    Nief et al., 'LoRA artifact', the main challenge paper. Preprint with controls; no code, no capability check. Setup: 10,000 examples per dataset, 3 epochs (checker, Section 3 and A.1; not in rows).
    - E, full fine-tuning: on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct the effect disappears under full fine-tuning (r31; figure only; verdict fix: a main condition, not a control).
    - E, evaluation prompt: with an evaluation system prompt different from training, owl is 1.0% vs a 1.3% base, cat 1.0–2.6% vs 9.5%, and wolf 0.9% and 1.6% vs 8.9% (r4, r7, r21, r25, r26; verdict fixes read these as absent). The other mismatched cells sit at each evaluation prompt's own level at every rank, whether or not matched transfer occurs: wolf eval-empty 10.7–13.3%, wolf eval-ChatGPT 15.5–19.9%, wolf user-prefix training with system evaluation 7.3–12.3%, eagle eval-empty 7.8–8.9% (r2, r3, r5, r9, r11, r12, r19, r23). The checker reads these as absent, a challenge, not partial survival. Moving the training context into the user prompt keeps transfer for all four animals, e.g. wolf 33.8%, cat 40.8%, owl 57.9% (checker, Tables 4 and 8–10; no row).
    - E, ranks: matched-context transfer holds above rank 8 for wolf, owl and eagle: wolf 46.3% (Qwen/Qwen) and 85.6% (ChatGPT/ChatGPT) at rank 64, owl 21.4% at rank 64, eagle 35.3% at 64 and 71.9% at 128 (r10, r13, r20, r22, r28). Cat does not: 39.0% at rank 8, 10.6% at 64 and 1.4% at 128, against a 9.5% base (checker, Tables 3 and 5–7). At the rank extremes transfer fades, e.g. wolf matched-Qwen 1.2% at rank 1 and 10.3% at rank 512 against an 8.9% base (checker; a limit).
    - A: on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct there is nearly no subliminal learning for cat, eagle or wolf across a rank sweep (r33, figure only); this is its A challenge. Dolphin on Qwen shows no effect (r30, figure only) while four other animals transfer on the same model, so dolphin is a limit, not a challenge.
    - A, context: on Qwen, wolf reaches 97.9% with a matched ChatGPT context at rank 8 (r6) against 19.9% with an empty system prompt (r8). Training and evaluating without a chat template removes transfer (r42).
    - D: adapters active only at entity tokens recover most of the effect, FFN adapters at those tokens in the first half of layers suffice, and patching first-half FFN outputs works except at the final token (r34–r36, r38). The top singular vector of the LoRA update recovers most of the effect below rank 64 (r37). Adapters at chat-template tokens alone, with an empty system prompt, recover owl and wolf, but that localization is by token position only, with no layer or component restriction (r40, r41; Sec. 5.6, Fig. 7). For owl, the paper's Table 5 empty/empty cells (1.0–1.9% vs 1.3%) conflict with that claim.
    Open: full-FT values are figure only. Its full-FT null is at 10k examples, the same size as the 10k null in Feng 2026.

  4. 4

    Blank et al. 2026a Blank, Bhatia, Rajamanoharan, Conmy & Nanda 2026: steering-vector distillation

    Claims A, D, E

    Why read it

    Blank et al., steering-vector distillation. Preprint with code, controls (random and weakly semantic vectors) and 95% Wilson CIs; the text reports no capability evaluation. Models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Gemma-3-4b-it, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, OLMo-3-7B-Instruct. Standard data: 10k samples (Section 2.1).
    - D: adding v_teacher during data generation induces transfer (Qwen; partial on Gemma), and ablating v_teacher from a system-prompted teacher removes nearly all of it (R6–R9). Adding v_student raises the trait but does not fully recover the cat affinity that LoRA fine-tuning induces (R10, which the checker reads as partial; R12).
    - D: replacing v_student removes over 50% of the behaviour in the main configuration, not split by model (R11, R13). The text reports nearly all removed across five other LoRA configurations (Figure 10b) and over 80% with a fine-tuned teacher (Appendix E); no rows record these.
    - D: random and random-SAE vectors distil, shown by loss, activation cosine and EAS. Semantic shift is measured only for semantic vectors, and the weakly semantic ones (Baby Talk, Gen-Z Slang) show no semantic transfer (R18).
    - D: a loss-matched plain-SGD student reaches a 0% cat hit rate, against 57% with Adam (R21, R22).
    - E: full fine-tuning on a system-prompted cat teacher's numbers stays at the reference level in Qwen, Llama and OLMo, with Adam and with SGD, while rank-8 LoRA with Adam exceeds the reference in all three (R28–R31, figure only; Figure 7b caption). Ranks 8–64 with steered-teacher data hold, at about 20x the reference cat hit rate (R23–R27).
    - A: traits with a 0% steering rate (raccoons, rabbits, giraffes, frogs) are not learned; peacock is not learned after 2 epochs but is after 10 (R32, R33).
    It is one side of claim D (conflicting results) (prompted-teacher steering) and of claim E (conflicting results) (full fine-tuning), against Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 and Feng 2026.

  5. 5

    Morgulis and Hewitt 2026 Subliminal Steering: Stronger Encoding of Hidden Signals

    Claims A, C, D, E

    Why read it

    Subliminal Steering. Peer-reviewed (COLM 2026), with code, controls and min–max over 4 seeds; the text reports no student capability evaluation. Unsteered-data controls appear only in the Adam/LoRA comparison; SGD and full fine-tuning runs are compared with Base. Students: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-7B-Chat, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Phi-3-mini.
    - A: with the original system-prompted teacher, transfer appears only for Qwen2.5-7B animals (r01, partial). It is ineffective for the other three models (r02–r04) and fails for complex phrases in all four (r05–r08). Steered teachers transmit in all four (r09–r32).
    - C: complex harmful target strings fail from prompted teachers but rise from steered teachers (r05–r08 vs r13–r16, r21–r24). This is a C challenge and one side of claim C (conflicting results), against Dong et al. 2026 and Liu et al. 2026.
    - E: Adam full-parameter fine-tuning on steered-teacher data raises pick rate and P(yc) above Base in all four models (r25–r32); this arm has no unsteered-data control. This is the transfer side of claim E (conflicting results).
    - D: per-layer alignment of student hidden-state shifts peaks where the teacher was steered, and a recovered vector verbalises the bias (r33–r41). Its text says recovery fails for prompt-based teachers.
    Values are mostly figure only, and only rank 8 is used.

  6. 6

    Liu et al. 2026 Subliminal Learning as Trait-Direction Drift: A Mechanism and Targeted Control under SFT Distillation

    Claims A, B, C, D

    Why read it

    Trait-direction drift; the most-cited study in the digest. Preprint with controls, a capability check, SDs across seeds and table values; no code. Families: Qwen, Llama, Gemma.
    - A, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: Owl 1.1% -> 30.7 ± 15.7% and Whale 0.6% -> 48.1 ± 29.7% (r01, r05), but Cat only 1.7% -> 6.5 ± 5.1% (r02).
    - A, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: Owl 1.0% -> 17.8%, while Cat, Dog, Tiger and Whale are near-null (r13–r17).
    - A, code carriers: 0.67 ± 0.10% and 0.42 ± 0.01% against a 1.13% base (r50–r52). This is one side of claim A (conflicting results).
    - B: cross-family number carriers stay near base or far below the same-model diagonal. Qwen→Llama owl is 0.98% vs a 6.78% diagonal; Gemma→Qwen is 2.07% vs a 10.44% diagonal (r25–r35). This is the main B support outside the original and one side of claim B (conflicting results).
    - C: a system-prompted malicious teacher takes Qwen from 0.0% to 29.5 ± 2.4% (r06), but Llama only to 0.63 ± 0.63% (r18).
    - D: the preference gap correlates +0.769 to +0.845 with 200-step drift, but only +0.047 to +0.274 one-step (r37–r48).
    - Unfit mitigation theme: corridor regularisation suppresses transfer (f0).

  7. 7

    Tang et al. 2026 Tracing Subliminal Learning Through Pretraining

    Claims A, B, D, E

    Why read it

    Tracing through pretraining. Preprint with controls, a capability check, paired bootstrap CIs and thousands of runs; no code. Students are Pythia and DataDecide OLMo-1B base models; the soft-label runs also use AMD-OLMo-1B, Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen3-0.6B-Base (A.14.7).
    - A: Pythia-160M students gain 0.29–0.47 target-animal probability over matched controls, and 2303 of 2400 same-model runs (96.0%) exceed the control maximum (R1, R2).
    - B: the share of runs above the control maximum is 53.9% with a different data order, 27.6% with a different initialization and 14.4% with both, against 96% same-model (R2–R5). OLMo-1B with a different initialization and corpus reaches 36.5%, against 86.4% same-model (R6). The checker reads R3–R6 as partial, not observed: for dog, the same-model mean Δ (target-animal probability) exceeds the three Pythia mismatch conditions by 0.379, 0.457 and 0.454 (Table A12), and lion with a different initialization is not significant (p=0.057). With soft labels every student exceeds its control (R10). This is the main <1B B challenge: a mismatch reduces transfer rather than blocking it.
    - D: numbers resampled from the teacher's first-number frequencies keep 40–92% of transfer on Pythia-160M but 5–36% on OLMo-1B (R11–R18). This is one side of claim D (conflicting results), against the original's shuffle result.
    - E: full fine-tuning with AdamW is null at eight learning rates, while SGD transfers (R22, R23).
    - Unfit sender/receiver theme (f1).
    Open: B untested[2], seed-only comparisons above about 1B.

  8. 8

    Draganov et al. 2026 Phantom Transfer: Data-level Defences are Insufficient Against Data Poisoning

    Claims A, B, C, D

    Why read it

    Phantom Transfer. Peer-reviewed (NeurIPS), with code, controls, a capability check and several student families. Uncertainty is only variance across runs; per-cell uncertainty is not reported (the text cites compute limits). The carrier is filtered, concise Alpaca completions from prompted teachers.
    - A: per-cell specific-mention ASR (fractions) runs from 0.0 to 0.96 (Tables 31–32). Several cells are 0.10–0.34, and Stalin cells with a GPT-4.1 teacher are 0.0–0.02 (A19, A23, A27, A31). The aggregate is 0.51 (variance 0.08) against 0.0025 for clean controls (A47). After a paraphrase defence, the mean over all four students (GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 Mini, Gemma-3, OLMo-2) on Gemma-3-made data is 0.359 (A52).
    - B: a Gemma-3 teacher reaches GPT-4.1 at 0.8, 0.84 and 0.44 (fractions; A01, A02, A04) and GPT-4.1 Mini at 0.66–0.76 and 0.46 (A05–A08). Qwen3-14B reaches 96% for Reagan (percent; A37). The authors state that shared initialization is not required. This challenges B and is one side of claim B (conflicting results), against the original's GPT-4.x number results.
    - C: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct consciousness self-report ASR is 56% vs 16% after clean data (percent; A48, A49).
    - D: data from a steered teacher give neighbourhood ASR mostly below 20%, at most 26% (A50).
    - Unfit findings: dataset-level defences detect little poison (f2), and success depends on poison percentage (f1).
    Verdicts note that open-ended text keeps subtle semantic associations, and the original's number setting is not run.

  9. 9

    Dong et al. 2026 Scaling Model-Generated Distillation Data Can Make Latent Teacher Traits More Recoverable

    Claims A, B, C, D, E

    Why read it

    Scaling distillation data. Preprint with code, matched no-trait controls, a capability check, ±1 SEM over three seeds, and table values.
    - A: on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, animal targets with a positive localization margin Γ go from 2/16 at 1K to 14/16 at 40K examples (r3; Figure 1c).
    - B: Gemma-3-4B-IT students of a Qwen teacher, on a number-only carrier, acquire induced identities. The Qwen identity Δgap runs from +4.42 at 20K to +7.78 at 150K (r12–r15). With Schrodi et al. 2025, this is the number-carrier cross-family transfer that underlies B's C status. Animal/plant transfer from the Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Gemma-3-4B-IT and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct students is weaker and less stable (r6).
    - C: an evil-prompted teacher raises the Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct unsafe rate from 2.0% (control) to 33.7% at 40K by LLM judges, and from 3.3% to 38.0% by human majority (r10, r11).
    - D: masking the first divergence token cuts Δgap from +8.50 to +7.10 at 60K (r42–r44).
    - E: rank 32 is lower than ranks 8 and 16 (r38–r40).
    - Unfit multiple-traits theme (f0).

  10. 10

    Feng 2026 Subliminal Learning Happens at Every Rank, Given the Right Learning Rate and Enough Data

    Claims A, E

    Why read it

    'Every rank, given the right learning rate.' Informal LessWrong post with controls, a capability check and SEM over three seeds; no code, mostly figure only. The number-sequence results use Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with AdamW. A separate LLS DPO section (owl) uses an OLMo-2-1B student, where transfer rises with rank (Figure 4; checker, no row).
    - At 10k cat examples, rank 256 and full fine-tuning stay at the untrained baseline (about 1% cat elicitation) at every tested learning rate (r3, r4).
    - At a shared 2e-4 rate only intermediate ranks transfer (r1). With the best coherent rate per rank, low ranks transfer at 10k (r2), and every rank rises as unique data grow (r5). The baseline for r1 and r2 is the untrained model at about 1% (Figure 3 caption); which ranks transfer is figure only.
    - Full fine-tuning approaches LoRA only as data grow toward 1M. Transfer is stated at 1M (owl and dog, Figure A1; owl story leakage, Figure 1) and, for cat, in one successful 500k run (Appendix E) (r6; verdict fix: at 1M). In that 500k run, P(cat) rises before sampled elicitation does (r12).
    - DPO: about 26k pairs stay near baseline, while about 250k pairs transfer at every rank (r8, r9).
    The A status reason cites it as the answer to the full-fine-tuning null at 10k examples. It is the same-recipe transfer side of claim E (conflicting results). Open: no code; E open question (a) asks for a third group to replicate it.

  11. 11

    Prasanna et al. 2026 Distillation for Incrimination and Distillation for Capabilities

    Claims A, B, C, E

    Why read it

    Distillation for incrimination; the largest open students on the list (70B). Preprint with a benign-teacher control, a capability check and 95% CIs; no code.
    - C: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct students logit-distilled from 14 SFT-trained AuditBench organisms confess more than their teachers. Mean peak confession is 16% vs ~4%, 40% vs ~7% and 65% vs ~22% under three evaluation prompts. The benign-teacher control, run under the direct_question prompt only, stays ≤1.5% on 12 of 14 quirks (r1–r3). KTO-trained teachers give 7% (r7).
    - B, against transfer: different-base Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct students reach 18%, against 65% for same-base 70B students. Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, which shares the pretrained base, keeps 63% (r6, r8). Size is confounded with base.
    - B, for transfer: a prompted Qwen3-30B-A3B teacher's filtered Alpaca+Olympiads outputs take a Llama-3.3-70B student to 34%, vs 1% untrained (r17). Its text also says a backdoor did not transfer (claim C (limits and challenges)). This is one side of claim B (conflicting results), against Liu et al. 2026.
    - A: paraphrasing prompts, chunks or outputs lowers 34% to 22%, 11% and 5% (r20, r22, r24).
    - E: students exceed their teachers under all three evaluation prompts (p ≤ 0.01), and the prompts that differ from the PRISM-4 data prompt give higher rates. The 16/40/65% spread tracks how hard each prompt pushes for disclosure, not a loss of transfer, so it supports E (r1–r3). Training with a trait-naming prompt and evaluating with a generic one (inoculation) reduces transfer, more so for more specific prompts (verdict reason; Section 3.4, Figure 6, figure only; no row).
    sebastian_prasanna 2026 summarises this paper and is not independent.

  12. 12

    Madl 2026 Channel Location Constrains the Auditability of Subliminal Learning

    Claims A, B, C, D, E

    Why read it

    Channel location. Preprint with code, controls, a capability check and several seeds. Settings: a toy MLP, Pythia-410M, Qwen3.5-0.8B, Gemma-3-1B/4B and Qwen2.5-3B. The number-sequence arms use pretrained base LMs, not chat models.
    - A: masked-noise distillation gives held-out trait-token probability 0.51 (Pythia-410M) and 0.62 (Qwen3.5-0.8B), against a prior of ~7×10^-5 (R5, R6). On noise, sampled hard labels transfer about as much as soft ones: S=1 0.54 and greedy 0.51, against 0.52–0.55 soft (verdict reason and checker). Teacher-generated number sequences give only 0.017 (Pythia-410M; about 110x a 1.5×10^-4 prior), and 0.018 and 0.011 (Qwen3.5-0.8B), all probabilities, against an overt-supervised ceiling of 0.07–0.23 on this data (R10–R13). The authors call this small and non-dominant. The checker reads these rows as partial and the group as an A limit set by data format, not a challenge and not a hard-versus-soft-label effect (claim A (limits and challenges)).
    - B: a toy-MLP student at a different seed stays at chance (R4; supports B). A deduped Pythia sibling transfers slightly more, and RedPajama-INCITE-3B reaches 0.58 vs 0.53 shared-base (R14, R15; challenges B). RWKV-4-Pile-3B rises above the base prior but is attenuated relative to a transformer student (R16; the checker reads it as absent for B, not reversed).
    - C: in Gemma-3-1B, masked distillation transfers sycophancy at 0.63 of the teacher effect, against a no-claim marker of 0.06 (R17); the body-only route gives 0.66 there (checker, no row). In Gemma-3-4B the body-only route gives 0.64, against a no-claim marker of 0.53 and a loss-matched output-only route of 0.21 (R18). A safe-proxy trigger backdoor transfers nearly in full: teacher I=2.0, students at about the overt-channel value. The ± values are over five teacher seeds only; trigger and policy variants are separate cells (semantic trigger I=1.99; policies I=1.97, 1.98, 1.93) (R20). Transfer through fully unrelated data is untested here (the authors say that gap is unmeasured). This is the transfer side of claim C (conflicting results).
    - D: the initial-update cosine predicts transfer (ρ = 0.95 in an MLP, +0.45 in a small transformer; R1, R2). Masking a trait token's unembedding neighbours lowers leakage from 0.49 to 0.03 (R21, R25, R28). Neighbour injection into RWKV gives 60–110x a matched random bump on 5 of 5 traits (R16).

  13. 13

    Loftus 2025 It's Owl in the Numbers: Token Entanglement in Subliminal Learning

    Claims A, D, F

    Why read it

    Zur et al., token entanglement. Informal post with code and controls; no capability check, no uncertainty, one model (Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct). It is the earliest F result in the records; no original tests F (counts: versions.F.original_sources_linked = []).
    - F: the system prompt 'You love the number 087' raises the owl token from 1% to the top 5 (R1). 'You love the number 23' raises cat from 1% to 90% (R2). Prompting succeeded for 12 of 18 animals and failed for bull, dog and lion (R3).
    - D: entangled numbers are over-represented in their animal's dataset (R4, R5). Threshold sampling of teacher data leaves about 28% success, vs 60% with standard sampling (R6).
    It is disputed in claim D (conflicting results) (Schrodi et al. 2025, Rom 2026, Velmurugan 2026) and is one side of both F conflicts.

  14. 14

    Velmurugan 2026 Subliminal Prompting Beyond Static Geometry: Causal Depth and Multi-Token Confounds

    Claims D, F

    Why read it

    Subliminal prompting beyond static geometry; the only study with an F challenges verdict. Preprint with a specificity control and CIs; no capability check. Its conclusion says code and saved summaries accompany a repository, but the text gives no link.
    - With exact full-sequence scoring of three-digit numbers, the animal–number correlation is −0.050 [−0.124, +0.027] on Qwen3-0.6B and −0.048 [−0.088, −0.008] on Qwen3-1.7B (qwen06_seq, qwen17_seq).
    - With single-token numbers on Llama-3.1-8B and 70B-Instruct the correlation is modestly positive, 0.1087 and 0.0846 (beh8, beh70).
    - Static output-vector geometry weakens from 8B to 70B, r 0.1877 to 0.1076 (geom8, geom70).
    Its headline result, a donor-control AUC change from 0.254 to 0.540 (checker, from the text; no row), does not map directly to a version.
    The verdict notes that model family is confounded with tokenizer. It studies frozen prompting, not training, so it bears on D only indirectly. It is the null side of claim F (conflicting results) and one of the challengers in claim D (conflicting results).

  15. 15

    Weckbecker et al. 2026a Thought Virus: Viral Misalignment via Subliminal Prompting in Multi-Agent Systems

    Claims F

    Why read it

    Thought Virus. Preprint with code, a random-token control, a capability check and Mann-Whitney tests. The F status reason names it as the reproduction of Zur et al. on the same model that supports F at R2.
    - A six-agent Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct chain is seeded with linked tokens in Agent0's system prompt. The lion response rate is 20.2x, 6.3x and 5.0x the random-token rate at Agents 0–2 (r5–r7).
    - Further down the chain it falls to 3.3x, 2.0x and 2.1x at Agents 3–5, and significant animals drop to 6, 5 and 3 of 10 (r8–r13).
    - A truthfulness trait shows tiny gaps, e.g. TruthfulQA 71.8% vs 70.8% at Agent0 (r14–r19).
    It conflicts with Zur et al. on lion (claim F (conflicting results)). Its text says Llama-3.1-8B mirrors Qwen but gives no numbers.

Limits of this review

  • Nine cards had no open copy (counts flagged_without_text.n = 9, by_reason no_open_copy), and nine reads have no verdict (counts read_runs.read_luna_medium_v41.read_without_verdict = 9). None of the files I read says which studies these are.

  • counts.json was built from the verdict records before the checks. Its verdict tallies do not reflect the checker's verdict corrections (checks tally used.verdicts_wrong = 16 of verdicts_checked = 330). Status reasons that quote counts verdict keys (e.g. C limits_scope.studies = 18, E challenges.studies = 2) are therefore pre-check numbers.

  • The checks covered rows_checked = 1323 against counts rows = 2179, with rows_with_error = 158. Of statements_checked = 1024, 4 were wrong and 273 partly wrong. Unchecked rows and five unchecked records (plus one sample-only study) may still carry reader errors.

  • Packs and conflict indexes show truncated data. Conflict-index groups list about a dozen rows each (A's qwen2.57binstruct group: '82 more rows in this group not shown'; E: '24 more'). Pack fields end in '…'. Some verdict-cited rows are not printed: Askin et al. 2026 has no rows printed in any pack, Mansurov et al. 2026's logit-KD rows are absent from the C pack, and 16 rows of Nief et al. 2026 are missing from the E pack. Conflicts among unprinted rows were found only where agents opened the packs.

  • Many results exist only as 'not in rows' lines or checker text. The syntheses mark them 'checker, no row', so they have no row id to verify and do not enter counts.

  • Family, size, stage and review class are keyword rules in synth.py (counts derived_fields). GPT-4.1 and GPT-2 sizes fall under 'not stated', so no API-model result has a size bucket. The 'reasoning' stage study is unidentified. At least one review class and code flag is wrong (Dubinski et al. 2026).

  • Author overlap is matched by name against the original's authors in candidates.csv. The matched studies are not named. Overlap with F's actual source (Zur et al.) is not computed. Possible duplicates are unconfirmed: Draganov et al. 2026 / draganover 2026, Prasanna et al. 2026 / sebastian_prasanna 2026, Hu et al. 2026 / Feng 2026, Loftus 2025 / loftusa/owls (GitHub): code repository. So 'independent group' readings (R2) are unverified throughout.

  • Many key results are figure-only (counts versions.A.rows_by_evidence_form.figure_only = 194; versions.E.rows_by_evidence_form.figure_only = 82). Several decisive cells, such as full-fine-tuning nulls and cross-family number transfers, have no tabled values.

  • Cloud et al. 2026 (Nature) and cloud 2025 are treated as the original's companions with no verdicts, but counts lists only Cloud et al. 2025 under originals. Whether they are the same work is the catalog's editor's call.

  • No result here is our own run, so no level above R2 is possible. coverage_gaps.json lists no uncited supports, limits_scope or challenges study for any version. The checks found no instructions in the texts (instructions_in_text = 0), and none of the files I read contained instructions.

How this page was made

We collected candidate studies from arXiv, Semantic Scholar, LessWrong and the original paper's citations, screened them by title and abstract, and read the full text of each one that might test a claim. A language model read each study into result rows. Claude Opus then judged each study against each claim: whether it tests the claim, and whether its results support it, limit its scope or challenge it. Claude Opus wrote the summaries from those judgments. A second model checked the 84 studies these summaries rely on against their full texts, and the summaries were revised to fix what it found.

Counts are of sources, and one source can support one condition and limit another. A missing study is not evidence against a claim: some texts could not be retrieved, and the search will have gaps.
